External lead IDs will be seat-qualified (66/68); payload must exclude private inventory/credentials (67). Browser and upstream-submission code are outside this delta (69/70). Fresh-folder fixtures use shipped defaults and current selected paths (71). The removed migration code cannot be treated as an active guard; current validator checks failures explicitly (72). Every fresh long check used watched command activity and all completion channels were consumed (73).

### Harness-contract drift lead

Literal search `rg -n seed-folders tools/pixelelated-cloud-folder-test` finds no-category calls at lines67,80,88,119,130,175,191,250,263,280. Source now requires exactly two arguments including explicit categories (`cloud_setup:785–786`). The tool header still calls itself a fast regression control; canonical instruction-files.md:196 lists it as the explicit-folder qualification tool. Proximate history is its introduction in bc4ae05d30; no deprecation in that tool. A finite current-source one-case run is prepared to distinguish stale harness from product failure.

### UI-to-backend context lead scope

Literal ES search finds two production seed callers: GuiMenu.cpp:6989 and CloudOffer.cpp:37. GuiMenu checks context before opening and accepting confirmation, then the worker starts asynchronously (`CloudTransferJob.cpp:54–68`); backend reads its own current roots at cloud_setup:789 and accepts no expected context. CloudOffer already used the same current-config shape before this delta; it is an adjacent pre-existing path. This is an unproven narrow external-change race, not a reproduced target defect. Backend snapshots its roots once and subsequent seeding does not re-read them, refuting mid-seed path drift.

Confirmed F-03 (Medium, Test Gap): current documented `pixelelated-cloud-folder-test` fails its fresh empty seeding case because it calls the deliberately retired no-category contract. Fresh one-case rc1, inner command rc2, all four watcher channels1; exact raw output under checks/retrospective-controls01. This is a developer regression-oracle defect, not a product seeding failure. Current validator controls separately passed explicit selected creation. Rewrite or explicitly retire superseded expectations and point the canonical tool entry at the replacement. Remaining no-arg sites must be classified together.

## Architecture, invariants and interactions

The delta replaces automatic account-wide migration with explicit folder selection and bounded per-category reads. It preserves existing stored paths and standalone writers. DuckStation capture uses the actual application export plus a target-built dependency; executable mode is a package property. No speculative relocation engine remains installed. The main complexity hotspots are the shell setup dispatcher, duplicated configuration grammar, ES menu composition and historical QA tools. No separate build-vs-adopt register exists in the frozen repository (`rg --files | rg -i 'build.vs.adopt|adoption.register'` is the search to verify before synthesis); platform-first is advisory, with existing readers reused.

| Invariant | Disposition and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Preserve progress; do not choose recency as truth | Current content excludes progress, saves retain explicit supported standalone paths. Fresh39save-layout/21content-scope controls and target cases; no relocation introduced. |
| No secrets in backups | Settings archive exclusion behavior is baseline-preserved; changed integrity summaries exclude private inventories and no private raw packet is opened. No new full secrets audit claimed. |
| Filter is an allowlist; no delete-excluded restore | Actual filter merge retains active custom rules before final catchall; content restore resets category exclusions; fresh scope controls and exact diff examined. |
| Upgrade and clean install | Source-level/default/custom and selected-path target overlays qualify affected behavior; current assembled-image/public adoption is pre-existing #508, not satisfied by these overlays. |

| Interaction | Shared state / wipe risk | Coverage | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ES validator × backend selected roots | Config identity, category list, bounded JSON; no writes | TESTED: changed-config/malformed/timeout/busy/UI target receipts plus host controls | Ready/present never implies integrity; stale results rejected. |
| ES creation confirmation × backend startup | Displayed root/config versus worker-time config; creates notes/folders | PARTIAL: pre-confirmation changes tested; tiny last-check→worker-read window not target-probed | L-01 unverified lead; snapshot after backend read prevents later root drift. |
| Content transfer × save writers | PSP SAVEDATA, N64 root states, DuckStation memcards; accidental cross-tier upload | TESTED: actual source writers,39+21host cases, target source-case receipts | No confirmed cross-tier loss; generic remapping intentionally unsupported. |
| Native screenshot × package/dependency/launcher | AppImage mode, libcomerr, custom destination, overlay reconfiguration | TESTED: original126/127failures, actual target mode/dependency install, two runtime capture paths and roundtrip | Qualified source; no assembled-firmware claim. |
| Config bootstrap × existing custom filter | Existing user rules, active catchall, default image changes | TESTED: old/fixed controls and target existing/default configurations | Existing active customization preserved; stored private paths not disclosed. |
| Build watchers × build root/cleanup | Logs, PID identity, retained source and installation paths | TESTED: lifecycle/install controls and sealed failed/successful runs | Original failures remain; cleanup is fixed-plan with explicit private membership limits. |
| Tracker × integration × next-session planning | Open bodies can restart retired work | CONFIRMED drift | F-01/#510/#497; root corrected M7 but lower bodies still require full reconciliation. |
| Evidence custody × public acceptance criteria | Private operational raw data | CONFIRMED drift | F-02/#504 criterion must name public summary/private custody boundary. |

Reference Implementation/tenant-zero and schema-before-code are not separate repository platform gates. JSON validator schema/parser/unit tests serve the actual typed boundary. Dogfooding is represented by retained installed guest receipts; API-first means explicit CLI categories, not a new web service. No schema migration is warranted for the instructions-only disposition.

## Executive Summary

The audited delta is coherent and substantially qualified at the source/affected-runtime level. Explicit manual cloud folder selection replaces automatic migration; bounded category checks distinguish readiness from integrity. Actual standalone save writers, custom filter preservation and native DuckStation screenshot/package prerequisites have source-bound target evidence. Build, retention and audit-cadence repairs retain original failures as well as successful controls. Candidate16 qualification is preserved as historical evidence, without replaying its full matrix or promoting a source overlay into assembled firmware.

Two provisional audit findings remain: current tracker bodies still describe completed work as active, and two documented folder regression tools still depend on the retired implicit-seeding contract. The proposed #504custody-wording finding was withdrawn after the complete body refuted its premise. A fresh synthetic case reproduces the test-tool failure. There is no newly confirmed High/Critical runtime defect. A narrow UI-confirmation-to-worker configuration race remains an unverified source lead. Independent cross-lab review, final punch list/resolution and completion publication remain required before this audit can close.

Strengths: explicit category arguments, bounded JSON parser/validator identity, selected-root discovery, progress/content separation, atomic default-filter merging and preserved custom writer paths. Target package mode and dependency closure are checked at actual installed consumers. The fresh finite checks cover42install/lifecycle cases,145cloud/integrity controls,15cadence/19retention/8cleanup controls,183ESunit cases/4752assertions, six syntax units and required package/instruction/catalog/map checks. These host controls corroborate separately bound target receipts; they are not new device-runtime qualification.

Concerns and complexity hotspots: cloud_setup's large shell dispatcher and repeated configuration/path grammar; GuiMenu's callbacks spanning a worker; many historical QA helpers retained beside their replacements. A tool can advertise current regression coverage while its first success expectation is obsolete. The source comment about scan locking also lags actual parent-held flock behavior (L-02), although the code and tested behavior are correct.

diff --git a/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/compat/fex-emu/patches/0006-guest-thunks-exclude-rebased-system-headers.patch b/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/compat/fex-emu/patches/0006-guest-thunks-exclude-rebased-system-headers.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..9b3b244016
--- /dev/null
+++ b/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/compat/fex-emu/patches/0006-guest-thunks-exclude-rebased-system-headers.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+guest-thunks: exclude the pkg-config sysroot's standard include directory
+
+The device build exports PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR for aarch64. pkg-config
+therefore reports its sysroot/usr/include instead of plain /usr/include,
+which the existing exclusion misses. Passing that directory to the x86
+guest compiler shadows its own libc headers: aarch64 bits/floatn.h aliases
+__builtin_nansf128 to long double, breaking the i686 C++ limits header.
+
+Apply the existing standard-header exclusion to its rebased form as well.
+Keep dependency-specific include directories and the host-thunk build intact.
+
+--- a/ThunkLibs/GuestLibs/CMakeLists.txt
++++ b/ThunkLibs/GuestLibs/CMakeLists.txt
+@@ -11,7 +11,8 @@
+ function(target_include_directories_from_pkgconfig target pkg)
+   pkg_check_modules(PKG QUIET ${pkg})
+   if (PKG_FOUND)
+-    list(REMOVE_ITEM PKG_INCLUDE_DIRS /usr/include)
++    list(REMOVE_ITEM PKG_INCLUDE_DIRS /usr/include
++      "$ENV{PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR}/usr/include")
+     target_include_directories(${target} INTERFACE ${PKG_INCLUDE_DIRS})
+   elseif (ARGN)
+     target_include_directories(${target} INTERFACE ${ARGN})

diff --git a/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/emulators/standalone/duckstation-sa/scripts/duckstation_screenshot_path b/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/emulators/standalone/duckstation-sa/scripts/duckstation_screenshot_path
new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..e8965505c5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/emulators/standalone/duckstation-sa/scripts/duckstation_screenshot_path
@@ -0,0 +1,137 @@
+#!/usr/bin/python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+# Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
+"""Keep the shipped screenshot default in the saves tree; never move captures."""
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import stat
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+TARGET = Path('/storage/roms/screenshots')
+MAX_CONFIG_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
+
+
+def read_config(path):
+    info = path.lstat()
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
+        raise ValueError('nonregular configuration')
+    with path.open('rb') as stream:
+        raw = stream.read(MAX_CONFIG_BYTES + 1)
+    if len(raw) > MAX_CONFIG_BYTES or b'\0' in raw:
+        raise ValueError('unreadable configuration')
+    return info, raw
+
+
+def updated_config(raw):
+    text = raw.decode('utf-8')
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    section = ''
+    folders = []
+    keys = []
+    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
+        content = line.strip().lstrip('\ufeff')
+        if not content or content.startswith(('#', ';')):
+            continue
+        if content.startswith('['):
+            match = re.fullmatch(r'\[([^\]\r\n]+)\]', content)
+            if not match:
+                raise ValueError('ambiguous section')
+            section = match[1].strip().casefold()
+            if section == 'folders':
+                folders.append(index)
+        elif section == 'folders' and '=' in content:
+            name, value = content.split('=', 1)
+            if name.strip().casefold() == 'screenshots':
+                keys.append((index, value.strip()))
+    if len(folders) > 1 or len(keys) > 1:
+        raise ValueError('ambiguous screenshot configuration')
+    value = keys[0][1] if keys else ''
+    if value == str(TARGET):
+        return raw
+    # Only absent, empty, or the exact shipped default is ours to change.
+    # Quoted, alternate, absolute and other custom values remain untouched.
+    if value not in ('', 'screenshots'):
+        return None
+    newline = '\r\n' if '\r\n' in text else '\n'
+    setting = 'Screenshots = ' + str(TARGET) + newline
+    if keys:
+        lines[keys[0][0]] = setting
+    elif folders:
+        index = folders[0]
+        if not lines[index].endswith(('\n', '\r')):
+            lines[index] += newline
+        lines.insert(index + 1, setting)
+    else:
+        if lines and not lines[-1].endswith(('\n', '\r')):
+            lines[-1] += newline
+        lines.extend([newline, '[Folders]' + newline, setting])
+    return ''.join(lines).encode('utf-8')
+
+
+def prepare(path):
+    original, raw = read_config(path)
+    replacement = updated_config(raw)
+    if replacement is None:
+        return
+    # An owner may have redirected the old default with a directory symlink.
+    # Keep that choice as well as explicit custom configuration values.
+    if replacement != raw and (path.parent / 'screenshots').is_symlink():
+        return
+    created = False
+    staged = None
+    try:
+        if TARGET.is_symlink():
+            raise ValueError('screenshot target is a symlink')
+        if not TARGET.exists():
+            TARGET.mkdir()
+            created = True
+        if not TARGET.is_dir():
+            raise ValueError('screenshot target is not a directory')
+        # Verify actual writes before changing the setting, including read-only
+        # mounts and full storage. The temporary byte is always removed.
+        with tempfile.TemporaryFile(dir=TARGET) as probe:
+            probe.write(b'\0')
+            probe.flush()
+            os.fsync(probe.fileno())
+        if replacement == raw:
+            return
+        descriptor, staged = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.screenshots-', dir=path.parent)
+        with os.fdopen(descriptor, 'wb') as output:
+            os.fchmod(output.fileno(), stat.S_IMODE(original.st_mode))
+            os.fchown(output.fileno(), original.st_uid, original.st_gid)
+            output.write(replacement)
+            output.flush()
+            os.fsync(output.fileno())
+        current, observed = read_config(path)
+        identity = lambda info: (info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_size, info.st_mtime_ns, info.st_ctime_ns)
+        if identity(current) != identity(original) or observed != raw:
+            raise ValueError('configuration changed during preparation')
+        os.replace(staged, path)
+        staged = None
+    except Exception:
+        if created:
+            try:
+                TARGET.rmdir()
+            except OSError:
+                pass
+        raise
+    finally:
+        if staged is not None:
+            os.unlink(staged)
+
+
+def main():
+    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
+        return 2
+    try:
+        prepare(Path(sys.argv[1]))
+    except (OSError, UnicodeError, ValueError):
+        print("Couldn't prepare the screenshot folder. Screenshot preparation moved no existing captures.", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    sys.exit(main())

@@ -0,0 +1,278 @@
+#!/usr/bin/python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
+# Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
+"""Bounded folder readiness metadata, never a transfer or integrity check.
+
+Private stdout contract for cloud_setup/ES. Missing means the selected endpoint
+returned not-found, or the selected content root listed without the child.
+Empty means a successful bounded listing found no recognized content; it is not
+an account-wide absence claim. No ancestor outside the selected root is read.
+"""
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import selectors
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+
+CATEGORIES = ('saves', 'settings', 'roms', 'bios', 'media')
+MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_ENTRIES = 4096
+TOTAL_SECONDS = 25
+# Only observed standard save subtrees get deeper reads; never widen the
+# whole selected root or infer progress from an uninspected directory.
+SAVE_SUBTREES = {'psp/PSP/SAVEDATA': 2, 'psx/duckstation/memcards': 1}
+MEDIA = {'images', 'videos', 'manuals', 'screenshots', 'fanart', 'boxart', 'wheel', 'mix', 'maps', 'media'}
+# Match the shipped progress allowlist and content transfer exclusions. These
+# are case-sensitive like rclone's filters; test controls compare actual bytes.
+PROGRESS = re.compile(r'\.(srm|sav|fs|state[^/]*|auto|dsv[^/]*|eep|mpk|sra|fla)$')
+N64_STATE = re.compile(r'\.(st[0-9]|pj[0-9](\.zip)?)$')
+CONTENT_SAVE = re.compile(r'\.(srm|sav|fs|state[^/]*|auto|dsv[^/]*|eep|mpk|sra|fla|mcd|mcr)$')
+DATABASE = re.compile(r'\.(db|db-wal|db-shm|db-journal|sqlite|sqlite3)$')
+PARTIAL = re.compile(r'\.[^/]{8}\.partial$')
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+
+
+class Unreadable(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def command(args, deadline, seconds=6, limit=MAX_BYTES):
+    """Drain only bounded stdout; diagnostics can contain provider credentials."""
+    remaining = min(seconds, deadline - time.monotonic())
+    if remaining <= 0:
+        raise Unreadable('time-limit')
+    end = time.monotonic() + remaining
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                            start_new_session=True)
+    output = bytearray()
+    try:
+        with selectors.DefaultSelector() as ready:
+            ready.register(proc.stdout, selectors.EVENT_READ)
+            while ready.get_map():
+                wait = end - time.monotonic()
+                if wait <= 0:
+                    raise Unreadable('time-limit')
+                if not ready.select(wait):
+                    raise Unreadable('time-limit')
+                chunk = os.read(proc.stdout.fileno(), 65536)
+                if not chunk:
+                    ready.unregister(proc.stdout)
+                    break
+                output.extend(chunk)
+                if len(output) > limit:
+                    raise Unreadable('listing-limit')
+        rc = proc.wait(timeout=max(0.01, end - time.monotonic()))
+        return rc, bytes(output)
+    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, Unreadable):
+        raise Unreadable('time-or-listing-limit')
+    finally:
+        if proc.poll() is None:
+            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        proc.wait()
+        proc.stdout.close()
+
+
+def context(deadline):
+    rc, raw = command([str(HERE / 'cloud_setup'), '--validation-context'], deadline)
+    if rc:
+        raise Unreadable('unreadable-config')
+    value = json.loads(raw)
+    if not re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{64}', value.get('config_id', '')):
+        raise Unreadable('unreadable-config')
+    return value
+
+
+def listing(remote, path, depth, deadline):
+    rc, raw = command(['rclone', 'lsjson', remote + path, '--recursive',
+                       '--max-depth', str(depth), '--no-mimetype', '--no-modtime',
+                       '--retries', '1', '--low-level-retries', '1',
+                       '--contimeout', '3s', '--timeout', '5s', '--max-duration', '6s'], deadline)
+    if rc:
+        # Entries on ANY error are not a valid observation. rclone lsjson
+        # emits its opening bracket before a directory-not-found response.
+        if rc in (3, 4) and (raw.strip() in (b'', b'[') or json.loads(raw) == []):
+            return None
+        raise Unreadable('listing-failed')
+    entries = json.loads(raw)
+    if not isinstance(entries, list) or len(entries) > MAX_ENTRIES:
+        raise Unreadable('listing-limit')
+    seen = set()
+    for entry in entries:
+        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not isinstance(entry.get('Path'), str) or type(entry.get('IsDir')) is not bool:
+            raise Unreadable('invalid-listing')
+        p = entry['Path']
+        if not p or len(p.split('/')) > depth or p.startswith('/') or any(x in ('', '.', '..') for x in p.split('/')) or any(ord(c) < 32 for c in p):
+            raise Unreadable('invalid-listing')
+        if p in seen:
+            raise Unreadable('invalid-listing')
+        seen.add(p)
+    return entries
+
+
+def save_entries(remote, path, entries, deadline):
+    """Inspect named save writers beyond the root's ordinary depth-three cut."""
+    combined = list(entries)
+    unchecked = {e['Path'] for e in entries if e['IsDir'] and len(e['Path'].split('/')) == 3}
+    for subtree, depth in SAVE_SUBTREES.items():
+        if subtree not in unchecked:
+            continue
+        child = path + ('' if not path or path.endswith('/') else '/') + subtree
+        extra = listing(remote, child, depth, deadline)
+        if extra is None:
+            raise Unreadable('folder-changed-during-check')
+        unchecked.remove(subtree)
+        for entry in extra:
+            full = subtree + '/' + entry['Path']
+            combined.append(dict(entry, Path=full))
+            if entry['IsDir'] and len(entry['Path'].split('/')) == depth:
+                unchecked.add(full)
+        if len(combined) > MAX_ENTRIES:
+            raise Unreadable('listing-limit')
+    return combined, unchecked
+
+
+def files(entries):
+    return [e['Path'] for e in entries if not e['IsDir'] and e['Path'] not in ('README.txt', '.layout')]
+
+
+def progress(path):
+    """The ordinary progress allowlist, excluding its separate archive tier."""
+    parts = path.split('/')
+    if DATABASE.search(parts[-1]):
+        return False
+    return (parts[0] in ('savefiles', 'savestates', 'screenshots') or bool(PROGRESS.search(parts[-1]))
+            or (parts[0] == 'n64' and len(parts) == 2 and bool(N64_STATE.search(parts[-1])))
+            or (path.startswith('psx/memcards/') and len(parts) == 3 and parts[-1].endswith(('.mcd', '.mcr')))
+            or (path.startswith('psx/duckstation/memcards/') and len(parts) == 4 and parts[-1].endswith(('.mcd', '.mcr')))
+            or path.startswith(('dc/shared/savefiles/', 'psp/PPSSPP/', 'psp/PSP/SAVEDATA/')))
+
+
+def content_excluded(path, system=None):
+    """SAVE_EXCLUDES/CONFLICT_EXCLUDES, relative to one ROM system or BIOS."""
+    parts = path.split('/')
+    return ((system == 'n64' and len(parts) == 1 and bool(N64_STATE.search(parts[-1])))
+            or bool(CONTENT_SAVE.search(parts[-1])) or 'conflicted copy' in path
+            or '.sync-conflict-' in path or bool(PARTIAL.search(parts[-1]))
+            or any(p in ('save', 'memcards', 'PPSSPP') for p in parts[:-1])
+            or any(parts[i:i+2] in (['shared', 'savefiles'], ['PSP', 'SAVEDATA']) for i in range(len(parts)-2))
+            or path == 'README.txt')
+
+
+def unchecked_directory(category, path, known):
+    if category in ('roms', 'media'):
+        parts = path.split('/')
+        return parts[0] in known and not content_excluded('/'.join(parts[1:]) + '/probe', parts[0])
+    if category == 'bios':
+        return not content_excluded(path + '/probe')
+    return True
+
+
+def classify(category, entries, known):
+    payload = files(entries)
+    if not payload:
+        return 'empty', 'no-recognized-content-in-checked-depth'
+    if category == 'settings':
+        good = [p for p in payload if p.lower().endswith(('.zip', '.tar.gz')) and len(p.split('/')) <= 2]
+        return ('present', 'archive-names-found-not-verified') if good else ('empty', 'no-recognized-settings-archives-in-checked-depth')
+    if category == 'bios':
+        return ('present', 'files-found-not-compatibility-checked') if any(not content_excluded(p) for p in payload) else ('empty', 'no-recognized-content-in-checked-depth')
+    if category == 'saves':
+        # The progress allowlist permits recognized saves at any depth. A
+        # repeated folder name alone is not evidence of a wrong location.
+        return ('present', 'progress-paths-found-not-verified') if any(progress(p) for p in payload) else ('empty', 'no-recognized-progress-in-checked-depth')
+    # ROM transfer expects one supported system folder beneath ROMs. A
+    # direct payload is a location finding even when other ROMs are valid;
+    # do not guess its system, move it, or describe that folder as empty.
+    if category == 'roms' and any('/' not in p and p != 'gamelist.xml' and not content_excluded(p) for p in payload):
+        return 'misplaced', 'files-outside-system-folders'
+    good = []
+    for path in payload:
+        parts = path.split('/')
+        if len(parts) < 2 or parts[0] not in known or content_excluded('/'.join(parts[1:]), parts[0]):
+            continue
+        media = parts[1] in MEDIA or parts[-1] == 'gamelist.xml'
+        if (category == 'media') == media:
+            good.append(path)
+    if good:
+        return 'present', 'supported-system-paths-found-not-verified'
+    return 'empty', 'no-recognized-content-in-checked-depth'
+
+
+def main():
+    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
+        return 2
+    selected = sys.argv[1].split(',')
+    run_id = sys.argv[2]
+    if not selected or len(selected) != len(set(selected)) or any(c not in CATEGORIES for c in selected) or not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}', run_id):
+        return 2
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + TOTAL_SECONDS
+    result = {'schema_version': 1, 'run_id': run_id, 'config_id': '', 'categories': [], 'complete': False,
+              'scope': {'max_depth': 3, 'save_subtree_depths': SAVE_SUBTREES, 'max_entries_per_listing': MAX_ENTRIES, 'max_bytes_per_listing': MAX_BYTES, 'max_seconds': TOTAL_SECONDS}}
+    try:
+        current = context(deadline)
+        result.update(config_id=current['config_id'], paths=current['paths'])
+        known = set()
+        if 'roms' in selected or 'media' in selected:
+            rc, raw = command([str(HERE / 'cloud_content_restore'), '--known-directories'], deadline)
+            if rc:
+                raise Unreadable('system-list-unavailable')
+            known = set(raw.decode().splitlines())
+        cache = {}
+        for category in selected:
+            path = current['paths'][category]
+            row = {'category': category, 'state': 'unreadable', 'path': path, 'detail': 'check-not-completed'}
+            try:
+                # The content root is selected, so its direct children are in
+                # scope. No account/ancestor fallback if that root is absent.
+                if category in ('roms', 'bios', 'media'):
+                    root = current['paths']['content']
+                    if (root, 1) not in cache:
+                        cache[root, 1] = listing(current['remote'], root, 1, deadline)
+                    parent = cache[root, 1]
+                    child = 'BIOS' if category == 'bios' else 'ROMs'
+                    if parent is None or not any(e['IsDir'] and e['Path'] == child for e in parent):
+                        misplaced = parent and any(e['IsDir'] and (e['Path'].lower() == child.lower() or (category == 'roms' and e['Path'] in known)) for e in parent)
+                        row.update(state='misplaced' if misplaced else 'missing', detail='recognized-folders-outside-expected-path' if misplaced else 'expected-folder-not-found')
+                        result['categories'].append(row)
+                        continue
+                if (path, 3) not in cache:
+                    cache[path, 3] = listing(current['remote'], path, 3, deadline)
+                entries = cache[path, 3]
+                if entries is None:
+                    row.update(state='missing', detail='selected-folder-not-found')
+                else:
+                    if not entries and category in ('saves', 'settings'):
+                        # Bucket prefixes do not exist as empty directories.
+                        # Without entries or an in-scope parent witness an
+                        # empty answer cannot prove this selected root exists.
+                        rc, raw = command(['rclone', 'backend', 'features', current['remote'] + path], deadline)
+                        if rc or json.loads(raw).get('Features', {}).get('BucketBased') is not False:
+                            raise Unreadable('folder-presence-unconfirmed')
+                    unchecked = {e['Path'] for e in entries if e['IsDir'] and len(e['Path'].split('/')) == 3}
+                    if category == 'saves':
+                        entries, unchecked = save_entries(current['remote'], path, entries, deadline)
+                    state, detail = classify(category, entries, known)
+                    if state == 'empty' and any(unchecked_directory(category, p, known) for p in unchecked):
+                        raise Unreadable('deeper-folders-not-checked')
+                    row.update(state=state, detail=detail)
+            except (Unreadable, ValueError, OSError) as error:
+                row['detail'] = str(error) if isinstance(error, Unreadable) else 'invalid-or-unreadable-listing'
+            result['categories'].append(row)
+        # A result belongs to the config actually inspected, even if another
+        # screen edits the selected remote or paths while listing is running.
+        after = context(deadline)
+        if after['config_id'] != current['config_id']:
+            raise Unreadable('configuration-changed')
+        result['complete'] = all(row['state'] != 'unreadable' for row in result['categories'])
+    except (Unreadable, ValueError, OSError) as error:
+        result['error'] = str(error) if isinstance(error, Unreadable) else 'unreadable-config'
+    print(json.dumps(result, separators=(',', ':')))
+    return 0 if result['complete'] else 5
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/network/rclone/sources/cloud_migrate_layout b/projects/ROCKNIX/packages/network/rclone/sources/cloud_migrate_layout

@@ -1,1693 +0,0 @@
-#!/bin/bash
-# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
-# Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
-
-# cloud_migrate_layout - move a device off the original cloud folder layout.
-#
-# The first layout put everything under /GAMES, with the settings backups nested
-# inside the saves folder at /GAMES/backup. Both are wrong in ways that bite:
-#
-#   - /GAMES is a name somebody may well have used for something else, and we
-#     write into it as though it were ours.
-#   - a backup folder inside the saves folder is inside the path that a `sync`
-#     backup mirrors, so the archive is deletable by the operation meant to
-#     protect it.
-#
-# The default has been /ROCKNIX/Saves and /ROCKNIX/Backups since b35c5832b1,
-# but cloud_sync_helper only ever adds keys that are missing -- it never
-# rewrites one already in the file -- so every device configured before that
-# is still on the old layout and will stay there for ever unless asked.
-#
-# This is an offer, never automatic. Where somebody's saves live is theirs to
-# decide, and the safe answer is always to leave it alone.
-#
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --check     what would move, and whether it is safe
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --apply     do it
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --state     one line per fact, for the interface to decide
-#                                    what to offer (STATE=current|kept|superseded-with-files|
-#                                    superseded-empty|own|no-remote; fork #353)
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --keep      record that this device keeps its superseded
-#                                    folder (LAYOUT_KEEP in the conf; asked once, D-CLOUD-160)
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --superseded  the superseded defaults, one per line (no network)
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --needs-step  0 when the cloud folder step has something to settle:
-#                                    an earlier default, not kept, a remote set up (no
-#                                    network; asked at every boot, D-CLOUD-170)
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --follow    re-point a device on a superseded default at the
-#                                    current layout when another device has already
-#                                    made it (no question; D-CLOUD-160's "the other
-#                                    devices follow"); 0 when it did, 3 when there was
-#                                    nothing to follow
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --join      point a device whose own folder holds no saves --
-#                                    the current default, or a default this project once
-#                                    shipped -- at the earlier folder that does hold them
-#                                    (no question; a fresh install, or a carried /GAMES,
-#                                    beside a fleet still on the earlier folder); 0 when
-#                                    it did, 3 when there was nothing to join
-#   cloud_migrate_layout --settle    the seeding's step (cloud_setup --seed-folders):
-#                                    --join, else a carried default with nothing in it
-#                                    anywhere is pointed at the current folders, which
-#                                    the seeding then makes, as for any new cloud
-#
-# Only the two folders we wrote are moved. Anything else under the old folder
-# is left exactly where it is, because it is not ours.
-
-. /etc/profile 2>/dev/null
-
-SYNC_CONF="/storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf"
-NEW_SAVES="/pixelelated/Saves"
-NEW_BACKUPS="/pixelelated/Backups"
-NEW_CONTENT="/pixelelated/Content"
-NEW_ROOT="${NEW_SAVES%/*}"   # the folder the tiers move into; named by the plan line below
-# Every saves folder this project ever shipped as its default. A device whose
-# saves folder is one of these is on a layout it never chose, so the move is
-# offered (D-CLOUD-160); any other folder is the player's own and stays
-# (the sibling-layout branch below). Oldest first; the current default is
-# NEW_SAVES and is not listed.
-SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES=("/GAMES" "/ROCKNIX/Saves")
-# The marker a cloud carries once it is on the current layout (#356): one
-# line, layout=<n>, at the parent of the saves folder. Read before anything
-# is offered; written after a move or a seeding.
-LAYOUT_VERSION=2
-LAYOUT_MARKER=".layout"
-REMOTE_LAYOUT=0
-MIGRATION_RECORD="/storage/.config/cloud-layout-migration.json"
-MIGRATION_ACTIVE=0
-MIGRATION_RESUMING=0
-
-# Which superseded default's saves folder holds files in this cloud, the
-# configured one first, then the others newest first: into SOURCE_FOUND,
-# empty when none does. Called directly, never inside $(...): its listings
-# stop the run when the cloud cannot be read (list_or_stop), and inside a
-# substitution that stop ended only the subshell -- a listing that failed
-# read as "no folder holds the saves", a provider error taken for absence,
-# and --state then said superseded-empty and the interface offered CREATE
-# IT (found 2026-10-01 reading for the mixed-installation test).
-SOURCE_FOUND=""
-superseded_source() { # <remote> <configured saves folder>
-    local remote="$1" saves="$2"
-    SOURCE_FOUND=""
-    if has_files "${remote}${saves}/"; then SOURCE_FOUND="${saves}"; return 0; fi
-    earlier_source "${remote}" "${saves}"
-}
-
-# The newest superseded default, other than <except>, whose saves folder
-# holds files: into SOURCE_FOUND. Newest first, because where both an
-# upstream /GAMES and the fork's /ROCKNIX/Saves hold saves, the fork's is
-# the one its other devices write.
-earlier_source() { # <remote> [except]
-    local remote="$1" except="${2:-}" i s
-    SOURCE_FOUND=""
-    for (( i = ${#SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[@]} - 1; i >= 0; i-- )); do
-        s="${SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[i]}"
-        [ -n "${except}" ] && same_folder "${s}" "${except}" && continue
-        if has_files "${remote}${s}/"; then SOURCE_FOUND="${s}"; return 0; fi
-    done
-    return 1
-}
-
-# The pointers of the layout an earlier saves folder belongs to, into
-# E_SAVES E_BACKUPS E_CONTENT: its siblings, or the nested /GAMES/backup of
-# the first layout. Content goes with it only where this device's own was
-# unset or the current default; a folder the player chose for ROMs stays
-# theirs.
-# An explicit empty CONTENT_REMOTE is the cloud root, not an unset option.
-content_unset() { ! grep -q '^CONTENT_REMOTE=' "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null; }
-
-# A pointer-only transition may follow an empty default backup tier, never
-# abandon its archives or replace a custom folder. Called directly: failed
-# listings terminate the caller through list_or_stop, not a subshell.
-backup_pointer_for() { # <remote> <configured backups> <destination default>
-    local remote="$1" backups="$2" target="$3" known=0
-    NEXT_BACKUPS="${backups}"
-    case "${backups%/}" in
-        ""|/GAMES/backup|/ROCKNIX/Backups|/pixelelated/Backups) known=1 ;;
-    esac
-    [ "${known}" -eq 1 ] || return 0
-    if [ -n "${backups}" ]; then
-        list_or_stop "${remote}${backups%/}/" --files-only -R --include '*.{zip,tar.gz}'
-        [ -n "${LISTING}" ] && return 0
-    fi
-    NEXT_BACKUPS="${target}"
-}
-
-earlier_layout() { # <saves folder> <this device's content pointer>
-    local src="$1" content="$2" parent
-    parent="${src%/*}"; [ -n "${parent}" ] || parent="${src}"
-    E_SAVES="${src}"
-    if [ "${src}" = "/GAMES" ]; then E_BACKUPS="/GAMES/backup"; else E_BACKUPS="${parent}/Backups"; fi
-    if content_unset || same_folder "${content}" "${NEW_CONTENT}"; then
-        E_CONTENT="${parent}/Content"
-    else
-        E_CONTENT="${content}"
-    fi
-}
-
-superseded_default() { # <saves folder>: 0 when it is a default this project once shipped
-    local s
-    for s in "${SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[@]}"; do same_folder "$1" "${s}" && return 0; done
-    return 1
-}
-
-say() { echo "$@"; }
-
-remote_name() {
-    rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1
-}
-
-# The shared reader (cloud_setup's, the content scripts', D-CLOUD-149): a
-# single-quoted or bare pointer used to come back as the whole line from
-# `cut -d'"' -f2`, and the new folder logic then moved the pointer off the
-# player's saves (the audit of the fixes, claude G3-D-05).
-conf_get() { # <KEY> (the content scripts' reader, mirrored so every reader agrees, D-CLOUD-149): its value, quotes off; nothing when absent; exit 2 when unreadable, and why on stdout
-    [ -f ${SYNC_CONF} ] || return 0
-    awk -v k="$1" '
-        { t = $0; gsub(/\t/, "", t); if (t ~ /[[:cntrl:]]/ && !cntrl) cntrl = NR }
-        index($0, k "=") != 1 && !other \
-            && $0 ~ ("^[ \t]*((export|declare|typeset|readonly|local)([ \t]+-[A-Za-z]+)*[ \t]+)?" k "[ \t]*[+]?=") { other = NR }
-        index($0, k "=") == 1 {
-            s = substr($0, length(k) + 2); v = ""; r = ""; ok = 1; why = ""

-                # character each (PL-015), and so does this; an unescaped $
-                # or backtick is an expansion this reader does not make, and
-                # any other backslash is refused as conf_valid refuses it.

-                while (i <= n) {
-                    d = substr(s, i, 1)
-                    if (d == "\"") { closed = 1; break }
-                    if (d == "\\") {
-                        e = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
-                        if (e == "\"" || e == "\\" || e == "$" || e == "`") { v = v e; i += 2; continue }
-                        ok = 0
-                        why = (e == "") ? "a value continued onto the next line, which this reader does not follow" \
-                                        : "a backslash inside double quotes that is not one of the escapes bash reads there"
-                        break
-                    }
-                    if (d == "$" || d == "`") { ok = 0; why = "a $ or a backtick inside double quotes"; break }
-                    v = v d; i++
-                }
-                if (ok && !closed) { ok = 0; why = "a double-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
-                if (ok) r = substr(s, i + 1)
-            } else if (c == "'"'"'") {
-                j = index(substr(s, 2), c)
-                if (j) { v = substr(s, 2, j - 1); r = substr(s, j + 2) } else { ok = 0; why = "a single-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
-            } else {
-                match(s, /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-]*/); v = substr(s, 1, RLENGTH); r = substr(s, RLENGTH + 1)
-            }
-            if (ok && r !~ /^([ \t]+(#.*)?)?$/) { ok = 0; why = "something after the value that is not a # comment" }
-            if (!found) { found = 1; first = v; firstok = ok; firstwhy = "line " NR ": " why }
-        }
-        END {
-            if (cntrl) { print "line " cntrl ": a control character other than a tab"; exit 2 }
-            if (other) { print "line " other ": " k " set in a form this reader does not read"; exit 2 }
-            if (found && !firstok) { print firstwhy; exit 2 }

-    ' ${SYNC_CONF}
-}
-conf_value() {
-    local v
-    v=$(conf_get "$1"); case $? in 2) echo "cloud_migrate_layout: ${SYNC_CONF}: ${v}" >&2; return 2 ;; esac
-    printf '%s\n' "${v}"
-}
-
-# One folder, one spelling (the audit of the fix round, PL-001). The guards
-# in main that decide whether a tier has already landed compared the conf's
-# raw string with /ROCKNIX/Saves, so SAVES_REMOTE="/ROCKNIX/Saves/" -- a
-# trailing slash, from a hand edit or an older setup -- read as the old
-# layout: --check offered the move, and --apply copied the saves onto
-# themselves (rclone's copy of a folder onto itself exits 0 and changes
-# nothing), checked them clean against themselves, and deleted every file
-# it had listed; the content folder went the same way. So a pointer is read
-# as the folder it names:
-#
-#   clean_path     runs of / as one, no "." component, no trailing /; a
-#                  leading / kept only if it had one, so the path handed to
-#                  rclone is the one the other scripts use; it fails on a
-#                  ".." component, which rclone resolves by rules of its
-#                  own, so main leaves such a layout alone;
-#   folder_key     that from the root, in one case when the cloud folds case
-#                  (Dropbox, OneDrive) or cannot say whether it does;
-#   same_folder    two keys equal;
-#   inside_folder  the first strictly under the second, and rel_inside the
-#                  part below, in the first one's own spelling.
-CASE_INSENSITIVE=1
-clean_path() { # <path>
-    local p="$1" lead="" out="" part
-    local -a parts=()
-    case "${p}" in /*) lead="/" ;; esac
-    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "${p}"
-    for part in "${parts[@]}"; do
-        case "${part}" in
-            ""|.) ;;
-            ..) return 1 ;;
-            *) out="${out:+${out}/}${part}" ;;
-        esac
-    done
-    printf '%s%s' "${lead}" "${out}"
-}
-folder_abs() { # <cleaned path>: the same folder from the root, in its own spelling
-    printf '/%s' "${1#/}"
-}
-folder_key() { # <path>
-    local p
-    p=$(clean_path "$1") || p="$1"
-    p="/${p#/}"
-    [ "${CASE_INSENSITIVE}" = 1 ] && p="${p,,}"
-    printf '%s' "${p}"
-}
-same_folder() { # <path> <path>
-    [ "$(folder_key "$1")" = "$(folder_key "$2")" ]
-}
-inside_folder() { # <path> <path>: the first strictly under the second
-    local ka kb
-    ka=$(folder_key "$1"); kb=$(folder_key "$2")
-    [ "${ka}" != "${kb}" ] || return 1
-    [ "${kb}" = "/" ] && return 0
-    case "${ka}" in "${kb}"/*) return 0 ;; esac
-    return 1
-}
-rel_inside() { # <path> <path>: the part of the first below the second (inside_folder holds)
-    local a b
-    a=$(clean_path "$1") || a="$1"; b=$(clean_path "$2") || b="$2"
-    a=$(folder_abs "${a}"); b=$(folder_abs "${b}")
-    if [ "${b}" = "/" ]; then printf '%s' "${a#/}"; else printf '%s' "${a:$(( ${#b} + 1 ))}"; fi
-}
-
-# A listing's bound (#143): three low-level retries, the value every other
-# cloud script lists with.
-readonly -a RCLONE_LIST_OPTS=(--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 3 --retries 1)
-# Every other call's (#308 claude F-CS-23): RCLONE_NET_OPTS from the conf,
-# or the shipped value when the conf has none -- the bound the transfers
-# carry everywhere else, where this script ran on rclone's own defaults
-# (a 60 s connect, a 5 min idle, ten low-level retries, three runs: the
-# behaviour #101 removed from every other script). Set in main.
-RCLONE_NET_OPTS_FALLBACK="--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 10 --retries 1"
-RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY=()
-# What a verification compares by: size and hash where the remote keeps
-# hashes, the bytes themselves where it keeps none (WebDAV, SFTP, SMB,
-# FTP), where `rclone check` would otherwise compare sizes alone. Set in
-# main from `rclone backend features`; a remote whose features cannot be
-# read is checked by content too.
-CHECK_OPTS=()
-
-# One cloud transfer at a time (F-CS-23): the lock every other cloud script
-# takes, for --apply only -- the check reads and writes nothing, as the
-# match preview does. Without it a startup or game-exit sync could write
-# into the folder this was moving. The same descriptor discipline as the
-# others: the body runs with fd 9 closed, so nothing it starts holds the
-# lock. Exit 75 is the skip EmulationStation names.
-CLOUD_SYNC_LOCK=/var/run/cloud_sync.lock
-take_cloud_lock() {
-    local tries=0
-    exec 9>"${CLOUD_SYNC_LOCK}"
-    while ! flock -n 9; do
-        if [ "${tries}" -ge 4 ]; then
-            echo "Skipped: another cloud sync is already running. Try again when it's done."
-            exit 75
-        fi
-        tries=$((tries + 1))
-        sleep 0.25
-    done
-}
-
-# A cloud that did not answer is not an empty cloud (audit #307 PL-027).
-# Every presence test here used to be `[ -n "$(rclone lsf ... 2>/dev/null |
-# head -1)" ]`, which discards rclone's exit: a listing that failed read as
-# a folder with nothing in it, and --apply went on to rewrite the pointers
-# with nothing copied. A listing now ends one of three ways: it listed
-# (LISTING holds what it said, perhaps nothing), the folder is not there
-# (rclone's 3/4, or the nearest listable parent lacks it -- #142's walk,
-# for a server whose "missing" rclone does not map to 3), or the cloud
-# could not be read -- and then the run stops where it is, saying so, with
-# every pointer that has not already landed left where it was.
-unreadable() { # <path> <rclone exit>
-    local rc="$2"
-    [ "${rc}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null || rc=1
-    say "Couldn't read your cloud, so nothing more was changed. Try again when you're online."
-    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
-    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "could not list $1 (rclone exit $2); stopped" 2>/dev/null
-    exit "${rc}"
-}
-
-# Is this remote path missing, rather than unreadable? cloud_content_restore's
-# walk, verbatim: up to the nearest level that lists; a level that lists and
-# lacks the next name is a path not created yet (0), one that holds it means
-# the failure was something else (1), and a root that will not list is
-# broken (1).
-absent_not_broken() {
-    local path="${1%/}" remote rel name parent listing
-    remote="${path%%:*}:"; rel="${path#*:}"; rel="${rel#/}"
-    while [ -n "${rel}" ]; do
-        name="${rel##*/}"; parent="${rel%/*}"
-        [ "${parent}" = "${rel}" ] && parent=""
-        if listing=$(rclone lsf --dirs-only "${remote}/${parent:+${parent}/}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
-            printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | grep -qFx -- "${name}/" && return 1
-            return 0
-        fi
-        [ -n "${parent}" ] || return 1
-        rel="${parent}"
-    done
-    return 1
-}
-
-# LISTING=what rclone lsf [args] <path> lists; nothing for a folder that is
-# not there; the run stops for one that cannot be read. Never called inside
-# $(...), so the stop is the script's.
-LISTING=""
-list_or_stop() { # <path> [lsf args...]
-    local path="$1" rc
-    shift
-    LISTING=$(rclone lsf "$@" "${path}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
-    case "${rc}" in
-        0) return 0 ;;
-        3|4) LISTING=""; return 0 ;;
-    esac
-    if absent_not_broken "${path}"; then
-        LISTING=""
-        return 0
-    fi
-    unreadable "${path}" "${rc}"
-}
-
-# Does a remote path exist and hold anything?
-has_entries() {
-    list_or_stop "$1"
-    [ -n "${LISTING}" ]
-}
-
-# Does it hold actual files, ignoring the backup folder underneath it?
-#
-# Not the same question as "is it empty". The original layout has the backups
-# nested inside the saves folder, so a saves folder with nothing in it but
-# that subdirectory still lists an entry -- and reading that as "the saves are
-# here" would move the backups into the middle of the saves.
-#
-# The same exclusions are what the saves relocation carries (audit #307
-# PL-025): a test that looks past backup/ and Backups/ and a copy that then
-# moves them is how the original layout's settings archives landed in
-# Saves/backup/. Anchored at the folder's root, where the nested layout put
-# them; the caller adds the tiers nested deeper. Every argument is passed
-# as it is given -- the exclusion used to travel as one unquoted word
-# (${extra}), which the shell split and glob-expanded against the working
-# directory (#308 claude F-CS-23).
-SAVES_EXCLUDES=(--exclude '/backup/**' --exclude '/Backups/**')
-has_files() { # <path> [more lsf arguments...]
-    local path="$1"
-    shift
-    # The setup note is not a save and must not outrank another root's data.
-    list_or_stop "${path}" --files-only -R "${SAVES_EXCLUDES[@]}" --exclude '/README.txt' "$@"
-    [ -n "${LISTING}" ]
-}
-
-# Does a remote path exist?
-#
-# NOT `rclone lsjson --stat`, which is what this used to be. On bucket-based
-# remotes (S3, B2, Minio) stat synthesises a directory entry for *any* path --
-# verified against Minio on rclone 1.60 and 1.74, where
-# "utterly-bogus-never-created" reports success with IsDir true. So it can
-# never report absence there, and every caller that branched on it took the
-# "exists" path unconditionally.
-#
-# A listing can report absence. Two questions, because a directory can be real
-# without holding files: does it contain anything, or does its parent list it
-# (which is what an --s3-directory-markers marker object produces)?
-exists() {
-    list_or_stop "$1"
-    [ -n "${LISTING}" ] && return 0
-    local parent name
-    parent="${1%/}"; name="${parent##*/}"; parent="${parent%/*}"
-    [ -n "${name}" ] || return 1
-    list_or_stop "${parent}/" --dirs-only
-    printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | grep -qxF -- "${name}/"
-}
-
-# Did a `rclone check` find the two sides the same? Only when it says so
-# both ways: its exit status is 0, and its count of differences is exactly
-# zero. The count alone was the test here, as a substring -- and "10
-# differences found" contains "0 differences found", so a check that found
-# ten changed files let the pointer move and the old folder go, and a new
-# folder holding ten other versions of the same names read as a partial
-# copy to resume into (the audit of the fixes to #307, G-A-01).
-check_clean() { # <rclone check's exit status> <its output>
-    [ "$1" -eq 0 ] 2>/dev/null || return 1
-    printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -qE '(^|[^0-9])0 differences found'
-}
-
-# Relocate a folder by copy, verify, delete -- never `rclone move`.
-#
-# move deletes as it goes, so an interruption -- a handheld dropping off wifi is
-# the normal case, not the exception -- leaves the library split across two
-# paths with no record of which files went where (#57, upgrade-and-install.md).
-# Copy first: a second run finds the copied files already present and skips
-# them. Verify by content with `rclone check`, reading its whole output rather
-# than one line of it (engineering-practices.md: rclone prints "N matching
-# files" last, and a check against the last line matched nothing). Only a
-# verified pass removes the source; a failed one leaves both sides intact and
-# says so.
-#
-# Pipelines are avoided on purpose: `rclone ... | tail` reports tail's status,
-# which is how a short backup once announced itself a success.
-#
-# The tier's pointer is written the moment its copy is verified, before its
-# source is removed (audit #307 PL-026). Both pointers used to be written
-# after both moves, so a run that moved the saves and was cut before the
-# end left SAVES_REMOTE at the emptied folder -- a device syncing to a
-# folder with nothing in it -- and the next run, finding the new folder
-# already there, refused it. Now a cut run leaves each tier either where it
-# was (not yet verified) or where it went (pointer written), and the next
-# run moves only what has not landed.
-#
-# Any filter arguments after the fourth are the tier's own (PL-025): they
-# decide which files are the tier's, so a folder nested in the source that
-# belongs to another tier -- the original layout's backup/ and Content/
-# inside the saves folder -- is neither moved with it nor deleted with it.
-#
-# And the source loses only what was copied and verified (audit #307
-# PL-053). The files are listed once, by those filters, and the list is the
-# whole job: the copy, the check and the deletion each take exactly it
-# (--files-from-raw, which keeps a name's spaces), and the empty folders go
-# after. The old folder used to be purged after a point-in-time check, so a
-# save another device wrote into it between the check and the purge was
-# lost; now it is not on the list, stays where it was written, and is
-# still there for that device's own migration.
-#
-# 0 when the tier moved; 1 when its copy or check failed, the old folder
-# whole; 2 when its pointer could not be written, which set_pointer has
-# said, the old folder whole too.
-# The second device's move, onto a current folder the fleet already made
-# (RELOCATE_MERGE=1, D-CLOUD-168): the first device's move made the folder
-# and removed the old one, and a device still on the old build then wrote
-# its saves back under the old name (the mixed-installation test, step 3),
-# so when it upgrades its old folder holds files and the new one exists.
-# Refusing would strand it on NOT NOW for ever; merging is the sync's own
-# rule -- the newer copy of each file wins -- made non-destructive: every
-# version that differs between the two folders is set aside first, under
-# the same <saves>-replaced/<stamp> shelf the backup keeps its conflict
-# losers on, then the copy runs with --update and the new folder's own
-# overwritten copies go to that shelf too (--backup-dir), and the old
-# folder is removed only once every name it held is present in the new
-# one. Nothing in the new folder is deleted, and nothing is lost: each
-# byte that was in the cloud is in the new folder or on the shelf.
-RELOCATE_MERGE=0
-merge_shelf() { # <dst>: the set-aside beside the destination, one folder per run
-    echo "${1%/}-replaced/$(date +%Y_%m_%d-%H%M%S)-move"
-}
-
-relocate() { # <src> <dst> <what> <pointer key> [filter arguments...]
-    local src="$1" dst="$2" what="$3" key="$4" out list
-    shift 4
-    local -a filt=("$@")
-    # One folder under two spellings is not a move (PL-001): copied onto
-    # itself it checks clean, and the delete after it removes every file
-    # it listed. Refused here whatever the caller compared.
-    if same_folder "${src#*:}" "${dst#*:}"; then
-        say "REFUSING: ${src} and ${dst} are the same folder, so nothing was copied or removed."
-        logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "relocate: ${src} and ${dst} are one folder; refused" 2>/dev/null
-        return 1
-    fi
-    # A destination inside the source -- a saves folder at /ROCKNIX moving
-    # to /ROCKNIX/Saves -- is never listed as the source's own: a run cut
-    # after its copy left part of it there, and the resume moved that copy
-    # into /ROCKNIX/Saves/Saves (PL-001, found with the spelling cases).
-    if inside_folder "${dst#*:}" "${src#*:}"; then
-        filt+=(--exclude "/$(rel_inside "${dst#*:}" "${src#*:}")/**")
-    fi
-    list_or_stop "${src}" -R --files-only "${filt[@]}"
-    if [ -z "${LISTING}" ]; then
-        [ -z "${key}" ] || set_pointer "${key}" "${dst#*:}" || return 2
-        return 0
-    fi
-    list=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud_migrate_layout.XXXXXX) || { say "Couldn't make a working file on this device; nothing was moved."; return 1; }
-    printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" > "${list}"
-    if [ "${RELOCATE_MERGE}" = 1 ]; then
-        merge_into "${src}" "${dst}" "${what}" "${key}" "${list}"
-        return $?
-    fi
-    say "Copying ${what}..."
-    # Under --apply the move runs on a page (GuiCloudTransfer, fork #353):
-    # ">>> doing" names the step for its row 3, and the copy's own progress
-    # goes to stdout for the page's counters (COPYING n OF m), as every
-    # transfer's does; the check and the delete print nothing it reads.
-    local copy_rc
-    if [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ]; then
-        echo ">>> doing copy"
-        rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false --progress --stats 2s \
-            "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${list}.out"; copy_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
-        out=$(cat "${list}.out" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "${list}.out"
-    else
-        out=$(rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1); copy_rc=$?
-    fi
-    if [ "${copy_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
-        printf '%s\n' "${out}" | tail -3
-        # A copy that stopped part-way has put some files in the new
-        # folder; only the old one is as it was (G-A-12).
-        say "Couldn't finish copying ${what}. Nothing was removed from the old folder; some files may already be in the new one."
-        rm -f "${list}"
-        return 1
-    fi
-    say "Verifying ${what}..."
-    [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing verify"
-    out=$(rclone check "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --one-way "${CHECK_OPTS[@]}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1)
-    if ! check_clean $? "${out}"; then
-        printf '%s\n' "${out}" | grep -iE "differ|missing|error" | head -3
-        say "The copy of ${what} didn't match, so nothing was removed from the old folder."
-        rm -f "${list}"
-        return 1
-    fi
-    # The source goes only once the pointer has landed (G-A-02): a pointer
-    # that could not be written leaves the device on the old folder, so the
-    # old folder must still hold everything -- the next run finds the copy
-    # already there and resumes.
-    # A folder with no pointer of its own (the set-aside beside the saves,
-    # named from SAVES_REMOTE by the scripts) has nothing to record here.
-    if [ -n "${key}" ] && ! set_pointer "${key}" "${dst#*:}"; then
-        rm -f "${list}"
-        return 2
-    fi
-    say "Removing the old ${what} folder..."
-    [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing remove"
-    if ! rclone delete "${src}" --files-from-raw "${list}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-        say "The verified copy is in the new folder, but the old files couldn't be removed. Try again to finish."
-        rm -f "${list}"
-        return 1
-    fi
-    rclone rmdirs "${src}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
-    rm -f "${list}"
-    return 0
-}
-
-# relocate's merge half (RELOCATE_MERGE, above): shelf, copy --update, verify
-# by presence, remove. <list> is the source's own file listing.
-merge_into() { # <src> <dst> <what> <pointer key> <list>
-    local src="$1" dst="$2" what="$3" key="$4" list="$5" shelf differ missing out rc
-    shelf="${dst%%:*}:$(merge_shelf "${dst#*:}")"
-    differ=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud_migrate_layout.XXXXXX) || { rm -f "${list}"; return 1; }
-    missing="${differ}.missing"
-    say "Merging ${what} into ${dst}: the newer copy of each file is kept, the other set aside under ${shelf#*:}."
-    # 1. What differs between the two folders is shelved from the source
-    #    first; the destination's own copies the update replaces follow
-    #    through --backup-dir. A check that cannot run shelves nothing and
-    #    stops here (guards fail closed).

-        [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing copy"

-            say "Couldn't set aside the ${what} that differ, so nothing was merged."
-            rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 1
-        fi
-        say "$(grep -c . "${differ}") ${what} file(s) differ between the folders; the old folder's copies are on the shelf."
-    fi
-    # 2. The copy, newer wins; a file the new folder had a newer copy of is
-    #    left as it is, and one it replaces goes to the shelf.
-    say "Copying ${what}..."
-    local copy_rc
-    if [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ]; then
-        echo ">>> doing copy"
-        rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --update --backup-dir "${shelf}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false --progress --stats 2s \
-            "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${list}.out"; copy_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
-        out=$(cat "${list}.out" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "${list}.out"

-        out=$(rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --update --backup-dir "${shelf}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1); copy_rc=$?
-    fi
-    if [ "${copy_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
-        printf '%s\n' "${out}" | tail -3
-        say "Couldn't finish merging ${what}. Nothing was removed from the old folder."
-        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 1
-    fi
-    # 3. Verified by presence: every name the old folder held is in the new
-    #    one. Content may differ where the new folder's copy was newer, and

-    say "Verifying ${what}..."
