-        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 1
-    fi
-    if [ -n "${key}" ] && ! set_pointer "${key}" "${dst#*:}"; then
-        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 2
-    fi
-    say "Removing the old ${what} folder..."
-    [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing remove"
-    if ! rclone delete "${src}" --files-from-raw "${list}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-        say "The merged files are in the new folder, but the old files couldn't be removed. Try again to finish."
-        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"
-        return 1
-    fi
-    rclone rmdirs "${src}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
-    rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"
-    return 0
-}
-
-# Point a key of the conf at a tier's new folder: the line rewritten in
-# place, or added when the conf has none -- and then read back. A write
-# that did not land (a full or read-only /storage, a path sed's
-# replacement would mangle) is a failure the caller must stop on, before
-# anything is removed (the audit of the fixes to #307, G-A-02): its result
-# used to go unread, and relocate deleted the old folder after it either
-# way, leaving the device pointed at a folder the run had just emptied.
-# 0 when the conf now says <remote path>, 1 when it does not.
-set_pointer() { # <key> <remote path>
-    if grep -q "^$1=" "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null; then
-        sed -i "s|^$1=.*|$1=\"$2\"|" "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null
-    else
-        printf '%s="%s"\n' "$1" "$2" >> "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null
-    fi
-    if [ "$(conf_value "$1")" != "$2" ]; then
-        say "Couldn't save the new folder in this device's settings. It still uses the old one, and nothing was removed from it."
-        echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE SAVED"
-        logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "could not write $1 to ${SYNC_CONF}; stopped before removing anything" 2>/dev/null
-        return 1
-    fi
-    say "Now using ${2:-the root of your cloud} for your $(tier_words "$1")."
-}
-
-# Pointer-only transitions describe one layout. Stage every change beside the
-# config, then publish it with one rename: failure at any write keeps the old
-# selection intact and a retry still sees the original transition (#471 PL-002).
-# Real copy/move steps keep their per-tier verified publication and recovery
-# record; they must not point at a destination before its copy is complete.
-set_pointers() { # <key> <path> [<key> <path> ...]
-    local tmp target="${SYNC_CONF}" rc=1
-    tmp=$(mktemp "${SYNC_CONF}.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || tmp=""
-    if [ -n "${tmp}" ] && [ -f "${target}" ] && cp -p "${target}" "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null; then
-        (
-            SYNC_CONF="${tmp}"
-            while [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; do
-                set_pointer "$1" "$2" >/dev/null || exit 1
-                shift 2
-            done
-        ) && mv -f "${tmp}" "${target}" 2>/dev/null && rc=0
-    fi
-    if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
-        [ -z "${tmp}" ] || rm -f "${tmp}"
-        say "Couldn't save the new folders in this device's settings. Its previous folder choices are unchanged."
-        echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE SAVED"
-        return 1
-    fi
-    while [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; do
-        say "Now using ${2:-the root of your cloud} for your $(tier_words "$1")."
-        shift 2
-    done
-}
-
-# A tier as the player knows it (es-player-text.md: the four tiers), for
-# the tidy page's lines -- which named the config key (audit of the fixes,
-# claude G-A-11).
-tier_words() { # <pointer key>
-    case "$1" in
-        SAVES_REMOTE) echo "saves" ;;
-        SETTINGS_REMOTE) echo "settings backups" ;;
-        CONTENT_REMOTE) echo "ROMs, BIOS, and game content" ;;
-        *) echo "files" ;;
-    esac
-}
-
-# Is an existing destination a partial copy of this source, and nothing else?
-#
-# The refusals below exist so two devices' libraries are never merged. But a
-# copy interrupted half-way also leaves a destination that exists, and the same
-# refusal would then block the resume forever. The two cases differ in one
-# checkable way: a partial copy holds nothing that did not come from the
-# source. The reverse one-way check asks exactly that -- every file in dst is
-# present and identical in src -- so a foreign file in dst fails it and the
-# refusal stands.
-resumable() {
-    local src="$1" dst="$2" out
-    out=$(rclone check "${dst}" "${src}" --one-way "${CHECK_OPTS[@]}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1)
-    check_clean $? "${out}" && return 0
-    # The equality check handles a subset of completed files, but a killed
-    # upload can also leave one file truncated (#479). Only the original,
-    # validated recovery record permits checking that case. Every destination
-    # name must exist in the source, and every byte must match its prefix;
-    # neither a record alone nor a smaller size authorizes a foreign merge.
-    [ "${MIGRATION_RESUMING}" = 1 ] || return 1
-    local source_files destination_files rows row name size source_hash destination_hash
-    source_files=$(rclone lsjson "${src}" --recursive --files-only "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
-    destination_files=$(rclone lsjson "${dst}" --recursive --files-only "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
-    rows=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "${source_files}" "${destination_files}" | jq -cer -s '
-        def valid:
-          type=="array" and all(.[];
-            (.Path | type=="string" and length>0 and
-              (explode | all(.[]; .>=32)) and
-              (split("/") | all(.[]; .!="" and .!="." and .!=".."))) and
-            (.Size | type=="number" and .>=0 and floor==.)) and
-          ((map(.Path) | unique | length)==length);
-        if length!=2 or (all(.[]; valid) | not) then error("invalid file listing") else . end |
-        (reduce .[0][] as $file ({}; .[$file.Path]=$file.Size)) as $source |
-        .[1] |
-        if length==0 or
-           (all(.[]; $source[.Path]!=null and .Size<=$source[.Path]) | not) or
-           (any(.[]; .Size<$source[.Path]) | not)
-        then error("not a truncated subset")
-        else .[] | [.Path,.Size] | @base64 end') || return 1
-    while IFS= read -r row; do
-        row=$(printf '%s' "${row}" | base64 -d) || return 1
-        name=$(printf '%s' "${row}" | jq -r '.[0]') || return 1
-        size=$(printf '%s' "${row}" | jq -r '.[1]') || return 1
-        # pipefail is local to each subshell: a failed provider read
-        # must never become the successful hash of an empty stream.
-        destination_hash=$(set -o pipefail; rclone cat "${dst%/}/${name}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null | sha256sum) || return 1
-        source_hash=$(set -o pipefail; rclone cat "${src%/}/${name}" --count "${size}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null | sha256sum) || return 1
-        [ "${source_hash}" = "${destination_hash}" ] || return 1
-    done <<< "${rows}"
-    return 0
-}
-
-# What cloud_sync_helper would have derived CONTENT_REMOTE to be for a given
-# SAVES_REMOTE. The helper deliberately derives it rather than taking the shipped
-# default, so that ROMs and saves stay in one namespace -- its own comment
-# calls a split "worse than either layout alone".
-#
-# That is exactly what this script used to produce: it moved saves and backups
-# to /ROCKNIX and left CONTENT_REMOTE behind, so a migrated device looked for its
-# ROMs under a /GAMES that no longer had anything in it. Matching against the
-# derived value is how we tell our own pointer from one the owner chose --
-# theirs is left alone.
-derived_content() {
-    local sync="$1" parent
-    parent=$(dirname "${sync}")
-    [ "${parent}" = "/" ] && parent="${sync}"
-    echo "${parent%/}/Content"
-}
-
-# RC2 could finish its saves/backups moves before /GAMES/Content; run101
-# could finish both pointers before its discarded/content tiers (#391).
-# Only these exact earlier defaults are inherited derived content. A custom
-# path ending in /Content is still the player's independent choice.
-historical_content() {
-    same_folder "$1" /GAMES/Content || same_folder "$1" /ROCKNIX/Content
-}
-
-moving_content() { # <saves source> <content pointer>
-    [ -n "$2" ] && ! same_folder "$2" "${NEW_CONTENT}" || return 1
-    same_folder "$2" "$(derived_content "$(folder_abs "$1")")" && return 0
-    { superseded_default "$1" || same_folder "$1" "${NEW_SAVES}"; } && historical_content "$2"
-}
-
-# Move content to the current namespace if it is safe to, and repoint the
-# config. Never merges into an existing destination -- that is the same
-# interruptible half-migrated state the saves move refuses.
-migrate_content() {
-    local remote="$1" content="$2" mode="$3"
-
-    if has_entries "${remote}${content}/"; then
-        if exists "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}" && ! resumable "${remote}${content}" "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}"; then
-            if fleet_made "${remote}"; then
-                RELOCATE_MERGE=1   # the fleet's folder: the second device's content merges (D-CLOUD-168)
-            else
-                say "REFUSING: ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT} already exists, and ${remote}${content}"
-                say "holds files. Nothing moved and the config is unchanged -- merging two"
-                say "content folders is not something to do without being asked."
-                [ "${mode}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> why THE NEW FOLDER ALREADY HAS FILES IN IT"
-                return 4
-            fi
-        fi
-        say "Would copy, verify, then remove  ${remote}${content}  ->  ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}"
-        if [ "${mode}" != "--apply" ]; then
-            echo ">>> plan content ${NEW_ROOT}"
-            say "Nothing has been changed. Run with --apply to do it."
-            return 0
-        fi
-        local rrc=0
-        relocate "${remote}${content}" "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}" "content" CONTENT_REMOTE || rrc=$?
-        if [ "${rrc}" -ne 0 ]; then
-            # 2 is a pointer that could not be written, which has said so.
-            if [ "${rrc}" -ne 2 ]; then
-                say "The config is unchanged."
-                echo ">>> why SOME FILES DIDN'T FINISH"
-            fi
-            return 5
-        fi
-        say "Content is now at ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}."
-        return 0
-    else
-        say "Nothing is stored at ${remote}${content}, so only the setting changes."
-        if [ "${mode}" != "--apply" ]; then
-            echo ">>> plan none ${NEW_ROOT}"
-            say "Nothing has been changed. Run with --apply to do it."
-            return 0
-        fi
-    fi
-
-    set_pointer CONTENT_REMOTE "${NEW_CONTENT}" || return 5
-    say "Content is now at ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}."
-    return 0
-}
-
-# --- the layout as facts (#353, #356) -----------------------------------
-#
-# One line per fact and nothing the interface has to parse out of prose:
-#
-#   STATE=current               the saves folder is the current default
-#   STATE=kept                  a superseded default this device chose to keep (--keep)
-#   STATE=superseded-with-files a default this project once shipped, holding saves:
-#                               the move is offered (D-CLOUD-160)
-#   STATE=superseded-empty      such a default with nothing in it, or absent:
-#                               the creation of the current layout is offered (D-CLOUD-161)
-#   STATE=own                   a folder the player chose; nothing is offered
-#   CURRENT_EXISTS=0|1          whether the current default's saves folder lists
-#   MARKER=layout=<n> | -       the cloud's marker, when one is there
-# An unrecorded old shelf can be an interrupted predecessor's, or a sibling's
-# live history. If saves still live at the earlier root, leave its shelf there.
-# A retained migration record identifies its own source independently and does
-# not use this inference. Failed listings still stop through has_files/entries.
-inherited_discarded() { # <remote>; sets RECOVERY_DISCARDED and RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL
-    local remote="$1" earlier
-    RECOVERY_DISCARDED=""
-    RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL=()
-    for earlier in "${SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[@]}"; do
-        has_entries "${remote}${earlier}-replaced/" || continue
-        if [ "${earlier}" = /GAMES ]; then
-            # The old root nests settings/content beside the actual saves.
-            has_files "${remote}${earlier}/" --exclude '/backup/**' \
-                --exclude '/Content/**' --exclude '/README.txt' && continue
-        else
-            has_files "${remote}${earlier}/" --exclude '/README.txt' && continue
-        fi
-        RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL+=("${earlier}-replaced")
-    done
-    [ "${#RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL[@]}" -gt 0 ] || return 1
-    RECOVERY_DISCARDED="${RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL[0]}"
-    return 0
-}
-
-layout_state() { # <remote> <saves> <backups> <content>
-    local remote="$1" saves="$2" backups="$3" content="$4" state keep cur=0 marker old_replaced=""
-    if [ -e "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" ]; then
-        migration_record_load "${remote}" || return $?
-        printf 'STATE=migration-pending\nSOURCE=%s\nCURRENT=%s\n' "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"
-        return 0
-    fi
-    keep=$(conf_value LAYOUT_KEEP) || return 2
-    echo "SAVES=${saves}"
-    echo "BACKUPS=${backups}"
-    echo "CONTENT=${content}"
-    echo "CURRENT=${NEW_SAVES}"
-    # The folder this device is configured for is one witness; the cloud is
-    # the other. A device upgraded from stock carries /GAMES in its conf
-    # while its saves sit in /ROCKNIX/Saves, made by its sibling on the
-    # fork's earlier build (the Retroid Pocket Nova, 2026-10-01): read from
-    # the conf alone it is "superseded, empty" and would be offered a fresh
-    # /pixelelated beside its real saves. So every default this project
-    # once shipped is looked at, and the one holding files is the source
-    # the move is offered from (SOURCE=), the configured one or not.
-    local source=""
-    if same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"; then
-        state=current
-        # Older builds wrote no recovery record. Their current primary
-        # pointers do not prove the derived content or discarded shelf moved.
-        # This is a folder-page read, never an extra probe on a direct sync.
-        if same_folder "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}"; then
-            if historical_content "${content}"; then
-                state=migration-pending
-            else
-                inherited_discarded "${remote}" && state=migration-pending
-            fi
-        fi
-    elif [ -n "${keep}" ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${keep}"; then
-        state=kept
-    elif superseded_default "${saves}"; then
-        superseded_source "${remote}" "${saves}"; source="${SOURCE_FOUND}"
-        if [ -n "${source}" ]; then state=superseded-with-files; else state=superseded-empty; fi
-    else
-        state=own
-    fi
-    echo "SOURCE=${source:--}"
-    exists "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}" && cur=1
-    echo "CURRENT_EXISTS=${cur}"
-    marker=$(rclone cat "${remote}${NEW_SAVES%/*}/${LAYOUT_MARKER}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -cd 'a-z0-9=')
-    echo "MARKER=${marker:--}"
-    echo "STATE=${state}"
-    return 0
-}
-
-# KEEP USING <folder>: asked once (D-CLOUD-160). The conf remembers the
-# folder kept, so --state reads "kept" until the folder changes.
-layout_keep() { # <saves>
-    set_pointer LAYOUT_KEEP "$1" || return 1
-    say "Keeping ${1}; the move will not be offered again for this folder."
-    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "layout kept at $1 by request" 2>/dev/null
-    return 0
-}
-
-# "Your other devices will follow": a device on a superseded default whose
-# current-default folder already exists in the cloud -- another device made
-# the move -- is re-pointed with no question and one line in the journal.
-# Nothing is copied or removed here; the folders are already where they
-# belong. 0 when the device now points at the current layout, 3 when there
-# was nothing to follow, 1 when the conf could not be written.
-layout_follow() { # <remote> <saves> <backups> <content>
-    local remote="$1" saves="$2" backups="$3" content="$4" keep
-    same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" && return 3
-    superseded_default "${saves}" || return 3
-    keep=$(conf_value LAYOUT_KEEP) || return 2
-    [ -n "${keep}" ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${keep}" && return 3
-    # One listing for the usual answer, "no device has moved yet": the
-    # current folder's parent, which names Saves/ once it exists (exists()
-    # would list the folder and then its parent, two rclone starts).
-    list_or_stop "${remote}${NEW_SAVES%/*}/" --dirs-only
-    printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | grep -qxF -- "${NEW_SAVES##*/}/" || return 3
-    # A device whose old folder still holds files is not followed: they
-    # would be stranded in a folder nothing reads once the pointer moves
-    # (the futro's pre-mortem, 2026-10-01). The move is offered instead,
-    # which copies, verifies and only then removes.
-    has_files "${remote}${saves}/" && return 3
-    backup_pointer_for "${remote}" "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}"
-    local -a pointers=(SAVES_REMOTE "${NEW_SAVES}" SETTINGS_REMOTE "${NEXT_BACKUPS}")
-    # Content follows only where it was derived from the old folder or
-    # never set; a folder the player chose for ROMs stays theirs.
-    if content_unset || same_folder "${content}" "$(derived_content "$(folder_abs "${saves}")")" \
-       || same_folder "${content}" "${saves%/}/Content"; then
-        pointers+=(CONTENT_REMOTE "${NEW_CONTENT}")
-    fi
-    set_pointers "${pointers[@]}" || return 1
-    say "Followed: this device now uses ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}, which another device already made."
-    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "followed the fleet from ${saves} to ${NEW_SAVES}" 2>/dev/null
-    return 0
-}
-
-# A fresh install beside a fleet still on the earlier folder: this device
-# is on the current default, the current saves folder holds no saves (it
-# is not there, or only the seeding's folders and README are), and a
-# folder this project once shipped as its default does hold them. Without
-# this the device was offered CREATE IT beside the player's saves, and saw
-# none of them on its first restore -- the mixed-installation test's fresh
-# device (D-CLOUD-158). It is pointed at the earlier folder's layout -- a
-# setting, nothing copied -- so it reads and writes where the saves are,
-# and is then offered the move as every device on that folder is

-# when the conf could not be written.
-layout_join() { # <remote> <saves> <content>

-        has_files "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}/" --exclude '/README.txt' && return 3
-    elif superseded_default "${saves}"; then
-        # The Nova's shape (2026-09-30): a carried /GAMES with nothing in it,
-        # the saves in /ROCKNIX/Saves beside it. Joined, the move is offered
-        # from the folder that holds them and KEEP USING keeps that folder;
-        # left on /GAMES, KEEP USING /ROCKNIX recorded /GAMES.

-        [ -n "${keep}" ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${keep}" && return 3
-        has_files "${remote}${saves}/" && return 3

-        return 3
-    fi

-    earlier_layout "${SOURCE_FOUND}" "${content}"

-    say "Joined: this device now uses ${remote}${E_SAVES}, where your saves already are."
-    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "joined the fleet at ${E_SAVES}: no saves in ${NEW_SAVES}" 2>/dev/null
-    return 0
-}
-
-# The wizard's seeding step (cloud_setup --seed-folders): join the earlier
-# folder that holds the saves; else a device still on a default this
-# project once shipped, with nothing in it and nothing anywhere, is on no
-# folder at all (D-CLOUD-161) and is pointed at the current folders, which
-# the seeding then makes and lists, as it does for any new cloud. Seeding
-# the carried /GAMES itself put a README there, which every later check

-    local -a pointers=(SAVES_REMOTE "${NEW_SAVES}" SETTINGS_REMOTE "${NEXT_BACKUPS}")

-    fi
-    set_pointers "${pointers[@]}" || return 1
-    say "Your cloud had nothing in ${remote}${saves}; this device now uses ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}."
-    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "settled a carried ${saves} with nothing in it on ${NEW_SAVES}" 2>/dev/null
-    return 0

-# Did another device of ours make the current layout? The marker at the
-# folder's parent says so (write_marker, after a move or a seeding). A
-# current folder with no marker is somebody's own folder of the same name,
-# which the refusals below still protect.
-fleet_made() { # <remote>
-    [ "${REMOTE_LAYOUT}" = "${LAYOUT_VERSION}" ]
-}

-# A marker is a version, not merely a prefix. Validate its complete bytes;

-# failed read is not absence if the parent still lists the marker.
-read_marker() { # <remote>

-        rm -f "${tmp}"
-        list_or_stop "${1}${NEW_ROOT}/" --files-only

-        return 0
-    fi

-        fi
-    done

-    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
-    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "unsupported or malformed layout marker; refused" 2>/dev/null
-    return 4
-}

-write_marker() { # <remote>

-        read_marker "$1" || return $?
-        [ "${REMOTE_LAYOUT}" = "${LAYOUT_VERSION}" ] || return 5
-        return 0
-    fi
-    say "Your files moved, but the cloud folder setup didn't finish. Try the move again to finish it."
-    echo ">>> why SOME FILES DIDN'T FINISH"
-    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "could not write ${LAYOUT_MARKER} at ${1}${NEW_SAVES%/*}" 2>/dev/null
-    return 5

-# Local recovery state keeps the sources after their live pointers advance.
-# It is never sourced as shell and never grants permission to merge a foreign
-# destination. Each retry still verifies the actual cloud bytes. A record is
-# bound to the remote configuration and the original/current pointer choices.
-remote_fingerprint() {
-    # rclone refreshes OAuth tokens during ordinary transfers. Bind the
-    # configured provider/root, not that routinely changing credential, file
-    # comments, whitespace or field order. Let rclone parse its own syntax;
-    # credentials pass only through memory to the digest, never into the record.
-    local config
-    if [ "${1:-}" = legacy ]; then

-MODE="--check"
-main() {

-    local mode="${1:---check}"
-    local remote saves backups content old_root

-    remote=$(remote_name)

-        say "No cloud remote is configured; nothing to migrate."

-    # The cloud answers before anything is asked of it (PL-027): a remote

-    # 2026-10-01). Nothing it writes depends on either.
-    local probe_rc
-    if [ "${mode}" != "--follow" ]; then
-        rclone lsd "${remote}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; probe_rc=$?
-        [ "${probe_rc}" -eq 0 ] || unreadable "${remote}" "${probe_rc}"
-    fi

-    local net_opts
-    net_opts=$(conf_value RCLONE_NET_OPTS | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ //; s/ $//')
-    [ -n "${net_opts}" ] || net_opts="${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_FALLBACK}"

-    # fixes, G-A-11/G-A-10); one that fails or times out reads as "no

-    case "${features}" in *'"CaseInsensitive":false'*) CASE_INSENSITIVE=0 ;; *) CASE_INSENSITIVE=1 ;; esac

-    saves=$(conf_value SAVES_REMOTE)
-    backups=$(conf_value SETTINGS_REMOTE)
-
-    content=$(conf_value CONTENT_REMOTE)
-
-    # Each pointer as the folder it names (PL-001): cleaned for the paths

-    # left exactly as it is.

-            echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"
-            logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "a pointer has a .. component; nothing done" 2>/dev/null

-    # seeding through --settle. A custom layout elsewhere is independent.
-    if superseded_default "${saves}" || same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"; then
-        read_marker "${remote}" || return $?
-    fi

-    # A layout the owner chose is current too. CHANGE CLOUD FOLDER writes the

-        --keep)   layout_keep "${saves}"; return $? ;;
-        --follow) layout_follow "${remote}" "${saves}" "${backups}" "${content}"; return $? ;;

-    # Step 1 is the supported predecessor (unmarked/layout 1) to layout 2.

-        *) return 4 ;;
-    esac

+folder_listing() { # <remote path> [lsf flags]; missing is distinct from unreadable
+    local path="$1" rc; shift
+    FOLDER_LISTING=$(rclone lsf "$@" "${path}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
+    [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ] || return 0

+    # establish presence or absence, even for a not-found return code.
+    if [ -n "${FOLDER_LISTING}" ]; then
+        echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
+        return "${rc}"
+    fi
+    if [ "${rc}" -eq 3 ] || [ "${rc}" -eq 4 ] || absent_not_broken "${path}"; then
+        FOLDER_LISTING=""
+        return 0
+    fi
+    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
+    return "${rc}"
+}
+folder_exists() { # return 0 present, 1 absent, or >1 unreadable
+    local path="$1" remote relative parent name rc
+    # An absolute remote root and its relative home are different on SFTP.
+    case "${path#*:}" in /) ;; *) path="${path%/}" ;; esac
+    folder_listing "${path}"; rc=$?
+    [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || return 5
+    [ -z "${FOLDER_LISTING}" ] || return 0

+    case "${path#*:}" in ""|/) return 0 ;; esac
+    remote="${path%%:*}:"; relative="${path#*:}"
+    name="${relative##*/}"
+    [ -n "${name}" ] || return 1

+    # to remote:/. Preserve that distinction for SFTP and similar providers.
+    case "${relative}" in */*) parent="${relative%/*}/" ;; *) parent="" ;; esac
+    folder_listing "${remote}${parent}" --dirs-only; rc=$?
+    [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || return 5
+    printf '%s\n' "${FOLDER_LISTING}" | grep -qxF -- "${name}/"
+}
+folder_current_namespace() {
+    local identity="${SAVES#/}" features folding
+    [ "${identity}" = pixelelated/Saves ] && return 0
+    [ "${identity,,}" = pixelelated/saves ] || return 1
+    # Case variants are the default only on a folding provider. Read the
+    # selected parent in its own spelling; SFTP leading slashes still matter.
+    features=$(rclone backend features "${REMOTE}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || features=""
+    folding=$(printf '%s' "${features}" | jq -r 'if .Features.CaseInsensitive == true then "true" elif .Features.CaseInsensitive == false then "false" else "unknown" end' 2>/dev/null)
+    case "${folding}" in
+        true) return 0 ;;
+        false) return 1 ;;
+        *)
+            echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
+            return 5 ;;
+    esac
+}
+folder_marker_read() {
+    FOLDER_VERSION=0
+    # Custom/legacy paths are independent choices, not a renamed layout.
+    folder_current_namespace; local scope=$?
+    case "${scope}" in 0) ;; 1) return 0 ;; *) return "${scope}" ;; esac
+    local tmp rc version
+    tmp=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud_folder_marker.XXXXXX) || return 5
+    rclone cat "${REMOTE}${SAVES%/*}/.layout" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" > "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
+    if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
+        rm -f "${tmp}"
+        folder_listing "${REMOTE}${SAVES%/*}/" --files-only || return $?
+        if printf '%s\n' "${FOLDER_LISTING}" | grep -qxF '.layout'; then
+            echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
+            return "${rc}"
+        fi
+        return 0
+    fi
+    for version in 1 2; do
+        if printf 'layout=%s\n' "${version}" | cmp -s - "${tmp}"; then
+            FOLDER_VERSION="${version}"
+            rm -f "${tmp}"
+            return 0
+        fi
+    done
+    rm -f "${tmp}"
+    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
+    echo "This cloud folder uses a layout this version can't read. Check for a newer system version before trying again."
+    return 4
+}
+folder_marker_write() {
+    folder_current_namespace; local scope=$?
+    case "${scope}" in 0) ;; 1) return 0 ;; *) return "${scope}" ;; esac
+    folder_marker_read || return $?
+    printf 'layout=2\n' | rclone rcat "${REMOTE}${SAVES%/*}/.layout" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || return 5
+    folder_marker_read || return $?
+    [ "${FOLDER_VERSION}" = 2 ] || return 5
+}

+    local remotes config_file config_id

+    [ -n "${REMOTE}" ] || return 2
+    config_file=$(timeout 3 rclone config file 2>/dev/null | tail -1)

+    config_id=$( set -o pipefail; { printf '%s\0' "${REMOTE}" "${SAVES}" "${BACKUPS}" "${CONTENT}";

+    } | sha256sum) || return 2
+    config_id="${config_id%% *}"

+        --arg saves "${SAVES}" --arg settings "${BACKUPS}" --arg content "${CONTENT}" \
+        '{schema_version:1,config_id:$id,remote:$remote,paths:{saves:$saves,settings:$settings,content:$content,
+          roms:(($content | rtrimstr("/")) + (if $content == "" then "" else "/" end) + "ROMs"),bios:(($content | rtrimstr("/")) + (if $content == "" then "" else "/" end) + "BIOS"),media:(($content | rtrimstr("/")) + (if $content == "" then "" else "/" end) + "ROMs")}}'

+def completed_audit_marker(marker, root, now):
+    """Validate an exact Phase 7 completion receipt before it resets cadence."""
+    root = Path(root).resolve()
+    marker = Path(marker)
+    audit = marker.parent.resolve()
+    if not audit.is_relative_to(root / 'docs/audits') or marker.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError('completion marker outside audit directory')
+    data = json.loads(marker.read_text())

+        raise ValueError('invalid completed-audit schema')

+    if ended.tzinfo is None or ended > now:

+    required = {str((audit / name).relative_to(root)) for name in ['04-analysis.md', '05-punch-list.md']}
+    required.update([data['tracker_readback'], data['tracker_completion']])

+        raise ValueError('completion receipt omits required evidence')
+    for name, expected in data['evidence'].items():
+        path = root / name
+        if Path(name).is_absolute() or path.is_symlink() or not path.resolve().is_relative_to(root):

+            or data['issue'] not in receipt.get('closed_completed', [])
+            or receipt.get('verified_utc') != data['completed_at']):

+

diff --git a/tools/cloud-save-integrity b/tools/cloud-save-integrity
new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..a538d90096
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/cloud-save-integrity
@@ -0,0 +1,219 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+# Copyright (C) 2026-present pixelelated
+"""Offline save-byte verification; no network, device actions or repair (#517).
+
+Input: before.json/after.json (successful full rclone lsjson --hash-type Dropbox),
+ordered.json (before sorted by Path), reads.json (index/rc/bytes), payloads/0000...
+from a bounded, separately authorized collector. Keep this directory private.
+This verifier cannot prove the collector's scope or honest success receipts.
+Exit 0 means byte checks passed and no supported-container defect was found;
+raw/core-specific semantics and emulator compatibility are ALWAYS unverified.
+
+Dropbox: https://docs.dropboxapi.com/dropbox-api/docs/technical-reference/content-hash
+RZIP v1: libretro-common/streams/rzip_stream.c; RASTATE v1: RetroArch/tasks/task_save.c
+PNG: chunk CRC, IHDR, IDAT zlib and non-interlaced scanline checks only, not rendering.
+"""
+import argparse
+import collections
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import struct
+import sys
+import zlib
+
+LIMIT = 64 * 1024 * 1024
+BLOCK = 4 * 1024 * 1024
+PNG = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
+
+
+def require(condition, reason):
+    if not condition:
+        raise ValueError(reason)
+
+
+def dropbox_hash(data):
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    for i in range(0, len(data), BLOCK):
+        h.update(hashlib.sha256(data[i:i + BLOCK]).digest())
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def inflate(data, limit):
+    require(0 <= limit <= LIMIT, 'decompression-bound')
+    d = zlib.decompressobj()
+    result = d.decompress(data, limit + 1)
+    require(len(result) <= limit and d.eof and not d.unused_data and not d.unconsumed_tail,
+            'incomplete-or-excess-zlib-stream')
+    return result
+
+
+def rastate(data):
+    if not data.startswith(b'RASTATE'):
+        return 'core-payload-unverified'
+    require(data[:8] == b'RASTATE\x01', 'unsupported-rastate-version')
+    p, mem = 8, False
+    while p + 8 <= len(data):
+        tag, size = data[p:p + 4], struct.unpack_from('<I', data, p + 4)[0]
+        p += 8
+        require(size <= len(data) - p, 'truncated-rastate-block')
+        if tag == b'END ':
+            require(size == 0 and mem, 'invalid-rastate-end')
+            # Some writers allocate trailing zero padding; it is not game state.
+            require(not any(data[p:]), 'nonzero-rastate-tail')
+            return 'rastate-envelope-ok-core-unverified'
+        if tag == b'MEM ':
+            require(size > 0 and not mem, 'invalid-rastate-mem')
+            mem = True
+        p += (size + 7) & ~7
+        require(p <= len(data), 'truncated-rastate-padding')
+    raise ValueError('missing-rastate-end')
+
+
+def rzip(data):
+    require(len(data) >= 20 and data[:8] == b'#RZIPv\x01#', 'unsupported-or-truncated-rzip')
+    chunk, total = struct.unpack_from('<IQ', data, 8)
+    require(0 < chunk <= LIMIT and 0 < total <= LIMIT, 'rzip-size-bound')
+    p, output = 20, bytearray()
+    while len(output) < total:
+        require(p + 4 <= len(data), 'missing-rzip-chunk')
+        size = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, p)[0]
+        p += 4
+        require(0 < size <= len(data) - p, 'truncated-rzip-chunk')
+        block = inflate(data[p:p + size], min(chunk, total - len(output)))
+        require(len(block) == min(chunk, total - len(output)), 'rzip-chunk-length')
+        output.extend(block)
+        p += size
+    require(p == len(data), 'rzip-trailing-data')
+    return 'rzip-stream-ok/' + rastate(bytes(output))
+
+
+def png(data):
+    require(data.startswith(PNG), 'invalid-png-signature')
+    p, chunks, image = 8, [], bytearray()
+    header = None
+    while p + 12 <= len(data):
+        size = struct.unpack_from('>I', data, p)[0]
+        tag = data[p + 4:p + 8]
+        require(size <= len(data) - p - 12, 'truncated-png-chunk')
+        value = data[p + 8:p + 8 + size]
+        crc = struct.unpack_from('>I', data, p + 8 + size)[0]
+        require(zlib.crc32(tag + value) & 0xffffffff == crc, 'png-crc')
+        p += size + 12
+        if not chunks:
+            require(tag == b'IHDR' and size == 13, 'missing-png-header')
+            header = struct.unpack('>IIBBBBB', value)
+        elif tag == b'IHDR':
+            raise ValueError('duplicate-png-header')
+        if tag == b'IDAT':
+            require(b'IDAT' not in chunks or chunks[-1] == b'IDAT',
+                    'nonconsecutive-png-data')
+            image.extend(value)
+        chunks.append(tag)
+        if tag == b'IEND':
+            require(size == 0 and p == len(data) and b'IDAT' in chunks, 'invalid-png-end')
+            break
+    require(chunks and chunks[-1] == b'IEND', 'missing-png-end')
+    w, h, depth, color, compression, filtering, interlace = header
+    depths = {0: (1, 2, 4, 8, 16), 2: (8, 16), 3: (1, 2, 4, 8), 4: (8, 16), 6: (8, 16)}
+    require(w > 0 and h > 0 and color in depths and depth in depths[color]
+            and compression == 0 and filtering == 0 and interlace in (0, 1), 'invalid-png-header')
+    if color == 3:
+        require(b'PLTE' in chunks and chunks.index(b'PLTE') < chunks.index(b'IDAT'), 'missing-png-palette')
+    pixels = inflate(bytes(image), LIMIT)
+    if interlace:
+        return 'png-crc-zlib-ok-interlaced-layout-unverified'
+    channels = {0: 1, 2: 3, 3: 1, 4: 2, 6: 4}[color]
+    row = 1 + (w * channels * depth + 7) // 8
+    require(row * h <= LIMIT and len(pixels) == row * h, 'png-scanline-length')
+    require(all(pixels[n] <= 4 for n in range(0, len(pixels), row)), 'png-row-filter')
+    return 'png-crc-zlib-scanlines-ok-rendering-unverified'
+
+
+def structure(data, path):
+    if data.startswith(PNG) or path.lower().endswith('.png'):
+        return png(data)
+    if data.startswith(b'#RZIP'):
+        return rzip(data)
+    if data.startswith(b'RASTATE'):
+        return rastate(data)
+    return 'raw-or-unsupported-structure-unverified'
+
+
+def inventory(rows):
+    require(isinstance(rows, list) and 0 < len(rows) <= 4096, 'inventory-count')
+    seen, size = {}, 0
+    for f in rows:
+        path = f['Path']
+        require(isinstance(path, str) and not path.startswith('/')
+                and all(part not in ('', '.', '..') for part in path.split('/'))
+                and not any(ord(c) < 32 for c in path), 'unsafe-inventory-path')
+        require(path not in seen and f['IsDir'] is False, 'duplicate-or-directory')
+        require(type(f['Size']) is int and 0 <= f['Size'] <= LIMIT, 'file-size-bound')
+        digest = f.get('Hashes', {}).get('dropbox', '')
+        require(isinstance(digest, str) and re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{64}', digest), 'missing-provider-hash')
+        require(isinstance(f.get('ID'), str) and f['ID'] and isinstance(f.get('ModTime'), str)
+                and f['ModTime'], 'missing-identity')
+        seen[path] = (f['Size'], f['ModTime'], f['ID'], digest)
+        size += f['Size']
+    require(size <= 128 * 1024 * 1024, 'total-size-bound')
+    return seen
+
+
+def verify(root):
+    def read(name):
+        p = root / name
+        require(p.stat().st_size <= 8 * 1024 * 1024, 'metadata-size-bound')
+        return json.loads(p.read_text())
+    before, after, ordered, reads = [read(x) for x in ('before.json', 'after.json', 'ordered.json', 'reads.json')]
+    original = inventory(before)
+    require(original == inventory(after), 'cloud-changed-during-read')
+    require(original == inventory(ordered) and ordered == sorted(before, key=lambda x: x['Path']),
+            'ordered-manifest-mismatch')
+    require(isinstance(reads, list) and len(reads) == len(ordered), 'incomplete-read-receipts')
+    outcomes = []
+    for i, (entry, receipt) in enumerate(zip(ordered, reads)):
+        row = {'index': i, 'bytes': entry['Size'], 'playability': 'unverified'}
+        try:
+            require(receipt['index'] == i and receipt['rc'] == 0, 'read-failed')
+            p = root / 'payloads' / f'{i:04d}'
+            require(not p.is_symlink() and p.is_file() and p.stat().st_size <= LIMIT, 'missing-or-invalid-payload')
+            data = p.read_bytes()
+            require(len(data) == entry['Size'] == receipt['bytes'], 'size-mismatch')
+            require(dropbox_hash(data) == entry['Hashes']['dropbox'], 'provider-hash-mismatch')
+            row.update(byte_integrity='ok', sha256=hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest())
+            row['structure'] = structure(data, entry['Path'])
+        except (ValueError, OSError, zlib.error, KeyError) as e:
+            row['error'] = str(e) if isinstance(e, ValueError) else type(e).__name__
+        outcomes.append(row)
+    summary = {'files': len(outcomes), 'bytes_ok': sum(x.get('byte_integrity') == 'ok' for x in outcomes),
+               'errors': sum('error' in x for x in outcomes),
+               'structure': dict(collections.Counter(x.get('structure', 'not-verified') for x in outcomes)),
+               'cloud_inventory_stable': True, 'playability': 'unverified'}
+    return {'summary': summary, 'files': outcomes}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('packet', type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument('--report', type=Path, required=True, help='New private JSON file; never overwrites')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    os.umask(0o077)
+    try:
+        result = verify(args.packet)
+        with args.report.open('x') as f:
+            json.dump(result, f, indent=2)
+            f.write('\n')
+        print(json.dumps(result['summary']))
+        return int(result['summary']['errors'] > 0)
+    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
+        # Paths and provider identities stay out of stdout/stderr.
+        print('Verification refused: ' + (str(e) if type(e) is ValueError else type(e).__name__), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/tools/cloud-save-integrity-test b/tools/cloud-save-integrity-test
new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..3af9a91362
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/cloud-save-integrity-test
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+# Copyright (C) 2026-present pixelelated
+"""Synthetic corruption controls for cloud-save-integrity (#517); no personal input."""
+import argparse
+import copy
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import runpy
+import struct
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import zlib
+
+api = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('cloud-save-integrity')))
+verify, digest, structure = api['verify'], api['dropbox_hash'], api['structure']
+p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+p.add_argument('--rclone', type=Path, required=True, help='Independent local Dropbox hash oracle')
+a = p.parse_args()
+count = 0
+
+
+def check(name, value):
+    global count
+    if not value:
+        raise SystemExit('FAIL ' + name)
+    count += 1
+    print('PASS ' + name)
+
+
+def rejects(fn):
+    try:
+        value = fn()
+        return isinstance(value, dict) and value['summary']['errors'] > 0
+    except (ValueError, KeyError, OSError, zlib.error):
+        return True
+
+
+def chunk(tag, data):
+    return struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xffffffff)
+
+
+png = api['PNG'] + chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', 1, 1, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(b'\0\xff\0\0')) + chunk(b'IEND', b'')
+state = b'RASTATE\x01MEM ' + struct.pack('<I', 3) + b'abc' + b'\0' * 5 + b'END ' + b'\0' * 4
+compressed = zlib.compress(state)
+rzip = b'#RZIPv\x01#' + struct.pack('<IQI', 131072, len(state), len(compressed)) + compressed
+with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='pix-save-integrity-control-') as temp:
+    root = Path(temp)
+    (root/'payloads').mkdir()
+    payloads = [png, rzip, b'raw save bytes']
+    entries = [{'Path': n, 'Size': len(d), 'ID': str(i + 1), 'IsDir': False,
+                'ModTime': '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'Hashes': {'dropbox': digest(d)}}
+               for i, (n, d) in enumerate(zip(['screenshots/key.png', 'savestates/a.state', 'gba/a.srm'], payloads))]
+    # Sort exactly as the collector contract specifies.
+    pairs = sorted(zip(entries, payloads), key=lambda x: x[0]['Path'])
+    entries, payloads = map(list, zip(*pairs))
+    reads = [{'index': i, 'rc': 0, 'bytes': len(d)} for i, d in enumerate(payloads)]
+    def write(name, obj):
+        (root/name).write_text(json.dumps(obj))
+    def reset():
+        for name in ['before.json', 'after.json', 'ordered.json']:
+            write(name, entries)
+        write('reads.json', reads)
+        for i, data in enumerate(payloads):
+            (root/'payloads'/f'{i:04d}').write_bytes(data)
+    reset()
+    check('valid scoped packet including filename containing key', verify(root)['summary']['errors'] == 0)
+    for label, data in [('changed', b'X' + payloads[0][1:]), ('truncated', payloads[0][:-1])]:
+        (root/'payloads/0000').write_bytes(data)
+        check(label + ' payload rejected', rejects(lambda: verify(root)))
+        reset()
+    (root/'payloads/0000').unlink()
+    check('missing payload rejected', rejects(lambda: verify(root)))
+    reset()
+    for label, change in [
+        ('wrong hash', lambda x: x[0]['Hashes'].update(dropbox='0' * 64)),
+        ('missing hash', lambda x: x[0].update(Hashes={})),
+        ('duplicate path', lambda x: x.append(copy.deepcopy(x[0]))),
+        ('unsafe path', lambda x: x[0].update(Path='../escape')),
+        ('size bound', lambda x: x[0].update(Size=api['LIMIT']+1)),
+    ]:
+        changed = copy.deepcopy(entries);change(changed)
+        for name in ['before.json', 'after.json', 'ordered.json']: write(name, changed)
+        check(label + ' rejected', rejects(lambda: verify(root)))
+        reset()
+    changed=copy.deepcopy(entries);changed[0]['ModTime']='2026-02-01T00:00:00Z'
+    write('after.json',changed)
+    check('remote change rejected', rejects(lambda: verify(root)))
+    reset()
+    changed=copy.deepcopy(reads);changed[0]['rc']=1;write('reads.json',changed)
+    check('nonzero collector read rejected', rejects(lambda: verify(root)))
+    reset();write('reads.json',reads[:-1])
+    check('missing read receipt rejected', rejects(lambda: verify(root)))
+    reset()
+    # Provider can accurately hash already-corrupt data: structure must still fail.
+    i=next(i for i,e in enumerate(entries) if e['Path'].endswith('.png'))
+    bad=png[:-1]+bytes([png[-1]^1]);changed=copy.deepcopy(entries)
+    changed[i]['Hashes']['dropbox']=digest(bad)
+    for name in ['before.json','after.json','ordered.json']:write(name,changed)
+    (root/'payloads'/f'{i:04d}').write_bytes(bad)
+    r=verify(root)
+    check('valid provider hash does not hide corrupt PNG', r['files'][i].get('byte_integrity')=='ok' and r['summary']['errors']==1)
+    for name, data, path in [('PNG truncation',png[:-5],'x.png'),('RZIP truncation',rzip[:-1],'x.state'),
+                             ('RZIP declared length',rzip[:12]+struct.pack('<Q',len(state)+1)+rzip[20:],'x.state'),
+                             ('RZIP checksum',rzip[:-1]+bytes([rzip[-1]^1]),'x.state'),
+                             ('RASTATE truncated block',state[:-4],'x.state')]:
+        check(name+' rejected',rejects(lambda:structure(data,path)))
+    check('raw save semantics stay unverified','unverified' in structure(b'raw save','x.srm'))
+    # Four block-boundary cases plus empty input use a separately implemented oracle.
+    for size in [0, api['BLOCK']-1, api['BLOCK'], api['BLOCK']+1, 2*api['BLOCK']+17]:
+        data=(b'0123456789abcdef' * ((size+15)//16))[:size]
+        oracle=subprocess.run([str(a.rclone),'hashsum','Dropbox','-'],input=data,capture_output=True,timeout=15)
+        check('Dropbox oracle '+str(size),oracle.returncode==0 and oracle.stdout.decode().split()[0]==digest(data))
+print('PASS total='+str(count))
diff --git a/tools/host-maintenance/retention-report b/tools/host-maintenance/retention-report
new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..48b46ce295
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/host-maintenance/retention-report
@@ -0,0 +1,313 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Read-only build capacity and completed-QA disk retention report (#461).
+
+Inputs are an explicit plan, not deletion authority. This tool never removes
+files, changes permissions, stops processes or invokes privileged commands.
+Only superseded QA disks are eligible; build trees use fork-worktree separately.
+"""
+import argparse
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import stat
+import subprocess
+import tarfile
+import time
+
+
+def digest(path):
+    with Path(path).open('rb') as stream:
+        return hashlib.file_digest(stream, 'sha256').hexdigest()
+
+
+def identity(path):
+    s = Path(path).lstat()
+    return dict(device=s.st_dev, inode=s.st_ino, size=s.st_size,
+                mtime_ns=s.st_mtime_ns, allocated_bytes=s.st_blocks * 512,
+                uid=s.st_uid, links=s.st_nlink, mode=s.st_mode)
+
+
+def within(path, root):
+    return Path(path) == Path(root) or Path(root) in Path(path).parents
+
+
+def strings(value):
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        yield value
+    elif isinstance(value, list):
+        for child in value:
+            yield from strings(child)
+    elif isinstance(value, dict):
+        for key, child in value.items():
+            yield key
+            yield from strings(child)
+
+
+def source_fixtures(plan):
+    """Only exact archive members in protected source trees are nonruntime."""
+    accepted, errors, archives = {}, [], {}
+    for item in plan.get('source_fixtures', []):
+        try:
+            path = Path(item['path'])
+            if (not any(within(path, p) for p in plan['protected'])
+                    or any(str(path) == c['path'] for c in plan['candidates'])
+                    or identity(path) != item['identity'] or path.is_symlink()):
+                raise ValueError('fixture is changed, unprotected or a removal candidate')
+            archive = Path(item['archive'])
+            key = (str(archive), item['archive_sha256'])
+            if key not in archives:
+                if digest(archive) != item['archive_sha256']:
+                    raise ValueError('archive digest changed')
+                archives[key] = True
+            with tarfile.open(archive) as source:
+                member = source.getmember(item['member'])
+                if not member.isfile():
+                    raise ValueError('archive member is not a regular file')
+                stream = source.extractfile(member)
+                expected = hashlib.file_digest(stream, 'sha256').hexdigest()
+            if expected != item['sha256'] or digest(path) != expected:
+                raise ValueError('fixture differs from exact archive member')
+            accepted[str(path)] = item
+        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, tarfile.TarError) as error:
+            errors.append('source fixture ' + item.get('path', '?') + ': ' + str(error))
+    return accepted, errors
+
+
+def inventory(plan):
+    roots = [Path(p) for p in plan['scan_roots']]
+    if not roots or any(not p.is_absolute() or not p.is_dir() or p.is_symlink() for p in roots):
+        raise ValueError('scan roots must be explicit existing absolute directories')
+    if any(not any(within(p, r) for r in roots) for p in plan['reference_stores']):
+        raise ValueError('reference stores must be inside scanned roots')
+    fixtures, errors = source_fixtures(plan)
+    edges, disks, manifests = [], [], []
+    count = 0
+    tick = time.monotonic()
+    targets = {str(Path(c['path'])) for c in plan['candidates']}
+    if len(targets) != len(plan['candidates']):
+        raise ValueError('duplicate candidate paths')
+    for root in roots:
+        pending = [root]
+        while pending:
+            base = pending.pop()
+            count += 1
+            try:
+                with os.scandir(base) as entries:
+                    for entry in entries:
+                        try:
+                            if entry.is_symlink():
+                                target = str(Path(entry.path).resolve())
+                                if any(within(target, t) or within(t, target) for t in targets):
+                                    edges.append(dict(source=entry.path, target=target, kind='symlink'))
+                                continue
+                            if entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
+                                pending.append(entry.path)
+                                continue
+                            name = entry.name
+                            disk_name = name.endswith(('.qcow2', '.qcow', '.img', '.raw', '.vmdk', '.vdi', '.vhd', '.vhdx'))
+                            if not disk_name and not name.endswith('.json'):
+                                continue
+                            p = Path(entry.path)
+                            if not entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False):
+                                errors.append('unclassified special file: ' + str(p))
+                                continue
+                            if str(p) in fixtures:
+                                item = fixtures[str(p)]
+                                if identity(p) != item['identity'] or digest(p) != item['sha256']:
+                                    errors.append('source fixture changed during discovery: ' + str(p))
+                                continue
+                            if disk_name:
+                                with p.open('rb') as stream:
+                                    magic = stream.read(4)
+                                if magic == b'QFI\xfb' or name.endswith(('.qcow2', '.qcow', '.vmdk', '.vdi', '.vhd', '.vhdx')):
+                                    disks.append(p)
+                            if name.endswith('.json') and any(within(p, r) for r in plan['reference_stores']):
+                                manifests.append(p)
+                        except (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
+                            errors.append(str(error))
+            except OSError as error:
+                errors.append(str(error))
+            if time.monotonic() - tick > 10:
+                print(f'Inspected {count} directories; {len(disks)} disk paths', flush=True)
+                tick = time.monotonic()
+    disk_rows = []
+    for n, p in enumerate(disks):
+        try:
+            before = identity(p)
+            run = subprocess.run(['qemu-img', 'info', '--force-share', '--backing-chain',
+                                  '--output=json', str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
+            if run.returncode:
+                raise ValueError(str(p) + ': ' + run.stderr.strip())
+            chain = json.loads(run.stdout)
+            if identity(p) != before:
+                raise ValueError('disk changed during inspection: ' + str(p))
+            for row in chain:
+                if row.get('format') not in ['qcow2', 'raw']:
+                    raise ValueError('unclassified disk format: ' + str(p))
+                source = Path(row['filename'])
+                if not source.is_absolute():
+                    source = p.parent / source
+                backing = row.get('full-backing-filename') or row.get('backing-filename')
+                if backing:
+                    target = Path(backing)
+                    if not target.is_absolute():
+                        target = source.parent / target
+                    edges.append(dict(source=str(source.resolve()), target=str(target.resolve()), kind='qcow-backing'))
+            disk_rows.append(dict(path=str(p), identity=before, chain=chain))
+        except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
+            errors.append(str(e))
+        if n % 25 == 0:
+            print(f'Inspected {n + 1}/{len(disks)} backing chains', flush=True)
+    for p in manifests:
+        try:
+            if p.stat().st_size > 32 * 1024 * 1024:
+                raise ValueError('unclassified oversized store manifest: ' + str(p))
+            for value in strings(json.loads(p.read_text())):
+                if value in targets:
+                    edges.append(dict(source=str(p), target=value, kind='cross-store-json'))
+        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
+            errors.append(str(e))
+    active, process_errors = [], []
+    for entry in Path('/proc').glob('[0-9]*/cmdline'):
+        try:
+            argv = entry.read_bytes().split(b'\0')
+            if not argv[0]:
+                continue
+            pid = int(entry.parent.name)
+            if pid == os.getpid():
+                continue
+            if Path(os.fsdecode(argv[0])).name.startswith('qemu-system-'):
+                active.append(dict(pid=pid, kind='live-qemu', scope='all candidates held'))
+            for c in plan['candidates']:
+                if any(os.fsencode(c['path']) in a or os.fsencode(c['owner']) in a for a in argv):
+                    active.append(dict(pid=pid, kind='owner-argv', path=c['path']))
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            pass  # Process exited between discovery and read.
+        except OSError as e:
+            process_errors.append(str(e))
+    mounts = []
+    try:
+        ids = subprocess.check_output(['docker', 'ps', '-aq'], text=True, timeout=30).split()
+        for cid in ids:
+            data = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['docker', 'inspect', cid], text=True, timeout=30))[0]
+            for mount in data['Mounts']:
+                mounts.append(dict(container=cid, running=data['State']['Running'], source=mount['Source']))
+    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
+        errors.append('container inspection: ' + str(e))
+    return dict(directories=count, errors=errors + process_errors, disks=disk_rows,
+                source_fixtures=list(fixtures.values()),
+                references=edges, active=active, container_mounts=mounts,
+                scope='All directories under explicit roots; directory symlinks not followed. '
+                      'QCOW magic in img/raw and named virtual disks; JSON references in explicit stores. '
+                      'Actual process argv and all container mounts. No whole-host root FD census claimed.')
+
+
+def evaluate(candidate, plan, observed):
+    path = Path(candidate['path'])
+    reasons = []
+    if candidate.get('classification') != 'superseded-qa-disk':
+        reasons.append('unclassified candidate')
+    if not any(within(path, r) for r in plan['scan_roots']):
+        reasons.append('outside scanned roots')
+    if any(within(path, p) or within(p, path) for p in plan['protected']):
+        reasons.append('protected identity or ancestor')
+    if observed['errors']:
+        reasons.append('unreadable or unclassified dependency inventory')
+    if any(a.get('path') == str(path) or a['kind'] == 'live-qemu' for a in observed['active']):
+        reasons.append('active process')
+    for m in observed['container_mounts']:
+        if within(path, m['source']) or within(m['source'], path):
+            reasons.append('container reference: ' + m['container'])
+    for edge in observed['references']:
+        if within(edge['target'], path) or within(path, edge['target']):
+            reasons.append(edge['kind'] + ' reference: ' + edge['source'])
+    try:
+        actual = identity(path)
+        if actual != candidate['identity']:
+            reasons.append('identity changed')
+        if not stat.S_ISREG(actual['mode']) or actual['links'] != 1 or actual['uid'] != os.getuid():
+            reasons.append('not an exclusively owned regular file')
+        if not any(d['path'] == str(path) and d['chain'][0]['format'] == 'qcow2' for d in observed['disks']):
+            reasons.append('candidate not classified as QCOW2')
+        evidence = candidate['evidence']
+        if not evidence or not candidate.get('superseded_by'):
+            reasons.append('missing preservation or replacement evidence')
+        for item in evidence + [candidate['superseded_by']]:
+            if within(item['path'], candidate['owner']):
+                reasons.append('evidence not independently retained')
+            if digest(item['path']) != item['sha256']:
+                reasons.append('retained evidence hash mismatch: ' + item['path'])
+        replacement = json.loads(Path(candidate['superseded_by']['path']).read_text())
+        if replacement.get('result') != 'PASS':
+            reasons.append('replacement qualification not accepted')
+        cleanup = json.loads(Path(candidate['cleanup_receipt']).read_text())
+        lifecycle = json.loads(Path(candidate['owner_receipt']).read_text())
+        if (not cleanup.get('passed') or not lifecycle.get('pids_absent')
+                or set(lifecycle['channels']) != {'inner.rc', 'outer.rc', 'tool-wrapper.rc', 'build.rc'}
+                or len(set(lifecycle['channels'].values())) != 1):
+            reasons.append('missing completed owner/cleanup proof')
+        for pid in lifecycle['pids_absent']:
+            if Path('/proc', str(pid)).exists():
+                reasons.append('recorded owner PID currently exists: ' + str(pid))
+        # Bind the two authority-bearing receipts to the independently retained set.
+        for receipt in [candidate['cleanup_receipt'], candidate['owner_receipt']]:
+            if not any(e['sha256'] == digest(receipt) for e in evidence):
+                reasons.append('completion receipt not preserved independently')
+        sha = digest(path)
+        if identity(path) != actual:
+            reasons.append('candidate changed while hashing')
+    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
+        reasons.append('unreadable or malformed candidate evidence: ' + str(e))
+        sha = None
+    return dict(path=str(path), identity=candidate['identity'], sha256=sha,
+                eligible=not reasons, rejection_reasons=reasons)
+
+
+def report(plan):
+    observed = inventory(plan)
+    rows = [evaluate(c, plan, observed) for c in plan['candidates']]
+    free = os.statvfs(plan['volume'])
+    available = free.f_bavail * free.f_frsize
+    preserved = []
+    for p in plan['protected']:
+        preserved.append(dict(path=p, identity=identity(p)))
+    budgets = []
+    for budget in plan['builds']:
+        if not budget['evidence']:
+            raise ValueError('capacity estimate requires retained measurements')
+        for evidence in budget['evidence']:
+            if digest(evidence['path']) != evidence['sha256']:
+                raise ValueError('capacity evidence changed')
+        terms = budget['terms_bytes']
+        if not terms or any(type(v) is not int or v < 0 for v in terms.values()):
+            raise ValueError('invalid capacity terms')
+        need = sum(terms.values())
+        reclaim = sum(r['identity']['allocated_bytes'] for r in rows if r['eligible'])
+        budgets.append(dict(name=budget['name'], terms_bytes=terms, required_bytes=need,
+                            available_bytes=available, fits_now=available >= need,
+                            eligible_reclaim_bytes=reclaim,
+                            headroom_after_proposed_bytes=available + reclaim - need,
+                            basis=budget['basis']))
+    return dict(utc=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), schema=1, deletion_performed=False,
+                result='REPORT_COMPLETE', protected=preserved, inventory=observed,
+                candidates=rows, builds=budgets, preservation_additional_bytes=0,
+                limitations='Evidence is already independently retained. Available bytes exclude filesystem reserve. '
+                            'A report is not deletion authority; refresh identities, dependencies and active use before execution.')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('--plan', type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    plan = json.loads(args.plan.read_text())
+    result = report(plan)
+    result['plan_sha256'] = digest(args.plan)
+    result['tool_sha256'] = digest(__file__)
+    with args.output.open('x') as stream:
+        json.dump(result, stream, indent=2); stream.write('\n')
+    print(json.dumps(dict(result=result['result'], candidates=len(result['candidates']),
+                          eligible=sum(r['eligible'] for r in result['candidates']),
+                          errors=len(result['inventory']['errors']), builds=result['builds'])), flush=True)
diff --git a/tools/host-maintenance/retention-report.md b/tools/host-maintenance/retention-report.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..4e119d8b28
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/host-maintenance/retention-report.md
@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+# Read-only retention and capacity reports
+
+`retention-report` implements the first reporting portion of #461 and
+D-INFRA-018. Run it after required qualification and before the next build:
+
+```sh
+tools/watch-build -- python3 -I tools/host-maintenance/retention-report \
+  --plan /absolute/review/plan.json --output /absolute/review/report.json
+```
+
+The output must be new. The tool reads production storage and writes only the
+requested report. It has no deletion, permission-changing, process-stopping,
+swap or privileged mode. A successful command means the report was produced;
+inspect each candidate's `eligible` and `rejection_reasons`, inventory errors
+and each build's `fits_now`. A completed report can reject every removal.
+
+The initial scope is explicitly identified, superseded QA disks. Other object
+classes are rejected. Worktree removals still use `tools/fork-worktree` under
+their own reviewed scope. A report does not authorize any deletion, and cannot
+extend an earlier batch's approval.
+
+The JSON plan contains:
+
+- `scan_roots`: existing absolute project storage roots. No directory symlinks
+  are followed. Read failures remain visible and prevent removal proposals.
+- `reference_stores`: preservation stores inside those roots. Any exact
+  candidate path in their JSON files conservatively counts as a reference,
+  including unfamiliar schemas. Oversized or unreadable JSON is unresolved.
+- `protected`: current and fallback candidate/build roots, upgrade baselines,
+  sources, licensing inputs, shared cache and required evidence. Their identity
+  observations are retained. Protection includes descendants and ancestors.
+- `volume`: the filesystem whose available bytes must accommodate the build.
+  Availability uses `f_bavail`; filesystem reserve is excluded.
+- `candidates`: exact paths classified as `superseded-qa-disk`, each with its
+  expected `identity`, owner path, original lifecycle and cleanup receipts,
+  independent retained evidence paths and SHA256 values, and a hash-bound
+  `superseded_by` acceptance receipt whose result is `PASS`.
+- `builds`: one explicit forecast per scheduled stage, with integer
+  `terms_bytes`, a written `basis`, and hash-bound measurement `evidence`.
+  Include independent build/copy, artifacts, QA and operating allowances.
+  Distinguish measurements from future growth estimates. For sequential
+  stages, later forecasts include earlier outputs that remain on disk.
+- Optional `source_fixtures`: exact protected source files that resemble disk
+  images but are package test samples. Each names its identity, SHA256, source
+  archive path and SHA256, and exact regular archive member. The tool compares
+  the actual member bytes and rechecks the file during discovery. An altered,
+  unprotected or proposed-for-removal fixture is held. This is an explicit
+  per-file classification; no source directory or extension is skipped.
+
+`identity` contains device, inode, size, nanosecond modification time,
+allocated bytes, uid, hardlink count and mode, as emitted by the tool's
+`identity()` function. Every proposed file is hashed and its identity read
+again. Hardlinked, changed, nonregular or differently owned files are held.
+
+The retained evidence list should cover the complete independently preserved
+compact record: logs, source/input identities, reports, frames and failure
+evidence. Hashing a receipt alone does not establish that this set is complete;
+that selection remains part of the reviewed plan. The tool verifies all listed
+bytes and independently retained copies of both completion receipts. Existing
+preservation is assumed complete, so additional preservation cost is zero;
+perform and verify any additional preservation before forming this plan.
+
+Dependencies are read from actual QCOW backing chains, relevant symlinks,
+hardlink counts and JSON references across preservation stores. QCOW headers
+are recognized in `.img`/`.raw` files; explicitly named virtual disks are also
+inspected. Unknown formats and failed chain inspection prevent proposals.
+A disk that another disk references is held even when both are candidates.
+Directory-entry metadata avoids repeated stat calls while retaining traversal
+of every directory in the declared roots. The first production run identified
+64 small shared-mime-info 2.4 MIME samples; they are classified only against
+the override recipe's pinned archive and its exact four members (#490).
+
+Active-use checks inspect actual host process arguments, recorded owner PIDs,
+and all running/stopped container mounts. Any live QEMU holds all candidates.
+The report does not claim a root file-descriptor census or coverage of disks
+outside the declared project roots. Establish those scope boundaries before
+using it for a batch. The isolated controls do not require root:
+
+```sh
+python3 -I tools/host-maintenance/test-retention-report
+```
+
+They create actual temporary QCOW files, backing chains, cross-store links,
+an owned process, unreadable paths and altered evidence. They assert both
+eligible independent files and refusals, and check that no disk is removed.
+
+Before any later authorized action, refresh the report, retained evidence,
+exact file identities and active-use observations. Available space and process
+state are snapshots, not reservations. Preserve the approved plan digest and
+verify actual recovery and retained inputs after the separate guarded action.

new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..f7788a9e1f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/host-maintenance/test-retention-report
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exercise retention refusals with real temporary QCOW files and processes."""
+import copy
+import importlib.machinery
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import tarfile
+import tempfile
+
+source = Path(__file__).with_name('retention-report')
+loader = importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader('retention', str(source))
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_loader(loader.name, loader)
+mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+loader.exec_module(mod)
+results = []
+with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='pixelelated-retention-controls-') as tmp:
+    root = Path(tmp); owner = root/'owner'; kept = root/'kept'; store = root/'store'
+    for p in [owner, kept, store]: p.mkdir()
+    disk = owner/'guest.qcow2'
+    subprocess.run(['qemu-img','create','-f','qcow2',str(disk),'16M'], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
+    ended = subprocess.Popen(['true']); ended.wait()
+    lifecycle = dict(pids_absent=[ended.pid], channels={n:'0' for n in ['inner.rc','outer.rc','tool-wrapper.rc','build.rc']})
+    for name, data in [('owner.json',lifecycle),('cleanup.json',{'passed':True})]:
+        text=json.dumps(data);(owner/name).write_text(text);(kept/name).write_text(text)
+    (kept/'replacement.json').write_text(json.dumps({'result':'PASS'}))
+    evidence=[dict(path=str(p),sha256=mod.digest(p)) for p in kept.iterdir()]
+    candidate=dict(path=str(disk),owner=str(owner),classification='superseded-qa-disk',
+                   identity=mod.identity(disk), evidence=evidence,
+                   cleanup_receipt=str(owner/'cleanup.json'),owner_receipt=str(owner/'owner.json'),
+                   superseded_by=dict(path=str(kept/'replacement.json'),sha256=mod.digest(kept/'replacement.json')))
+    plan=dict(scan_roots=[str(root)],reference_stores=[str(store)],protected=[str(kept)],candidates=[candidate],
+              volume=str(root),builds=[dict(name='fixture',terms_bytes={'required':1},
+                                          evidence=[candidate['superseded_by']],basis='fixture')])
+    def check(name, expected, changed=None):
+        current=changed or plan
+        result=mod.report(current);row=result['candidates'][0]
+        assert row['eligible']==expected,(name,row)
+        assert disk.exists() and result['deletion_performed'] is False
+        results.append(dict(name=name,passed=True,eligible=row['eligible'],reasons=row['rejection_reasons']))
+    check('eligible independent completed QA disk',True)
+    other=copy.deepcopy(plan);other['candidates'][0]['classification']='unknown'
+    check('unclassified candidate',False,other)
+    disk.chmod(0)
+    try: check('actual unreadable disk',False)
+    finally: disk.chmod(0o644)
+    # Permission changes altered identity; restore the expected observation.
+    candidate['identity']=mod.identity(disk)
+    hidden=root/'unreadable';hidden.mkdir();hidden.chmod(0)
+    try: check('unreadable dependency tree',False)
+    finally: hidden.chmod(0o755);hidden.rmdir()
+    child=store/'dependent.qcow2'
+    subprocess.run(['qemu-img','create','-f','qcow2','-F','qcow2','-b',str(disk),str(child)],check=True,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
+    check('actual cross-store QCOW backing dependency',False);child.unlink()
+    link=store/'disk-link';link.symlink_to(disk)
+    check('cross-store symlink',False);link.unlink()
+    manifest=store/'objects.json';manifest.write_text(json.dumps({'object':str(disk)}))
+    check('cross-store JSON reference',False);manifest.unlink()
+    hard=store/'hardlink';os.link(disk,hard)
+    check('hardlinked candidate',False);hard.unlink()
+    sleeper=subprocess.Popen(['python3','-c','import time;time.sleep(60)',str(disk)])
+    try: check('actual live owner process',False)
+    finally: sleeper.terminate();sleeper.wait()
+    other=copy.deepcopy(plan);other['protected'].append(str(owner))
+    check('protected tree',False,other)
+    other=copy.deepcopy(plan);other['candidates'][0]['identity']['inode']+=1
+    check('changed identity',False,other)
+    receipt=kept/'cleanup.json';before=receipt.read_bytes();receipt.write_text('{}')
+    try: check('tampered retained evidence',False)
+    finally: receipt.write_bytes(before)
+    check('eligible after temporary controls removed',True)
+    # A truncated real QCOW header forces an inspection error; arbitrary bytes
+    # can legitimately be detected as a raw image by qemu-img.
+    sample=kept/'source-sample.qcow2';sample.write_bytes(disk.read_bytes()[:32])
+    archive=kept/'source.tar.gz'
+    with tarfile.open(archive,'w:gz') as source_archive:
+        source_archive.add(sample,arcname='tests/mime-detection/source-sample.qcow2')
+    item=dict(path=str(sample),identity=mod.identity(sample),sha256=mod.digest(sample),
+              archive=str(archive),archive_sha256=mod.digest(archive),
+              member='tests/mime-detection/source-sample.qcow2')
+    check('unclassified source disk is still held',False)
+    plan['source_fixtures']=[item]
+    check('exact protected archive fixture classified',True)
+    before=sample.read_bytes();sample.write_bytes(before+b'changed')
+    try: check('changed source fixture rejected',False)
+    finally: sample.write_bytes(before);item['identity']=mod.identity(sample)
+    before=archive.read_bytes();archive.write_bytes(before+b'changed')
+    try: check('changed source archive rejected',False)
+    finally: archive.write_bytes(before)
+    other=copy.deepcopy(plan);other['protected']=[]
+    check('unprotected fixture rejected',False,other)
+    check('exact fixture remains valid after controls',True)
+print(json.dumps(dict(result='PASS',controls=results,tool_sha256=mod.digest(source)),indent=2))
