1: #!/bin/bash
2: # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
3: # Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
4: 
5: # cloud_setup - configure the rclone cloud remote.
6: #
7: # Walks the player through rclone's own interactive configuration over SSH:
8: # it is the only flow that handles every provider completely (OAuth sign-in,
9: # folder choices, provider-specific questions). This screen supplies the
10: # connection details in big text, waits, then verifies the remote actually
11: # works before declaring success.
12: #
13: # The native UI wizard drives the same flow through three flags:
14: #   --info       key=value connection facts (IP, SSH command, override
15: #                state, password, sshd state, OAuth-port state,
16: #                configured remotes)
17: #   --free-auth-port  clear a stale sign-in webserver holding rclone's
18: #                OAuth port 53682
19: #   --set-content-remote <path>  change the content root alone (CONTENT_REMOTE;
20: #                the chooser's, fork #352); nothing moves
21: #   --set-saves-remote <path>  change the cloud folder (SAVES_REMOTE) the sync
22: #                (--set-syncpath is accepted as the older spelling)
23: #                tools use, preserving settings and content choices; refuses a
24: #                path the remote cannot use
25: #   --accept-saves-root  the saves folder is on a different card than the last
26: #                sync and that is intended (cloud_saves_root)
27: #   --check-syncpath [path]  validate a cloud folder against the remote's
28: #                shape without changing anything (default: the current one)
29: #   --folder-state  read configured folder availability; never change pointers
30: #   --validation-context  local config identity and exact selected category paths
31: #   --validate-folders <categories csv> <run-id>  bounded read-only JSON findings
32: #   --seed-folders <categories csv>  create only explicitly selected folders
33: #   --set-settings-remote <path>  change only the settings archive location
34: #   --content-location  report where this device's ROMs/BIOS actually are in
35: #                the selected cloud folder (key=value; STATE=ok|empty;
36: #                unreadable, exit 1, when its value is not in a form the
37: #                sync reads)
38: #   --use-content-root  point content back at the remote root, moving nothing
39: #   --connected  exit 0 when an inbound SSH session is established, so the
40: #                connect step can be verified rather than taken on faith
41: #   --check [remote]  verify a remote (default: first); exit 0 working,
42: #                1 missing, 2 configured but unreachable
43: 
44: . /etc/profile
45: 
46: SCRIPT_NAME=$(basename "$0")
47: LOG_FILE="/var/log/cloud_sync.log"
48: SYNC_CONF="/storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf"
49: 
50: log_message() {
51:     local message="$1"
52:     local timestamp=$(date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
53:     echo "[${timestamp}] [INFO] [${SCRIPT_NAME}] ${message}" >> ${LOG_FILE}
54: }
55: 
56: # The config is shell: every cloud script sources it. So a value is written
57: # as text between double quotes, never through a sed replacement -- where &
58: # is the matched line and | ends the expression, so "/R&D/Saves" became
59: # garbage and "/a|b" failed the write while OK was printed (audit #307
60: # PL-051) -- and a value that would mean something to a shell between double
61: # quotes (" $ ` \) is refused where it is typed (syncpath_problem).
62: #
63: # conf_set KEY VALUE [KEY VALUE ...] writes every pair in one pass, each
64: # KEY= line replaced (every one, as the sed was) or appended, to a file
65: # beside the config that is renamed over it: all the keys or none, and the
66: # previous config intact when the write fails. The values reach awk through
67: # the environment, so nothing in them is interpreted. Returns non-zero when
68: # the config could not be written.
69: conf_set() {
70:     local tmp="${SYNC_CONF}.tmp.$$" src="${SYNC_CONF}" n=0 i
71:     local -a pairs=() want=()
72:     # Something at the config's path that is not a file is not a config this
73:     # can write: read as "absent", `mv -f` then put the new file INSIDE a
74:     # directory there and succeeded (audit of stream C, G-C-04).
75:     if [ -e "${SYNC_CONF}" ] && [ ! -f "${SYNC_CONF}" ]; then
76:         return 1
77:     fi
78:     [ -f "${src}" ] || src=/dev/null
79:     while [ $# -ge 2 ]; do
80:         n=$((n + 1)); pairs+=("CONF_K${n}=$1" "CONF_V${n}=$2")
81:         want+=("$1=\"$2\""); shift 2
82:     done
83:     # Braced, and silenced as a whole: a redirection that fails opening the
84:     # temp file happens before a `2>/dev/null` written after it, and the
85:     # shell printed its own diagnostic -- a line number and the temp file's
86:     # path -- ahead of the caller's sentence (G-C-07).
87:     if { env "${pairs[@]}" CONF_N="${n}" awk '
88:         BEGIN {
89:             n = ENVIRON["CONF_N"] + 0
90:             for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
91:                 k[i] = ENVIRON["CONF_K" i]
92:                 line[i] = k[i] "=\"" ENVIRON["CONF_V" i] "\""
93:             }
94:         }
95:         {
96:             for (i = 1; i <= n; i++)
97:                 if (index($0, k[i] "=") == 1) { print line[i]; seen[i] = 1; next }
98:             print
99:         }
100:         END { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!seen[i]) print line[i] }
101:     ' "${src}" > "${tmp}" && mv -f "${tmp}" "${SYNC_CONF}"; } 2>/dev/null; then
102:         # Written is what the file says, not what mv returned: a regular
103:         # file at the path, holding every line asked for.
104:         [ -f "${SYNC_CONF}" ] || return 1
105:         for i in "${want[@]}"; do
106:             grep -qFx -- "${i}" "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null || return 1
107:         done
108:         return 0
109:     fi
110:     rm -f "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null
111:     return 1
112: }
113: 
114: # One value from the config, read as text -- never by sourcing or eval, since
115: # a value an earlier build wrote with $( ) in it would run (PL-051) -- and as
116: # the scripts that run with it read it, so this and they never disagree
117: # about a player's folder:
118: #   - Of two assignments of a key, the FIRST: every saves run the interface
119: #     starts is --yes, which runs cloud_sync_cleanup_duplicates.sh, which
120: #     keeps the first and is what the file becomes; the content scripts'
121: #     conf_get reads the first too. This read the last, as `source` alone
122: #     would, so with a key written twice the hub's line and
123: #     --content-location named a folder the scripts stopped using at their
124: #     next run (the audit of the fix round, PL-021; the first cut's G-C-03
125: #     gpt and G-C-06 claude had moved it from first to last).
126: #   - The value double quoted, single quoted or a bare word, then nothing,
127: #     or blanks and a # comment: the forms conf_valid lets a file through
128: #     with. Anything else is exit 2 and nothing printed -- /Mine/'My Saves',
129: #     text after a closing quote, a double-quoted value with $, ` or \ in it
130: #     (what a shell would expand there) -- as the content scripts' conf_get
131: #     answers it and as conf_valid refuses the whole file. The first cut
132: #     read /Mine/'My as the folder, one no script would ever use (the audit
133: #     of the fix round, gpt G2-C-01).
134: # Nothing when the key is absent. The same awk as cloud_content_backup's and
135: # cloud_content_restore's conf_get, on the file SYNC_CONF names.
136: conf_get() { # <KEY> (the content scripts' reader, mirrored so every reader agrees, D-CLOUD-149): its value, quotes off; nothing when absent; exit 2 when unreadable, and why on stdout
137:     [ -f ${SYNC_CONF} ] || return 0
138:     awk -v k="$1" '
139:         { t = $0; gsub(/\t/, "", t); if (t ~ /[[:cntrl:]]/ && !cntrl) cntrl = NR }
140:         index($0, k "=") != 1 && !other \
141:             && $0 ~ ("^[ \t]*((export|declare|typeset|readonly|local)([ \t]+-[A-Za-z]+)*[ \t]+)?" k "[ \t]*[+]?=") { other = NR }
142:         index($0, k "=") == 1 {
143:             s = substr($0, length(k) + 2); v = ""; r = ""; ok = 1; why = ""
144:             c = substr(s, 1, 1)
145:             if (c == "\"") {
146:                 # Inside double quotes bash reads \" \\ \$ and \` as the one
147:                 # character each (PL-015), and so does this; an unescaped $
148:                 # or backtick is an expansion this reader does not make, and
149:                 # any other backslash is refused as conf_valid refuses it.
150:                 n = length(s); i = 2; closed = 0
151:                 while (i <= n) {
152:                     d = substr(s, i, 1)
153:                     if (d == "\"") { closed = 1; break }
154:                     if (d == "\\") {
155:                         e = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
156:                         if (e == "\"" || e == "\\" || e == "$" || e == "`") { v = v e; i += 2; continue }
157:                         ok = 0
158:                         why = (e == "") ? "a value continued onto the next line, which this reader does not follow" \
159:                                         : "a backslash inside double quotes that is not one of the escapes bash reads there"
160:                         break
161:                     }
162:                     if (d == "$" || d == "`") { ok = 0; why = "a $ or a backtick inside double quotes"; break }
163:                     v = v d; i++
164:                 }
165:                 if (ok && !closed) { ok = 0; why = "a double-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
166:                 if (ok) r = substr(s, i + 1)
167:             } else if (c == "'"'"'") {
168:                 j = index(substr(s, 2), c)
169:                 if (j) { v = substr(s, 2, j - 1); r = substr(s, j + 2) } else { ok = 0; why = "a single-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
170:             } else {
171:                 match(s, /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-]*/); v = substr(s, 1, RLENGTH); r = substr(s, RLENGTH + 1)
172:             }
173:             if (ok && r !~ /^([ \t]+(#.*)?)?$/) { ok = 0; why = "something after the value that is not a # comment" }
174:             if (!found) { found = 1; first = v; firstok = ok; firstwhy = "line " NR ": " why }
175:         }
176:         END {
177:             if (cntrl) { print "line " cntrl ": a control character other than a tab"; exit 2 }
178:             if (other) { print "line " other ": " k " set in a form this reader does not read"; exit 2 }
179:             if (found && !firstok) { print firstwhy; exit 2 }
180:             if (found) print first
181:         }
182:     ' ${SYNC_CONF}
183: }
184: 
185: # Wait for any confirm/cancel input: controller (evtest) or keyboard.
186: wait_for_button() {
187:     local input_device=""
188:     for dev in /dev/input/event*; do
189:         if [ -c "$dev" ]; then
190:             local supports=$(udevadm info "$dev" 2>/dev/null | awk '/ID_INPUT_JOYSTICK=1/ {print "joystick"}')
191:             if [ "$supports" = "joystick" ]; then
192:                 input_device="$dev"
193:                 break
194:             fi
195:         fi
196:     done
197:     if [ -n "$input_device" ]; then
198:         evtest "$input_device" 2>/dev/null | grep -m 1 -E "BTN_(SOUTH|EAST|A|B|START).*value 1" >/dev/null
199:     else
200:         read -sn1 2>/dev/null
201:     fi
202: }
203: 
204: # Connection facts, shared by the console flow and the native UI.
205: # resolve_connection sets SSH_CMD, SHOW_QR, OVERRIDE_ACTIVE and IP_ADDR
206: # (empty when offline).
207: resolve_connection() {
208:     OVERRIDE_ACTIVE=0
209:     IP_ADDR=$(ip route get 1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i=="src") {print $(i+1); exit}}')
210:     # The -L tunnel lets the provider sign-in page (which rclone serves on
211:     # the handheld at localhost:53682) open in the computer's own browser,
212:     # so the full 'auto config' flow works over SSH - see
213:     # rclone.org/remote_setup.
214:     SSH_CMD="ssh -L 53682:localhost:53682 root@${IP_ADDR}"
215:     SHOW_QR=1
216:     # Optional connection override: when the device is reached through a
217:     # gateway that remaps its address (development setups, tunnels,
218:     # proxies), the command in this file is shown instead of the direct one.
219:     OVERRIDE_FILE="/storage/.config/cloud_setup_ssh"
220:     if [ -s "${OVERRIDE_FILE}" ]; then
221:         SSH_CMD=$(head -n1 "${OVERRIDE_FILE}")
222:         SHOW_QR=0
223:         OVERRIDE_ACTIVE=1
224:         log_message "Using connection override: ${SSH_CMD}"
225:     fi
226: }
227: 
228: # True when at least one inbound SSH session is established (a peer is
229: # connected to local port 22). Reads /proc/net/tcp* directly so it works
230: # without ss/netstat; port 22 is 0016 hex, state 01 is ESTABLISHED.
231: ssh_session_established() {
232:     local f
233:     for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do
234:         [ -r "$f" ] || continue
235:         if awk 'NR>1 { n=split($2,a,":"); if (a[n]=="0016" && $4=="01") found=1 } END { exit found?0:1 }' "$f"; then
236:             return 0
237:         fi
238:     done
239:     return 1
240: }
241: 
242: # True when something on the device already listens on rclone's OAuth
243: # port 53682 (hex D1B2, state 0A is LISTEN) - a stale sign-in webserver
244: # from an interrupted `rclone config` would make the next auto-config
245: # attempt fail with "bind: address already in use".
246: auth_port_busy() {
247:     local f
248:     for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do
249:         [ -r "$f" ] || continue
250:         if awk 'NR>1 { n=split($2,a,":"); if (a[n]=="D1B2" && $4=="0A") found=1 } END { exit found?0:1 }' "$f"; then
251:             return 0
252:         fi
253:     done
254:     return 1
255: }
256: 
257: # Does this cloud folder work on this remote?
258: #
259: # Dropbox, Google Drive and OneDrive are path-based: "/GAMES" is a folder and
260: # any name will do. S3, B2 and friends are bucket-based - the first path
261: # component IS the bucket, and bucket names have rules the shipped default
262: # breaks (uppercase is illegal), so a sync fails with InvalidBucketName and
263: # nothing in that message points back at this setting.
264: #
265: # rclone reports the distinction itself, so no provider list is hardcoded.
266: # Returns 0 when the path will work; prints a reason and returns 1 when not.
267: # Listings that decide something get a bound (as the sync scripts' do) -- the
268: # folder probe below and the parent walk alike; `backend features` asks
269: # rclone about itself and makes no round trip: a cloud that never answers is
270: # a refusal in 30 s, not a wizard that hangs. Until #151 PL-15 the probe was
271: # the one unbounded listing here, and this comment covered only the walk.
272: readonly -a RCLONE_LIST_OPTS=(--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 3 --retries 1)
273: # Is this remote path missing, rather than unreadable? rclone answers "not
274: # found" (exit 3) when the server's reply is the one it maps to that, and a
275: # plain error (exit 1) when the words differ: an FTP server that answers a
276: # missing folder with 501 "No such directory." where the standard reply is
277: # 550 makes every "is it there yet?" branch read as "the cloud is broken"
278: # (#142, from the #133 matrix). The parent settles it, whatever the words:
279: # walk up until a level lists. A level that lists and lacks the next name is
280: # a path not created yet (0); one that lists and holds it means the failure
281: # was something else (1); a remote whose root will not list is broken (1).
282: # On a bucket an absent prefix lists as empty, which is the same answer
283: # (D-CLOUD-120). Called only after a listing has already failed with a code
284: # other than 3, so the everyday path costs nothing extra.
285: absent_not_broken() {
286:     local path="${1%/}" remote rel name parent listing
287:     remote="${path%%:*}:"; rel="${path#*:}"
288:     while [ -n "${rel}" ]; do
289:         name="${rel##*/}"
290:         case "${rel}" in */*) parent="${rel%/*}/" ;; *) parent="" ;; esac
291:         if listing=$(rclone lsf --dirs-only "${remote}${parent}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
292:             printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | grep -qFx -- "${name}/" && return 1
293:             return 0
294:         fi
295:         [ -n "${parent}" ] || return 1
296:         rel="${parent%/}"
297:     done
298:     return 1
299: }
300: 
301: # Configuration, availability and the current format are read separately
302: # from linking an rclone remote. Existing paths are never adopted or rewritten
303: # from another device's folders; only explicit setters change these values.
304: folder_path() {
305:     local part out="" lead=""; local -a parts=()
306:     case "$1" in /*) lead=/ ;; esac
307:     IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "$1"
308:     for part in "${parts[@]}"; do
309:         case "${part}" in ""|.) ;; ..) return 2 ;; *) out="${out:+${out}/}${part}" ;; esac
310:     done
311:     # A nonempty relative dot-only path names the remote root. It must never
312:     # collapse into a missing setting and silently select a fresh default.
313:     [ -z "$1" ] || [ -n "${lead}${out}" ] || return 2
314:     printf '%s%s' "${lead}" "${out}"
315: }
316: folder_values() {
317:     local value field
318:     if [ -e "${SYNC_CONF}" ] && [ ! -f "${SYNC_CONF}" ]; then
319:         echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"
320:         return 2
321:     fi
322:     for field in SAVES_REMOTE SETTINGS_REMOTE CONTENT_REMOTE; do
323:         value=$(conf_get "${field}") || { echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"; return 2; }
324:         value=$(folder_path "${value}") || { echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"; return 2; }
325:         case "${field}" in
326:             SAVES_REMOTE) SAVES="${value:-/pixelelated/Saves}" ;;
327:             SETTINGS_REMOTE) BACKUPS="${value:-/pixelelated/Backups}" ;;
328:             CONTENT_REMOTE)
329:                 # Explicit empty still means the cloud root; an absent setting
330:                 # alone receives the fresh-install default.
331:                 CONTENT="${value}"
332:                 grep -q '^CONTENT_REMOTE=' "${SYNC_CONF}" || CONTENT=/pixelelated/Content ;;
333:         esac
334:     done
335: }
336: folder_listing() { # <remote path> [lsf flags]; missing is distinct from unreadable
337:     local path="$1" rc; shift
338:     FOLDER_LISTING=$(rclone lsf "$@" "${path}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
339:     [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ] || return 0
340:     # A failed listing may already have printed entries. Those bytes cannot
341:     # establish presence or absence, even for a not-found return code.
342:     if [ -n "${FOLDER_LISTING}" ]; then
343:         echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
344:         return "${rc}"
345:     fi
346:     if [ "${rc}" -eq 3 ] || [ "${rc}" -eq 4 ] || absent_not_broken "${path}"; then
347:         FOLDER_LISTING=""
348:         return 0
349:     fi
350:     echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
351:     return "${rc}"
352: }
353: folder_exists() { # return 0 present, 1 absent, or >1 unreadable
354:     local path="$1" remote relative parent name rc
355:     # An absolute remote root and its relative home are different on SFTP.
356:     case "${path#*:}" in /) ;; *) path="${path%/}" ;; esac
357:     folder_listing "${path}"; rc=$?
358:     [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || return 5
359:     [ -z "${FOLDER_LISTING}" ] || return 0
360:     # A successfully listed remote root exists even when it is empty.
361:     case "${path#*:}" in ""|/) return 0 ;; esac
362:     remote="${path%%:*}:"; relative="${path#*:}"
363:     name="${relative##*/}"
364:     [ -n "${name}" ] || return 1
365:     # A relative one-component name belongs to remote:, while /Name belongs
366:     # to remote:/. Preserve that distinction for SFTP and similar providers.
367:     case "${relative}" in */*) parent="${relative%/*}/" ;; *) parent="" ;; esac
368:     folder_listing "${remote}${parent}" --dirs-only; rc=$?
369:     [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || return 5
370:     printf '%s\n' "${FOLDER_LISTING}" | grep -qxF -- "${name}/"
371: }
372: folder_current_namespace() {
373:     local identity="${SAVES#/}" features folding
374:     [ "${identity}" = pixelelated/Saves ] && return 0
375:     [ "${identity,,}" = pixelelated/saves ] || return 1
376:     # Case variants are the default only on a folding provider. Read the
377:     # selected parent in its own spelling; SFTP leading slashes still matter.
378:     features=$(rclone backend features "${REMOTE}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || features=""
379:     folding=$(printf '%s' "${features}" | jq -r 'if .Features.CaseInsensitive == true then "true" elif .Features.CaseInsensitive == false then "false" else "unknown" end' 2>/dev/null)
380:     case "${folding}" in
381:         true) return 0 ;;
382:         false) return 1 ;;
383:         *)
384:             echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
385:             return 5 ;;
386:     esac
387: }
388: folder_marker_read() {
389:     FOLDER_VERSION=0
390:     # Custom/legacy paths are independent choices, not a renamed layout.
391:     folder_current_namespace; local scope=$?
392:     case "${scope}" in 0) ;; 1) return 0 ;; *) return "${scope}" ;; esac
393:     local tmp rc version
394:     tmp=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud_folder_marker.XXXXXX) || return 5
395:     rclone cat "${REMOTE}${SAVES%/*}/.layout" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" > "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
396:     if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
397:         rm -f "${tmp}"
398:         folder_listing "${REMOTE}${SAVES%/*}/" --files-only || return $?
399:         if printf '%s\n' "${FOLDER_LISTING}" | grep -qxF '.layout'; then
400:             echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
401:             return "${rc}"
402:         fi
403:         return 0
404:     fi
405:     for version in 1 2; do
406:         if printf 'layout=%s\n' "${version}" | cmp -s - "${tmp}"; then
407:             FOLDER_VERSION="${version}"
408:             rm -f "${tmp}"
409:             return 0
410:         fi
411:     done
412:     rm -f "${tmp}"
413:     echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
414:     echo "This cloud folder uses a layout this version can't read. Check for a newer system version before trying again."
415:     return 4
416: }
417: folder_marker_write() {
418:     folder_current_namespace; local scope=$?
419:     case "${scope}" in 0) ;; 1) return 0 ;; *) return "${scope}" ;; esac
420:     folder_marker_read || return $?
421:     printf 'layout=2\n' | rclone rcat "${REMOTE}${SAVES%/*}/.layout" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || return 5
422:     folder_marker_read || return $?
423:     [ "${FOLDER_VERSION}" = 2 ] || return 5
424: }
425: 
426: # Callers pass the first remote; an empty one stops after the string checks,
427: # which hold with no remote configured at all.
428: syncpath_problem() {
429:     local path="$1" remote="$2" bucket probe
430:     path="${path%/}"
431:     case "${path}" in .|..|./*|../*) echo "That folder name can't be used."; return 1 ;; esac
432: 
433:     if [ -z "${path}" ] || [ "${path}" = "/" ]; then
434:         echo "Your cloud folder can't be empty."
435:         return 1
436:     fi
437:     # The config is shell, sourced by every cloud script: the characters a
438:     # shell reads inside double quotes, and control characters, are refused
439:     # where the folder is typed (audit #307 PL-051, conf_set).
440:     case "${path}" in
441:         *[\"\$\`\\]*|*[[:cntrl:]]*)
442:             echo "Your cloud folder's name can't contain \", \$, \`, or \\."
443:             return 1
444:             ;;
445:     esac
446:     # Every part of the path is a folder's name, and the checks below read
447:     # the text. A part that is empty (//), . or .. names no folder of its
448:     # own: /Mine/Backups/. is /Mine/Backups on a cloud that resolves it,
449:     # while its siblings -- <parent>/Backups and <parent>/Content, made from
450:     # the text by dirname -- came out as /Mine/Backups/Backups and
451:     # /Mine/Backups/Content, inside it: the nesting the sibling check below
452:     # exists to stop, walked past (the audit of the fix round, PL-009; gpt
453:     # G2-C-04). Refused where it is typed, before any other check reads the
454:     # text, with the folder the path would have meant.
455:     case "${path}/" in
456:         *//*|*/./*|*/../*)
457:             local part canon="" try
458:             local -a parts=()
459:             IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "${path#/}"
460:             for part in "${parts[@]}"; do
461:                 case "${part}" in
462:                     ""|.) ;;
463:                     ..) canon="${canon%/*}" ;;
464:                     *) canon="${canon}/${part}" ;;
465:                 esac
466:             done
467:             if [ -z "${canon}" ]; then
468:                 echo "Your cloud folder can't be empty."
469:                 return 1
470:             fi
471:             try="${canon}"
472:             case "${path}" in /*) ;; *) try="${try#/}" ;; esac
473:             echo "Your cloud folder can't have an empty part, or a part called . or .., in its path."
474:             echo "Try ${try}."
475:             return 1
476:             ;;
477:     esac
478:     [ -n "${remote}" ] || return 0
479: 
480:     # No provider rules are encoded here on purpose. rclone does not validate
481:     # bucket names itself - it hands them to the provider and relays the
482:     # rejection - so the rules live with the provider, differ between them,
483:     # and would go stale in this script. The problem was never missing
484:     # validation; it was validation arriving at sync time, in a log, as
485:     # "InvalidBucketName" with nothing tying it to the folder that caused it.
486:     #
487:     # So: ask the provider now, and attach the answer to the setting.
488:     #
489:     # Only what rclone says went wrong, never its listing. This used to read
490:     # stdout as well, so a folder that already existed and held anything --
491:     # a saves folder with savestates/ in it, which is every folder somebody
492:     # would type on a second device -- was refused as "your provider would
493:     # not accept this folder", with the folder's own contents quoted as the
494:     # reason (found by the A3 fixture on the VM pair, 2026-09-06).
495:     probe=$(rclone lsd "${remote}${path}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" --log-level ERROR 2>&1 >/dev/null | head -2)
496:     case "${probe}" in
497:         # A folder that does not exist yet is fine - it gets created on use.
498:         *"not found"*|*NoSuchBucket*|"") return 0 ;;
499:     esac
500:     # The same folder, on a server whose "missing" rclone relays as a plain
501:     # error rather than "not found" (#142). On a path-based cloud a folder
502:     # its parent lacks is a folder not created yet, whatever the words. On
503:     # a bucket the first component is a bucket name the provider judges,
504:     # and the provider's own answer stands -- the parent rule would read
505:     # InvalidBucketName as "not there yet" and store the name it rejected.
506:     #
507:     # Which kind this remote is, rclone says in JSON, and the answer has to
508:     # be one of the two before anything rests on it. A `backend features`
509:     # that fails or prints neither is "unknown", and unknown takes the
510:     # provider's refusal at face value: the parent walk runs only on a
511:     # remote known to be path-based. Until #151 PL-14 a failed call read as
512:     # "not bucket-based" -- a grep over empty output -- and the walk ran,
513:     # so the one guard against storing a rejected bucket name fell open
514:     # exactly when rclone could not be asked.
515:     local features bucket_based=unknown
516:     if features=$(rclone backend features "${remote}" 2>/dev/null); then
517:         case "${features}" in
518:             *'"BucketBased": true'*)  bucket_based=yes ;;
519:             *'"BucketBased": false'*) bucket_based=no ;;
520:         esac
521:     fi
522:     if [ "${bucket_based}" = no ] && absent_not_broken "${remote}${path}"; then
523:         return 0
524:     fi
525: 
526:     # Something is wrong. If the remote is bucket-based, name the reason the
527:     # message will not: the first path component is a bucket, not a folder.
528:     if [ "${bucket_based}" = yes ]; then
529:         bucket="${path#/}"; bucket="${bucket%%/*}"
530:         echo "Your provider wouldn't accept \"${bucket}\"."
531:         echo
532:         echo "This provider keeps things in buckets, so the first part of the"
533:         echo "folder is a bucket name, not a folder - and bucket names have"
534:         echo "rules that folders do not. They are also shared with everyone"
535:         echo "else using the provider, not private to your account."
536:         echo
537:         echo "  ${probe}"
538:         echo
539:         echo "Try something like /pixelelated-saves-yourname/Saves instead."
540:     else
541:         echo "Your provider wouldn't accept this folder:"
542:         echo
543:         echo "  ${probe}"
544:     fi
545:     return 1
546: }
547: 
548: validation_context() {
549:     folder_values >/dev/null || return 2
550:     local remotes config_file config_id
551:     remotes=$(timeout 3 rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null) || return 2
552:     REMOTE=$(printf '%s\n' "${remotes}" | head -1)
553:     [ -n "${REMOTE}" ] || return 2
554:     config_file=$(timeout 3 rclone config file 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
555:     [ -f "${config_file}" ] && [ -r "${config_file}" ] || return 2
556:     # Only a digest leaves this scope; never print credential/config bytes.
557:     config_id=$( set -o pipefail; { printf '%s\0' "${REMOTE}" "${SAVES}" "${BACKUPS}" "${CONTENT}";
558:         sha256sum "${config_file}" || exit 1
559:         if [ -f "${SYNC_CONF}" ]; then sha256sum "${SYNC_CONF}" || exit 1; fi
560:     } | sha256sum) || return 2
561:     config_id="${config_id%% *}"
562:     jq -n --arg id "${config_id}" --arg remote "${REMOTE}" \
563:         --arg saves "${SAVES}" --arg settings "${BACKUPS}" --arg content "${CONTENT}" \
564:         '{schema_version:1,config_id:$id,remote:$remote,paths:{saves:$saves,settings:$settings,content:$content,
565:           roms:(($content | rtrimstr("/")) + (if $content == "" then "" else "/" end) + "ROMs"),bios:(($content | rtrimstr("/")) + (if $content == "" then "" else "/" end) + "BIOS"),media:(($content | rtrimstr("/")) + (if $content == "" then "" else "/" end) + "ROMs")}}'
566: }
567: 
568: seed_categories() {
569:     local category
570:     [ -n "$1" ] || return 2
571:     case "$1" in ,*|*,|*,,*|*[!a-z,]*) return 2 ;; esac
572:     IFS=, read -r -a SEED_CATEGORIES <<< "$1"
573:     local seen=,
574:     for category in "${SEED_CATEGORIES[@]}"; do
575:         case "${category}" in saves|settings|roms|bios|media) ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
576:         case "${seen}" in *,"${category}",*) return 2 ;; esac
577:         seen+="${category},"
578:     done
579: }
580: seed_selected() { local category; for category in "${SEED_CATEGORIES[@]}"; do [ "${category}" != "$1" ] || return 0; done; return 1; }
581: 
582: case "$1" in
583:     --validation-context)
584:         [ "$#" -eq 1 ] || exit 2
585:         validation_context || { echo '{"schema_version":1,"error":"unreadable-config"}'; exit 2; }
586:         exit 0
587:     ;;
588:     --validate-folders)
589:         [ "$#" -eq 3 ] || exit 2
590:         tool="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/cloud_folder_validate"
591:         [ -x "${tool}" ] || tool=/usr/bin/cloud_folder_validate
592:         exec "${tool}" "$2" "$3"
593:     ;;
594:     --folder-state)
595:         REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
596:         [ -n "${REMOTE}" ] || { echo "STATE=no-remote"; exit 1; }
597:         folder_values || exit $?
598:         folder_marker_read || exit $?
599:         folder_exists "${REMOTE}${SAVES}"; rc=$?
600:         case "${rc}" in 0) state=ready; present=1 ;; 1) state=missing; present=0 ;; *) exit "${rc}" ;; esac
601:         printf 'STATE=%s\nSAVES=%s\nBACKUPS=%s\nCONTENT=%s\nSAVES_EXISTS=%s\n' \
602:             "${state}" "${SAVES}" "${BACKUPS}" "${CONTENT}" "${present}"
603:         exit 0
604:     ;;
605:     --info)
606:         # Machine-readable connection facts for the native UI.
607:         resolve_connection
608:         echo "IP=${IP_ADDR}"
609:         echo "SSH_CMD=${SSH_CMD}"
610:         echo "OVERRIDE=${OVERRIDE_ACTIVE}"
611:         # Whether a root password is set, never the password: this output is
612:         # parsed by EmulationStation through a pipeline, and a credential that
613:         # crosses a script boundary is one careless echo from a log (#116,
614:         # D-INFRA-008). The page that must show or pre-fill it reads
615:         # root.password in-process from its own settings.
616:         echo "PASSWORD_SET=$([ -n "$(get_setting root.password)" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
617:         echo "SSH_UP=$(systemctl is-active sshd 2>/dev/null)"
618:         echo "AUTH_PORT=$(auth_port_busy && echo busy || echo free)"
619:         # Both names for one value: EmulationStation reads SYNCPATH= until its
620:         # side of the vocabulary sweep (#73) lands; SAVES_REMOTE= is the name.
621:         # A folder in a form the scripts cannot read is named as none: the
622:         # sync refuses that config too, and the folder editor the interface
623:         # opens from this line is the way to set one it can (gpt G2-C-01).
624:         if ! saves_remote="$(conf_get SAVES_REMOTE)"; then
625:             log_message "SAVES_REMOTE in ${SYNC_CONF} is not in a form the sync reads (${saves_remote}); no folder named"
626:             saves_remote=""
627:         fi
628:         echo "SAVES_REMOTE=${saves_remote}"
629:         echo "SYNCPATH=${saves_remote}"
630:         if folder_values >/dev/null; then
631:             echo "SETTINGS_REMOTE=${BACKUPS}"
632:             echo "CONTENT_REMOTE=${CONTENT}"
633:         else
634:             echo "SETTINGS_REMOTE="
635:             echo "CONTENT_REMOTE="
636:         fi
637:         echo "REMOTES=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
638:         # Which provider this device is actually connected to. The name is the
639:         # player's own label for the remote; the type is rclone's word for the
640:         # service (dropbox, drive, webdav...), which EmulationStation turns
641:         # into the name the player picked it by. Until this, nothing on any
642:         # screen said who the cloud was -- the setup page offered to connect
643:         # one and never mentioned the one already there (fork #110).
644:         remote_name="$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
645:         remote_name="${remote_name%:}"
646:         echo "REMOTE_NAME=${remote_name}"
647:         echo "REMOTE_TYPE=$(rclone config show "${remote_name}" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*type[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' | head -1)"
648:         exit 0
649:     ;;
650:     --content-location)
651:         tool="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/cloud_folder_validate"
652:         [ -x "${tool}" ] || tool=/usr/bin/cloud_folder_validate
653:         result=$("${tool}" roms,bios "location-$$") || { echo "STATE=unreadable"; exit 1; }
654:         CP=$(printf '%s' "${result}" | jq -r '.paths.content')
655:         AT_PATH=$(printf '%s' "${result}" | jq '[.categories[] | select(.state == "present")] | length')
656:         printf 'CONTENT_REMOTE=%s\nAT_PATH=%s\nAT_ROOT=0\nROOT_DIRS=\nFOUND=\n' "${CP}" "${AT_PATH}"
657:         if [ "${AT_PATH}" -gt 0 ]; then echo "STATE=ok"; else echo "STATE=empty"; fi
658:         exit 0
659:     ;;
660: 
661:     --set-content-remote|--set-settings-remote)
662:         SETTING=CONTENT_REMOTE
663:         [ "$1" != --set-settings-remote ] || SETTING=SETTINGS_REMOTE
664:         # Change exactly one selected location. Leading slash semantics are
665:         # preserved for path-based providers; no discovery or relocation.
666:         # Spaces, apostrophes and dots within a name are literal text.
667:         NEWPATH="$2"
668:         [ -z "${NEWPATH}" ] && { echo "ERROR empty path"; exit 1; }
669:         # Reject controls before command substitution can strip a trailing
670:         # newline and turn an invalid name into a different valid one.
671:         case "${NEWPATH}" in
672:             *[\$\`\\\"]*|*[[:cntrl:]]*) echo "That folder name has characters your cloud sync settings can't hold."; exit 1 ;;
673:         esac
674:         [ "${NEWPATH}" = / ] || NEWPATH="${NEWPATH%/}"
675:         case "${NEWPATH}" in
676:             .|..|./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|*/./*|*/.|*//*) echo "That folder name can't be used."; exit 1 ;;
677:         esac
678:         if ! conf_set "${SETTING}" "${NEWPATH}"; then
679:             echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be saved."
680:             log_message "${SETTING} NOT changed to ${NEWPATH}: ${SYNC_CONF} could not be written"
681:             exit 1
682:         fi
683:         log_message "${SETTING} set to ${NEWPATH} by request"
684:         echo "OK ${NEWPATH}"
685:         exit 0
686:     ;;
687:     --use-content-root)
688:         # The safe resolution: point this device back at the root where its
689:         # content already is. Moves nothing, reversible, instant.
690:         if ! conf_set CONTENT_REMOTE ""; then
691:             echo "ERROR the cloud sync settings could not be saved"
692:             log_message "Content path NOT changed: ${SYNC_CONF} could not be written"
693:             exit 1
694:         fi
695:         log_message "Content path set to the remote root by request"
696:         echo "OK content stays at the remote root"
697:         exit 0
698:     ;;
699: 
700:     --accept-saves-root)
701:         # The owner says the card the saves folder is on now is the right
702:         # one (#83): remember it, so saves transfers stop refusing.
703:         tool="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/cloud_saves_root"
704:         [ -x "${tool}" ] || tool=/usr/bin/cloud_saves_root
705:         exec "${tool}" accept
706:     ;;
707:     --check-syncpath)
708:         # Validate a candidate cloud folder without changing anything, so the
709:         # UI can refuse a bad one where it is typed rather than letting it
710:         # fail later inside a sync.
711:         if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
712:             CAND="$2"
713:         elif ! CAND="$(conf_get SAVES_REMOTE)"; then
714:             echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be read."
715:             exit 1
716:         else
717:             # One trailing slash is a spelling, not an empty part
718:             # (the audit of the fixes, claude G3-D-07).
719:             CAND="${CAND%/}"
720:         fi
721:         REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
722:         if [ -z "${REMOTE}" ]; then
723:             echo "No cloud remote configured."
724:             exit 2
725:         fi
726:         if syncpath_problem "${CAND}" "${REMOTE}"; then
727:             echo "OK ${CAND}"
728:             exit 0
729:         fi
730:         exit 1
731:     ;;
732: 
733:     --set-saves-remote|--set-syncpath)
734:         # Select only the saves location. Settings and library choices belong
735:         # to separate controls, including on upgrades from public ROCKNIX.
736:         NEWPATH="$2"
737:         if [ -z "${NEWPATH}" ]; then
738:             echo "ERROR empty path"
739:             exit 1
740:         fi
741:         case "${NEWPATH}" in
742:             *[\$\`\\\"]*|*[[:cntrl:]]*) echo "That folder name can't be used."; exit 1 ;;
743:         esac
744:         NEWPATH="${NEWPATH%/}"
745:         if [ "${NEWPATH}" = "/" ]; then
746:             echo "ERROR root path not allowed"
747:             exit 1
748:         fi
749:         # Refuse a path this remote cannot use. The literal path checks also
750:         # hold with no remote; existing independent pointers are preserved.
751:         SP_REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
752:         if ! syncpath_problem "${NEWPATH}" "${SP_REMOTE}"; then
753:             exit 1
754:         fi
755:         if ! conf_set SAVES_REMOTE "${NEWPATH}"; then
756:             # Under the interface's "THE CLOUD FOLDER WAS NOT CHANGED": this line
757:             # says why, and nothing the title already said (G-C-03 claude).
758:             echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be saved."
759:             log_message "Sync path NOT changed to ${NEWPATH}: ${SYNC_CONF} could not be written"
760:             exit 1
761:         fi
762:         log_message "Sync path changed to ${NEWPATH}"
763:         echo "OK ${NEWPATH}"
764:         exit 0
765:     ;;
766:     --free-auth-port)
767:         # Clear a stale sign-in webserver left by an interrupted
768:         # `rclone config`, so the next auto-config attempt can bind.
769:         pkill -f "rclone config" 2>/dev/null
770:         pkill -f "rclone authorize" 2>/dev/null
771:         log_message "Cleared stale processes holding the OAuth port"
772:         echo "OK"
773:         exit 0
774:     ;;
775:     --connected)
776:         # The native UI gates its connect step on this, so the player
777:         # cannot advance without an SSH session actually being open.
778:         if ssh_session_established; then
779:             echo "CONNECTED"
780:             exit 0
781:         fi
782:         echo "NONE"
783:         exit 1
784:     ;;
785:     --seed-folders)
786:         [ "$#" -eq 2 ] && seed_categories "$2" || { echo "Choose which cloud folders to create."; exit 2; }
787:         REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
788:         [ -n "${REMOTE}" ] || { echo "ERROR no remote"; exit 2; }
789:         folder_values || exit $?
790:         seed_failed=0
791:         # Only the saves action reads/writes its historical layout guard.
792:         if seed_selected saves; then folder_marker_read || exit $?; fi
793:         declare -a seed_dirs=() check_dirs=()
794:         for category in "${SEED_CATEGORIES[@]}"; do
795:             case "${category}" in
796:                 saves) seed_dirs+=("${SAVES}" "${SAVES}/savefiles" "${SAVES}/savestates" "${SAVES}/screenshots"); check_dirs+=("${SAVES}") ;;
797:                 settings) seed_dirs+=("${BACKUPS}"); check_dirs+=("${BACKUPS}") ;;
798:                 roms|media) seed_dirs+=("${CONTENT%/}${CONTENT:+/}ROMs"); check_dirs+=("${CONTENT%/}${CONTENT:+/}ROMs") ;;
799:                 bios) seed_dirs+=("${CONTENT%/}${CONTENT:+/}BIOS"); check_dirs+=("${CONTENT%/}${CONTENT:+/}BIOS") ;;
800:             esac
801:         done
802:         for d in "${seed_dirs[@]}"; do
803:             if ! rclone mkdir --s3-directory-markers "${REMOTE}${d}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null; then
804:                 echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDERS COULDN'T BE CREATED"
805:                 exit 5
806:             fi
807:         done
808:         if seed_selected saves; then folder_marker_write || exit $?; fi
809: 
810:         seed_note() {
811:             local dir="$1" listing tmp rc; shift
812:             # Never clobber a note the owner may have written themselves, and
813:             # never write on a guess. The folder's own listing says whether a
814:             # README.txt is in it. Asking for the file by name could not: a
815:             # listing that failed for any reason read as "absent" and the
816:             # owner's note was replaced (audit #307 PL-047), and on a bucket
817:             # a key that is not there lists as nothing with exit 0, which read
818:             # as "present" -- so no README was ever written there (#308
819:             # claude F-RS-09). A listing that fails writes nothing.
820:             if ! listing=$(rclone lsf --files-only "${REMOTE}${dir}/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
821:                 log_message "Seeding: ${dir} could not be listed, so its README was not written"
822:                 return 1
823:             fi
824:             printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | grep -qFx -- 'README.txt' && return 0
825:             tmp=$(mktemp) || return 1
826:             printf '%s\n' "$@" > "${tmp}"
827:             # --ignore-existing: another device may have written one since
828:             # the listing.
829:             rclone copyto --ignore-existing "${tmp}" "${REMOTE}${dir}/README.txt" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
830:             rm -f "${tmp}"
831:             return "${rc}"
832:         }
833: 
834:         if seed_selected saves; then
835:             seed_note "${SAVES}" "Game saves, save states, and screenshots." "" \
836:                 "Use savefiles/, savestates/, and screenshots/ for emulator progress." \
837:                 "Game saves in supported system folders keep their normal layout." || seed_failed=1
838:         fi
839:         if seed_selected settings; then
840:             seed_note "${BACKUPS}" "Settings backups, one folder per handheld." \
841:                 "Written by the device when you back up your settings." || seed_failed=1
842:         fi
843:         if seed_selected roms || seed_selected media; then
844:             seed_note "${CONTENT%/}${CONTENT:+/}ROMs" "Your games, one folder per system." "" \
845:                 "Use system folder names such as snes, psx, n64, or gba." \
846:                 "Game content stays in its system folder beside the games." || seed_failed=1
847:         fi
848:         if seed_selected bios; then
849:             seed_note "${CONTENT%/}${CONTENT:+/}BIOS" "BIOS and firmware files." \
850:                 "Keep the subfolders required by the emulator you use." || seed_failed=1
851:         fi
852: 
853:         # Report what is actually there, not what we asked for: on a bucket
854:         # remote a mkdir can succeed and leave nothing behind.
855:         for d in "${check_dirs[@]}"; do
856:             # A listing, never lsjson --stat: on a bucket remote stat reports
857:             # success for any path at all, so the MISSING branch could never
858:             # be reached -- the report would have been unconditionally OK,
859:             # which is the shape of an assertion that cannot fail.
860:             folder_exists "${REMOTE}${d}"; read_rc=$?
861:             case "${read_rc}" in
862:                 0) echo "OK ${d}" ;;
863:                 1) echo "MISSING ${d}"; seed_failed=1 ;;
864:                 *) seed_failed=1 ;;
865:             esac
866:         done
867:         [ "${seed_failed}" -eq 0 ] || { echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDERS COULDN'T BE CREATED"; exit 5; }
868:         exit 0
869:     ;;
870: 
871:     --check)
872:         # Verify a remote ($2 if given, else the first configured one);
873:         # plain-text verdict on stdout, exit 0 = working, 1 = missing,
874:         # 2 = configured but unreachable.
875:         REMOTE="$2"

1: #!/usr/bin/python3
2: # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
3: # Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
4: """Bounded folder readiness metadata, never a transfer or integrity check.
5: 
6: Private stdout contract for cloud_setup/ES. Missing means the selected endpoint
7: returned not-found, or the selected content root listed without the child.
8: Empty means a successful bounded listing found no recognized content; it is not
9: an account-wide absence claim. No ancestor outside the selected root is read.
10: """
11: import json
12: import os
13: from pathlib import Path
14: import re
15: import selectors
16: import signal
17: import subprocess
18: import sys
19: import time
20: 
21: CATEGORIES = ('saves', 'settings', 'roms', 'bios', 'media')
22: MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024
23: MAX_ENTRIES = 4096
24: TOTAL_SECONDS = 25
25: # Only observed standard save subtrees get deeper reads; never widen the
26: # whole selected root or infer progress from an uninspected directory.
27: SAVE_SUBTREES = {'psp/PSP/SAVEDATA': 2, 'psx/duckstation/memcards': 1}
28: MEDIA = {'images', 'videos', 'manuals', 'screenshots', 'fanart', 'boxart', 'wheel', 'mix', 'maps', 'media'}
29: # Match the shipped progress allowlist and content transfer exclusions. These
30: # are case-sensitive like rclone's filters; test controls compare actual bytes.
31: PROGRESS = re.compile(r'\.(srm|sav|fs|state[^/]*|auto|dsv[^/]*|eep|mpk|sra|fla)$')
32: N64_STATE = re.compile(r'\.(st[0-9]|pj[0-9](\.zip)?)$')
33: CONTENT_SAVE = re.compile(r'\.(srm|sav|fs|state[^/]*|auto|dsv[^/]*|eep|mpk|sra|fla|mcd|mcr)$')
34: DATABASE = re.compile(r'\.(db|db-wal|db-shm|db-journal|sqlite|sqlite3)$')
35: PARTIAL = re.compile(r'\.[^/]{8}\.partial$')
36: HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
37: 
38: 
39: class Unreadable(Exception):
40:     pass
41: 
42: 
43: def command(args, deadline, seconds=6, limit=MAX_BYTES):
44:     """Drain only bounded stdout; diagnostics can contain provider credentials."""
45:     remaining = min(seconds, deadline - time.monotonic())
46:     if remaining <= 0:
47:         raise Unreadable('time-limit')
48:     end = time.monotonic() + remaining
49:     proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
50:                             start_new_session=True)
51:     output = bytearray()
52:     try:
53:         with selectors.DefaultSelector() as ready:
54:             ready.register(proc.stdout, selectors.EVENT_READ)
55:             while ready.get_map():
56:                 wait = end - time.monotonic()
57:                 if wait <= 0:
58:                     raise Unreadable('time-limit')
59:                 if not ready.select(wait):
60:                     raise Unreadable('time-limit')
61:                 chunk = os.read(proc.stdout.fileno(), 65536)
62:                 if not chunk:
63:                     ready.unregister(proc.stdout)
64:                     break
65:                 output.extend(chunk)
66:                 if len(output) > limit:
67:                     raise Unreadable('listing-limit')
68:         rc = proc.wait(timeout=max(0.01, end - time.monotonic()))
69:         return rc, bytes(output)
70:     except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, Unreadable):
71:         raise Unreadable('time-or-listing-limit')
72:     finally:
73:         if proc.poll() is None:
74:             os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
75:         proc.wait()
76:         proc.stdout.close()
77: 
78: 
79: def context(deadline):
80:     rc, raw = command([str(HERE / 'cloud_setup'), '--validation-context'], deadline)
81:     if rc:
82:         raise Unreadable('unreadable-config')
83:     value = json.loads(raw)
84:     if not re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{64}', value.get('config_id', '')):
85:         raise Unreadable('unreadable-config')
86:     return value
87: 
88: 
89: def listing(remote, path, depth, deadline):
90:     rc, raw = command(['rclone', 'lsjson', remote + path, '--recursive',
91:                        '--max-depth', str(depth), '--no-mimetype', '--no-modtime',
92:                        '--retries', '1', '--low-level-retries', '1',
93:                        '--contimeout', '3s', '--timeout', '5s', '--max-duration', '6s'], deadline)
94:     if rc:
95:         # Entries on ANY error are not a valid observation. rclone lsjson
96:         # emits its opening bracket before a directory-not-found response.
97:         if rc in (3, 4) and (raw.strip() in (b'', b'[') or json.loads(raw) == []):
98:             return None
99:         raise Unreadable('listing-failed')
100:     entries = json.loads(raw)
101:     if not isinstance(entries, list) or len(entries) > MAX_ENTRIES:
102:         raise Unreadable('listing-limit')
103:     seen = set()
104:     for entry in entries:
105:         if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not isinstance(entry.get('Path'), str) or type(entry.get('IsDir')) is not bool:
106:             raise Unreadable('invalid-listing')
107:         p = entry['Path']
108:         if not p or len(p.split('/')) > depth or p.startswith('/') or any(x in ('', '.', '..') for x in p.split('/')) or any(ord(c) < 32 for c in p):
109:             raise Unreadable('invalid-listing')
110:         if p in seen:
111:             raise Unreadable('invalid-listing')
112:         seen.add(p)
113:     return entries
114: 
115: 
116: def save_entries(remote, path, entries, deadline):
117:     """Inspect named save writers beyond the root's ordinary depth-three cut."""
118:     combined = list(entries)
119:     unchecked = {e['Path'] for e in entries if e['IsDir'] and len(e['Path'].split('/')) == 3}
120:     for subtree, depth in SAVE_SUBTREES.items():
121:         if subtree not in unchecked:
122:             continue
123:         child = path + ('' if not path or path.endswith('/') else '/') + subtree
124:         extra = listing(remote, child, depth, deadline)
125:         if extra is None:
126:             raise Unreadable('folder-changed-during-check')
127:         unchecked.remove(subtree)
128:         for entry in extra:
129:             full = subtree + '/' + entry['Path']
130:             combined.append(dict(entry, Path=full))
131:             if entry['IsDir'] and len(entry['Path'].split('/')) == depth:
132:                 unchecked.add(full)
133:         if len(combined) > MAX_ENTRIES:
134:             raise Unreadable('listing-limit')
135:     return combined, unchecked
136: 
137: 
138: def files(entries):
139:     return [e['Path'] for e in entries if not e['IsDir'] and e['Path'] not in ('README.txt', '.layout')]
140: 
141: 
142: def progress(path):
143:     """The ordinary progress allowlist, excluding its separate archive tier."""
144:     parts = path.split('/')
145:     if DATABASE.search(parts[-1]):
146:         return False
147:     return (parts[0] in ('savefiles', 'savestates', 'screenshots') or bool(PROGRESS.search(parts[-1]))
148:             or (parts[0] == 'n64' and len(parts) == 2 and bool(N64_STATE.search(parts[-1])))
149:             or (path.startswith('psx/memcards/') and len(parts) == 3 and parts[-1].endswith(('.mcd', '.mcr')))
150:             or (path.startswith('psx/duckstation/memcards/') and len(parts) == 4 and parts[-1].endswith(('.mcd', '.mcr')))
151:             or path.startswith(('dc/shared/savefiles/', 'psp/PPSSPP/', 'psp/PSP/SAVEDATA/')))
152: 
153: 
154: def content_excluded(path, system=None):
155:     """SAVE_EXCLUDES/CONFLICT_EXCLUDES, relative to one ROM system or BIOS."""
156:     parts = path.split('/')
157:     return ((system == 'n64' and len(parts) == 1 and bool(N64_STATE.search(parts[-1])))
158:             or bool(CONTENT_SAVE.search(parts[-1])) or 'conflicted copy' in path
159:             or '.sync-conflict-' in path or bool(PARTIAL.search(parts[-1]))
160:             or any(p in ('save', 'memcards', 'PPSSPP') for p in parts[:-1])
161:             or any(parts[i:i+2] in (['shared', 'savefiles'], ['PSP', 'SAVEDATA']) for i in range(len(parts)-2))
162:             or path == 'README.txt')
163: 
164: 
165: def unchecked_directory(category, path, known):
166:     if category in ('roms', 'media'):
167:         parts = path.split('/')
168:         return parts[0] in known and not content_excluded('/'.join(parts[1:]) + '/probe', parts[0])
169:     if category == 'bios':
170:         return not content_excluded(path + '/probe')
171:     return True
172: 
173: 
174: def classify(category, entries, known):
175:     payload = files(entries)
176:     if not payload:
177:         return 'empty', 'no-recognized-content-in-checked-depth'
178:     if category == 'settings':
179:         good = [p for p in payload if p.lower().endswith(('.zip', '.tar.gz')) and len(p.split('/')) <= 2]
180:         return ('present', 'archive-names-found-not-verified') if good else ('empty', 'no-recognized-settings-archives-in-checked-depth')
181:     if category == 'bios':
182:         return ('present', 'files-found-not-compatibility-checked') if any(not content_excluded(p) for p in payload) else ('empty', 'no-recognized-content-in-checked-depth')
183:     if category == 'saves':
184:         # The progress allowlist permits recognized saves at any depth. A
185:         # repeated folder name alone is not evidence of a wrong location.
186:         return ('present', 'progress-paths-found-not-verified') if any(progress(p) for p in payload) else ('empty', 'no-recognized-progress-in-checked-depth')
187:     # ROM transfer expects one supported system folder beneath ROMs. A
188:     # direct payload is a location finding even when other ROMs are valid;
189:     # do not guess its system, move it, or describe that folder as empty.
190:     if category == 'roms' and any('/' not in p and p != 'gamelist.xml' and not content_excluded(p) for p in payload):
191:         return 'misplaced', 'files-outside-system-folders'
192:     good = []
193:     for path in payload:
194:         parts = path.split('/')
195:         if len(parts) < 2 or parts[0] not in known or content_excluded('/'.join(parts[1:]), parts[0]):
196:             continue
197:         media = parts[1] in MEDIA or parts[-1] == 'gamelist.xml'
198:         if (category == 'media') == media:
199:             good.append(path)
200:     if good:
201:         return 'present', 'supported-system-paths-found-not-verified'
202:     return 'empty', 'no-recognized-content-in-checked-depth'
203: 
204: 
205: def main():
206:     if len(sys.argv) != 3:
207:         return 2
208:     selected = sys.argv[1].split(',')
209:     run_id = sys.argv[2]
210:     if not selected or len(selected) != len(set(selected)) or any(c not in CATEGORIES for c in selected) or not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}', run_id):

212:     deadline = time.monotonic() + TOTAL_SECONDS
213:     result = {'schema_version': 1, 'run_id': run_id, 'config_id': '', 'categories': [], 'complete': False,
214:               'scope': {'max_depth': 3, 'save_subtree_depths': SAVE_SUBTREES, 'max_entries_per_listing': MAX_ENTRIES, 'max_bytes_per_listing': MAX_BYTES, 'max_seconds': TOTAL_SECONDS}}
215:     try:
216:         current = context(deadline)
217:         result.update(config_id=current['config_id'], paths=current['paths'])
218:         known = set()
219:         if 'roms' in selected or 'media' in selected:
220:             rc, raw = command([str(HERE / 'cloud_content_restore'), '--known-directories'], deadline)
221:             if rc:
222:                 raise Unreadable('system-list-unavailable')
223:             known = set(raw.decode().splitlines())
224:         cache = {}
225:         for category in selected:
226:             path = current['paths'][category]
227:             row = {'category': category, 'state': 'unreadable', 'path': path, 'detail': 'check-not-completed'}
228:             try:
229:                 # The content root is selected, so its direct children are in
230:                 # scope. No account/ancestor fallback if that root is absent.
231:                 if category in ('roms', 'bios', 'media'):
232:                     root = current['paths']['content']

234:                         cache[root, 1] = listing(current['remote'], root, 1, deadline)
235:                     parent = cache[root, 1]
236:                     child = 'BIOS' if category == 'bios' else 'ROMs'
237:                     if parent is None or not any(e['IsDir'] and e['Path'] == child for e in parent):
238:                         misplaced = parent and any(e['IsDir'] and (e['Path'].lower() == child.lower() or (category == 'roms' and e['Path'] in known)) for e in parent)
239:                         row.update(state='misplaced' if misplaced else 'missing', detail='recognized-folders-outside-expected-path' if misplaced else 'expected-folder-not-found')
240:                         result['categories'].append(row)
241:                         continue
242:                 if (path, 3) not in cache:
243:                     cache[path, 3] = listing(current['remote'], path, 3, deadline)
244:                 entries = cache[path, 3]
245:                 if entries is None:
246:                     row.update(state='missing', detail='selected-folder-not-found')

248:                     if not entries and category in ('saves', 'settings'):

250:                         # Without entries or an in-scope parent witness an

252:                         rc, raw = command(['rclone', 'backend', 'features', current['remote'] + path], deadline)

272:         result['error'] = str(error) if isinstance(error, Unreadable) else 'unreadable-config'

1: #!/bin/bash
2: # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
3: # Copyright (C) 2026-present rasteratops (https://github.com/rasteratops)
4: 
5: # cloud_scan - what the cloud holds for this device, before anything is offered.
6: #
7: # The transfer pages scan first and offer only what the scan found
8: # (D-CLOUD-156, fork #350): the folder's state, the settings archives by
9: # device label, where the content is, and -- once the player has ticked
10: # what to move -- the content listing in those classes. This runs those
11: # reads and talks to the scan page in the protocol every cloud page reads
12: # (">>> unit", ">>> doing", ">>> why"), writing each result to a file the
13: # options page builds from.
14: #
15: #   cloud_scan                   the opening scan: the folder, the settings
16: #                                archives, where the content is (three items)
17: #   cloud_scan --content [--with-media|--media-only]
18: #                                the content listing for the systems page,
19: #                                in the classes ticked (one item)
20: #   cloud_scan --folder          configured folder availability (one item)
21: #
22: # Read-only: scans never adopt another device's folders, rewrite settings,
23: # move files, or offer migration. Folder changes use explicit setup choices.
24: #
25: # Results, under /storage/.cache/cloud_sync/scan/:
26: #   state             cloud_setup --folder-state, one fact per line
27: #   archives          every settings archive in the Backups folder, one per line
28: #   settings          LABEL= (this device's), MINE= (its newest), NEWEST= (overall), COUNT=
29: #   content-location  cloud_setup --content-location, key=value
30: #   done              JSON binding the opening result to its run/configuration
31: #   scan              cloud_content_restore --scan's rows        (--content)
32: #   systems           the systems this device syncs (--systems)  (--content)
33: #   content-done      equivalent binding for the selected content mode
34: #
35: # Exit: 0 all read; 69 no network (the page says SKIPPED - YOU'RE NOT
36: # ONLINE); 1 no cloud storage set up; otherwise the failing read's code,
37: # with a ">>> why" in the player's words before it (D-UI-028).
38: 
39: . /etc/profile 2>/dev/null
40: 
41: OUT=/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/scan
42: SYNC_CONF=/storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf
43: readonly EXIT_NO_NETWORK=69
44: # Every listing here is bounded as the other readers' are (#308 claude F-RS-13).
45: readonly -a RCLONE_LIST_OPTS=(--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 3 --retries 1)
46: 
47: say() { echo "$@"; }
48: log() { logger -t cloud_scan "$*" 2>/dev/null; }
49: why() { echo ">>> why $*"; }
50: 
51: # The shared reader (cloud_setup's, the content scripts', D-CLOUD-149): a
52: # value in a form the sync does not read is nothing here, never a folder.
53: conf_get() { # <KEY> (the content scripts' reader, mirrored so every reader agrees, D-CLOUD-149): its value, quotes off; nothing when absent; exit 2 when unreadable, and why on stdout
54:     [ -f ${SYNC_CONF} ] || return 0
55:     awk -v k="$1" '
56:         { t = $0; gsub(/\t/, "", t); if (t ~ /[[:cntrl:]]/ && !cntrl) cntrl = NR }
57:         index($0, k "=") != 1 && !other \
58:             && $0 ~ ("^[ \t]*((export|declare|typeset|readonly|local)([ \t]+-[A-Za-z]+)*[ \t]+)?" k "[ \t]*[+]?=") { other = NR }
59:         index($0, k "=") == 1 {
60:             s = substr($0, length(k) + 2); v = ""; r = ""; ok = 1; why = ""
61:             c = substr(s, 1, 1)
62:             if (c == "\"") {
63:                 # Inside double quotes bash reads \" \\ \$ and \` as the one
64:                 # character each (PL-015), and so does this; an unescaped $
65:                 # or backtick is an expansion this reader does not make, and
66:                 # any other backslash is refused as conf_valid refuses it.
67:                 n = length(s); i = 2; closed = 0
68:                 while (i <= n) {
69:                     d = substr(s, i, 1)
70:                     if (d == "\"") { closed = 1; break }
71:                     if (d == "\\") {
72:                         e = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
73:                         if (e == "\"" || e == "\\" || e == "$" || e == "`") { v = v e; i += 2; continue }
74:                         ok = 0
75:                         why = (e == "") ? "a value continued onto the next line, which this reader does not follow" \
76:                                         : "a backslash inside double quotes that is not one of the escapes bash reads there"
77:                         break
78:                     }
79:                     if (d == "$" || d == "`") { ok = 0; why = "a $ or a backtick inside double quotes"; break }
80:                     v = v d; i++
81:                 }
82:                 if (ok && !closed) { ok = 0; why = "a double-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
83:                 if (ok) r = substr(s, i + 1)
84:             } else if (c == "'"'"'") {
85:                 j = index(substr(s, 2), c)
86:                 if (j) { v = substr(s, 2, j - 1); r = substr(s, j + 2) } else { ok = 0; why = "a single-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
87:             } else {
88:                 match(s, /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-]*/); v = substr(s, 1, RLENGTH); r = substr(s, RLENGTH + 1)
89:             }
90:             if (ok && r !~ /^([ \t]+(#.*)?)?$/) { ok = 0; why = "something after the value that is not a # comment" }
91:             if (!found) { found = 1; first = v; firstok = ok; firstwhy = "line " NR ": " why }

1: #!/usr/bin/python3
2: # SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
3: # Copyright (C) 2026-present ROCKNIX (https://github.com/ROCKNIX)
4: """Keep the shipped screenshot default in the saves tree; never move captures."""
5: import os
6: from pathlib import Path
7: import re
8: import stat
9: import sys
10: import tempfile
11: 
12: TARGET = Path('/storage/roms/screenshots')
13: MAX_CONFIG_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
14: 
15: 
16: def read_config(path):
17:     info = path.lstat()
18:     if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
19:         raise ValueError('nonregular configuration')
20:     with path.open('rb') as stream:
21:         raw = stream.read(MAX_CONFIG_BYTES + 1)
22:     if len(raw) > MAX_CONFIG_BYTES or b'\0' in raw:
23:         raise ValueError('unreadable configuration')
24:     return info, raw
25: 
26: 
27: def updated_config(raw):
28:     text = raw.decode('utf-8')
29:     lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
30:     section = ''
31:     folders = []
32:     keys = []
33:     for index, line in enumerate(lines):
34:         content = line.strip().lstrip('\ufeff')
35:         if not content or content.startswith(('#', ';')):
36:             continue
37:         if content.startswith('['):
38:             match = re.fullmatch(r'\[([^\]\r\n]+)\]', content)
39:             if not match:
40:                 raise ValueError('ambiguous section')
41:             section = match[1].strip().casefold()
42:             if section == 'folders':
43:                 folders.append(index)
44:         elif section == 'folders' and '=' in content:
45:             name, value = content.split('=', 1)
46:             if name.strip().casefold() == 'screenshots':
47:                 keys.append((index, value.strip()))
48:     if len(folders) > 1 or len(keys) > 1:
49:         raise ValueError('ambiguous screenshot configuration')
50:     value = keys[0][1] if keys else ''
51:     if value == str(TARGET):
52:         return raw
53:     # Only absent, empty, or the exact shipped default is ours to change.
54:     # Quoted, alternate, absolute and other custom values remain untouched.
55:     if value not in ('', 'screenshots'):
56:         return None
57:     newline = '\r\n' if '\r\n' in text else '\n'
58:     setting = 'Screenshots = ' + str(TARGET) + newline
59:     if keys:
60:         lines[keys[0][0]] = setting
61:     elif folders:
62:         index = folders[0]
63:         if not lines[index].endswith(('\n', '\r')):
64:             lines[index] += newline
65:         lines.insert(index + 1, setting)
66:     else:
67:         if lines and not lines[-1].endswith(('\n', '\r')):
68:             lines[-1] += newline
69:         lines.extend([newline, '[Folders]' + newline, setting])
70:     return ''.join(lines).encode('utf-8')
71: 
72: 
73: def prepare(path):
74:     original, raw = read_config(path)
75:     replacement = updated_config(raw)
76:     if replacement is None:
77:         return
78:     # An owner may have redirected the old default with a directory symlink.
79:     # Keep that choice as well as explicit custom configuration values.
80:     if replacement != raw and (path.parent / 'screenshots').is_symlink():
81:         return
82:     created = False
83:     staged = None
84:     try:
85:         if TARGET.is_symlink():
86:             raise ValueError('screenshot target is a symlink')
87:         if not TARGET.exists():
88:             TARGET.mkdir()
89:             created = True
90:         if not TARGET.is_dir():
91:             raise ValueError('screenshot target is not a directory')
92:         # Verify actual writes before changing the setting, including read-only
93:         # mounts and full storage. The temporary byte is always removed.
94:         with tempfile.TemporaryFile(dir=TARGET) as probe:
95:             probe.write(b'\0')
96:             probe.flush()
97:             os.fsync(probe.fileno())
98:         if replacement == raw:
99:             return
100:         descriptor, staged = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.screenshots-', dir=path.parent)
101:         with os.fdopen(descriptor, 'wb') as output:
102:             os.fchmod(output.fileno(), stat.S_IMODE(original.st_mode))
103:             os.fchown(output.fileno(), original.st_uid, original.st_gid)
104:             output.write(replacement)
105:             output.flush()
106:             os.fsync(output.fileno())
107:         current, observed = read_config(path)
108:         identity = lambda info: (info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_size, info.st_mtime_ns, info.st_ctime_ns)
109:         if identity(current) != identity(original) or observed != raw:
110:             raise ValueError('configuration changed during preparation')
111:         os.replace(staged, path)
112:         staged = None
113:     except Exception:
114:         if created:
115:             try:
116:                 TARGET.rmdir()
117:             except OSError:
118:                 pass
119:         raise
120:     finally:
121:         if staged is not None:
122:             os.unlink(staged)
123: 
124: 
125: def main():
126:     if len(sys.argv) != 2:
127:         return 2
128:     try:
129:         prepare(Path(sys.argv[1]))
130:     except (OSError, UnicodeError, ValueError):
131:         print("Couldn't prepare the screenshot folder. Screenshot preparation moved no existing captures.", file=sys.stderr)
132:         return 1
133:     return 0
134: 
135: 
136: if __name__ == '__main__':
137:     sys.exit(main())

## Artifact docs/cloud-save-integrity.md

1: # Scoped save integrity verification
2: 
3: Refs #517; D-CLOUD-181. This is a host QA/operations procedure, not a new
4: player flow or a replacement for CHECK CLOUD FOLDERS. M7 order remains
5: #515 -> #508 -> #507 -> assembled firmware/adoption/release qualification.
6: 
7: ## What each check means
8: 
9: | Check | Evidence | Limit |
10: | --- | --- | --- |
11: | Folder readiness | Selected category listing/classification | Does not prove payload integrity |
12: | Byte integrity | Successful bounded reads, provider hashes and stable before/after identity | Does not establish historical progress or catch an already-damaged file with a matching hash |
13: | Container structure | PNG chunk CRC/zlib/scanline checks; RZIP v1 lengths/zlib; RASTATE v1 block boundaries | No image rendering, core deserialization or game-specific SRAM validation |
14: | Local/cloud equality | Exact relative-path comparison and hashes, with read errors/races reported separately | A difference does not establish a winner; timestamps alone do not choose progress |
15: | Playability | Separately scoped game/core loading evidence | Never implied by an offline structural pass |
16: 
17: Raw saves, sidecar metadata and unknown formats receive byte checks and an
18: explicit unsupported-structure result. Do not call repeated-byte SRAM corrupt
19: without a game-specific basis. PNG interlaced scanline layout is not checked.
20: Limits/unsupported versions require review, not an assumption of corruption.
21: 
22: ## Collection contract
23: 
24: 1. Name the selected save root and authorized read transport. A personal
25:    operational read is separate from release QA, which uses synthetic data.
26:    Never export credentials or invoke a backup/restore/migration writer to
27:    inspect data. Exclude ROM libraries and settings archives unless separately
28:    scoped; small-file categories are not necessarily small.
29: 2. Obtain a complete successful metadata inventory and provider hashes.
30:    Record the collector's scope, flags, exit code and byte/file/time bounds.
31:    Reject duplicates, invalid paths, absent hashes and oversize inputs. A
32:    truncated/failed list is not an empty folder. No lossy text filter belongs
33:    on the authoritative JSON or binary stream. Restrict private files and
34:    produce a separate sanitized report; credentials are never collected.
35: 3. Read each enumerated object into private numeric payload filenames,
36:    recording each exit code and byte count. Bound per-file and total work.
37:    Re-list the same selected root and compare identity, size, mtime and hash.
38:    Changes fail the packet rather than silently mixing versions. This is
39:    before/after observation, not a transactional provider snapshot.
40: 4. Inspect exact local counterparts separately, preserving missing, unreadable,
41:    differing and changed-during-read outcomes. Check for extra local saves
42:    within the actual allowlist. Read current client pointers, automatic-sync
43:    settings and retained recovery state; remote rewind cannot reset these.
44: 5. Run the offline verifier. Keep the per-file report private. Hash/structural
45:    evidence cannot prove the historically desired game progress. Preserve
46:    originals/recovery files; a validation result never authorizes replacement.
47: 6. Record the outcome, controls and limits. Retire downloaded scratch after its
48:    named proof, retaining compact private manifests/reports. This scratch is
49:    not the independent recovery-copy project (#518).
50: 
51: Long reads use `tools/watch-job` with an actual PID, result and progress log.
52: The active agent consumes terminal results and reports completion. The monitor
53: writes local state; it does not itself deliver a chat notification.
54: 
55: ## Offline verifier
56: 
57: `tools/cloud-save-integrity` uses Python's standard library and performs no
58: network or device operations. Its packet contains `before.json`, `after.json`
59: (full successful rclone `lsjson --files-only --hash-type Dropbox` results),
60: `ordered.json` (before sorted by Path), `reads.json` (ordered index/rc/bytes),
61: and `payloads/0000`, `0001`, etc. The collector is responsible for complete
62: scope and truthful receipt codes; the verifier cannot reconstruct missing
63: remote metadata or certify the collection transport.
64: 
65: ```sh
66: tools/cloud-save-integrity /private/packet --report /private/new-report.json
67: tools/cloud-save-integrity-test --rclone /path/to/qualified/rclone
68: ```
69: 
70: The report refuses overwriting. Exit 0 means scoped byte checks passed with no
71: supported-container error; playability remains unverified. Exit 1 records
72: per-file failures; exit 2 refuses an invalid packet/report. Bounds: 4096 files,
73: 128 MiB total, 64 MiB/file and decompressed stream, 8 MiB/metadata input.
74: Collector limits may be smaller. Default output contains only aggregate
75: results. Reports contain hashes, so keep them private.
76: 
77: Dropbox hashing follows its [content-hash specification](https://docs.dropboxapi.com/dropbox-api/docs/technical-reference/content-hash),
78: with independent rclone controls at zero length and around 4 MiB boundaries.
79: RZIP v1 follows [libretro-common's reader](https://github.com/libretro/libretro-common/blob/master/streams/rzip_stream.c);
80: RASTATE follows [RetroArch's state writer](https://github.com/libretro/RetroArch/blob/bdba046fa6766380bc2457532f38e589df769aaf/tasks/task_save.c).
81: These validate envelopes, not the embedded core state.
82: 
83: ## Carry-forward to existing work
84: 
85: - **#515 targeted repairs:** synthetic complete-manifest cases (including benign
86:   credential-like filename substrings), stale/failed reads, conflicting versions,
87:   cancellation, retention and verification cost. Reuse these checks where the
88:   repair actually needs byte proof; derive layouts from emulator writers.
89: - **#508 adoption:** assert local pointers, automatic-sync settings and obsolete
90:   migration consumers separately from cloud contents. Replacing firmware alone
91:   must not be mistaken for resetting stored configuration. No private owner
92:   compatibility branch is added.
93: - **#507 audit:** review those implemented contracts in the frozen product delta;
94:   this operational review is not the independent milestone code audit.
95: - **#518 redundancy:** later independent recovery design and synthetic restore
96:   drill; a current provider hash or provider rewind is not another backup copy.
97: 
98: No ES screen or IA changes occur here. Existing qualified CF01-CF15 source
99: proof remains attributed to its original source; CF10 assembled firmware
100: adoption remains pending. No new screenshot claim is made for this host tool.
