3: This packet retains qualified M7.P5 source work, integrated through #508 in
4: `e6645cb5ea` and published with evidence at next `bc4ae05d30`. #515 and source
5: fixes #520/#521/#522/#523 are closed; #507's independent audit is next. It contains synthetic fixtures and public/package
6: source references, never a personal cloud inventory. It is not assembled-image
7: adoption, gameplay compatibility, or the independent audit.
8: 
9: ## Case disposition
10: 
11: [source-cases.md](source-cases.md) traces a finite set through public ROCKNIX
12: release20261001 and the exact packaged writers. Legitimate standalone paths
13: remain in place; path names alone cannot identify the historical unpublished
14: extra wrapper or the unique consumer of a flat save/state/image. The current
15: relocation disposition is instructions and explicit root selection, with no
16: repair action or repair-screen completion claimed. Concrete coverage defects
17: are fixed separately, not dismissed as ambiguous layouts.
18: 
19: ## #520 — source, host and affected VM proof accepted
20: 
21: Product commit `1ee8e5199da0bc02e6aa4ebff94b951f5e8b4804` covers PPSSPP savedata,
22: DuckStation cards and Mupen64Plus native/alternate slots across saves, content
23: transfer/list/count/match and bounded metadata checks. Old remote content copies
24: must not replace local progress. Both rule templates and custom-rule precedence
25: are exercised. No file relocation or remote historical-copy cleanup occurs.
26: 
27: - [Focused qualification](coverage/qualification.json):39PASS,0FAIL on final03.
28:   Fifteen accepted old-source failures demonstrate omitted saves, unsafe content
29:   transfer/media treatment and shallow classifier gaps. Failed fixture startup
30:   is retained separately and is not a product-defect reproduction.
31: - [Root source review](coverage/root-source-review.json): committed hashes,
32:   22-file install map, actual failing controls/startup witnesses and retirement.
33: - [Affected regressions](coverage/affected-regressions.json):21 content checks,
34:   30 validator checks and nine actual-image BusyBox find/awk controls. The last
35:   are isolated host fixtures using the image applets, not a guest/gameplay claim.
36: - [UI evidence index](ui/evidence-index.json): actual owned GENERIC_X64 source
37:   overlay: ten reviewed frames, one rejected fixture frame, no pending #520 case. EN640 and FR1280
38:   representative layouts; no full locale/panel Cartesian coverage claim.
39: 
40: Base validator depth remains3. Only observed `psp/PSP/SAVEDATA` and
41: `psx/duckstation/memcards` receive bounded supplementary metadata reads;
42: unknown deeper content is not marked inspected. The25-second budget,4096-entry
43: and2MiB per-listing limits remain. Files found means readiness within that
44: scope, not byte integrity or emulator compatibility.
45: 
46: ## #521/#522/#523 — source, package and native capture qualification
47: 
48: The exact DuckStation action/writer and shipped configurations put default
49: captures in application data outside the saves tree. #521 corrects new default
50: capture placement on clean and retained-default configs while preserving custom
51: paths and historical files. Old captures are not automatically moved or claimed
52: backed up; that requires separate deliberate placement. Both game and Tools
53: entrypoints must be exercised.
54: 
55: Actual guest preparation reproduced the exact pinned AppImage installed with
56: mode0644 and direct execution refusal126. #522 owns the recipe mode correction,
57: original/fixed install control and real target entrypoint proof before #521's
58: screenshot test. A guest-only chmod cannot close that package defect.
59: 
60: The complete121 bundled ELF/plugin closure then found one missing target
61: library, `libcom_err.so.2`; #523 adds the existing target package dependency.
62: Its normal build/install passed in an isolated owner with accepted build roots
63: read-only. The helper and package-mode source passes31host controls against four
64: original failures. [Native proof](duckstation-captures/vm-ui/README.md) verifies
65: the unchanged hotkey writes rendered PNGs to default and explicit custom paths,
66: and ordinary save backup/restore preserves the generated default PNG. Existing
67: captures/custom settings remain unchanged. This uses an original synthetic
68: reset ROM, not commercial game/BIOS or save-compatibility testing.
69: 
70: The guest/compiler were retired after final completeness review, with compact
71: receipts; the two owned scratch paths are absent. Product integration commit
72: `e6645cb5ea5ae3c7f699390a74b22d098fbeb7fb` carries the exact26 package changes
73: and the matched ES pin; ES4e410dc9 is published on its integration branch.
74: Distribution source and evidence are published on next `bc4ae05d30`. No firmware build, physical
75: action, private backend, independent audit or release publication has started.
76:

6831: static std::string cloudFolderCategoryLabel(const std::string& category)
6832: {
6833: 	if (category == "saves") return _("SAVES");
6834: 	if (category == "settings") return _("SETTINGS");
6835: 	if (category == "roms") return _("ROMS");

6839: static std::string cloudFolderStateLabel(const std::string& state)
6840: {
6841: 	if (state == "present") return _("FILES FOUND");
6842: 	if (state == "missing") return _("FOLDER MISSING");
6843: 	if (state == "empty") return _("NO FILES FOUND");
6844: 	if (state == "misplaced") return _("CHECK FILE LOCATIONS");
6845: 	return _("COULDN'T READ THIS FOLDER");
6846: }
6847: // Legacy line readers discard chunks longer than their line buffer. JSON is
6848: // a byte stream, and a populated five-category result can exceed that buffer.
6849: static std::pair<std::string, int> cloudReadFolderJson(const std::string& command)
6850: {
6851: 	FILE* pipe = popen(command.c_str(), "r");
6852: 	if (!pipe) return {"", -1};
6853: 	std::string json;
6854: 	char buffer[1024];
6855: 	bool bounded = true;
6856: 	std::size_t count;
6857: 	while ((count = fread(buffer, 1, sizeof(buffer), pipe)) != 0)
6858: 		if (bounded) bounded = CloudFolderValidation::appendOutput(json, buffer, count);
6859: 	const bool failed = ferror(pipe) != 0;
6860: 	const int status = pclose(pipe);
6861: 	if (!bounded || failed) json.clear();
6862: 	return {json, status != -1 && WIFEXITED(status) ? WEXITSTATUS(status) : -1};
6863: }
6864: static CloudFolderValidation::Context cloudFolderContext()
6865: {
6866: 	const auto output = cloudReadFolderJson("timeout 5 /usr/bin/cloud_setup --validation-context");
6867: 	return output.second == 0 ? CloudFolderValidation::parseContext(output.first) : CloudFolderValidation::Context();
6868: }

55: 	int itemsExpected, int itemsAfterContent)
56: {
57: 	std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(sMutex);
58: 	if (sCurrent != nullptr && !sCurrent->finished())
59: 		return sCurrent;
60: 
61: 	std::shared_ptr<CloudTransferJob> job(new CloudTransferJob(command, title, itemsExpected, itemsAfterContent));
62: 	sCurrent = job;
63: 	// Detached, and holding its own reference: the run ends when the command
64: 	// does, not when a page closes -- the scan job's shape.
65: 	std::thread([job] { job->run(); }).detach();

43: 					? _("DONE. YOUR SAVES WILL GO THERE THE NEXT TIME YOU BACK THEM UP.")
44: 					: _("COULDN'T CREATE IT. CHECK YOUR CONNECTION AND TRY AGAIN FROM MANAGE CLOUD STORAGE."),
45: 					_("OK")));
46: 			}));
47: 	};
48: 
49: 	if (!near.empty())
50: 	{
51: 		window->pushGui(new GuiMsgBox(window,
52: 			Utils::String::format(_("NOTHING TO RESTORE: YOUR CLOUD HAS %s, NOT %s.\n\nIS THE NAME RIGHT?").c_str(),
53: 				near.c_str(), folder.c_str()),
54: 			_("CHANGE FOLDER"), [window, folder] { GuiMenu::openCloudFolderEditor(window, folder); },
55: 			_("CREATE ANYWAY"), create,
56: 			_("NOT NOW"), nullptr));
57: 		return;
58: 	}
59: 	window->pushGui(new GuiMsgBox(window,
60: 		folder.empty()
61: 			? _("YOUR CLOUD HAS NO SAVES FOLDER YET.\n\nCREATE IT NOW?")
62: 			: Utils::String::format(_("YOUR CLOUD HAS NO %s FOLDER YET.\n\nCREATE IT NOW?").c_str(), folder.c_str()),
63: 		_("CREATE IT"), create,
64: 		_("NOT NOW"), nullptr));
65: }
66: 
67: void present(Window* window, const std::string& offer, const std::vector<std::string>& args)
68: {
69: 	if (window == nullptr || offer != "create-saves-folder")
70: 		return;
71: 
72: 	// The dialog is built on the interface thread wherever the answer came
73: 	// from: the card reads the script on a worker, the page reads it on a
74: 	// worker and asks from its own input handler, having just deleted
75: 	// itself. Posting covers both -- and on the page it also puts the
76: 	// dialog up on the frame after the one that took the press, rather than
77: 	// inside the input dispatch of a component that is gone. Through
78: 	// AppWindow: the card's worker is detached and asks after its linger,
79: 	// which can be after main() has let the window go (#308 8-es claude
80: 	// F-ES-26's rule).
81: 	AppWindow::post(window, [window, args]() { createSavesFolder(window, args); });
82: }
83: 
84: }

## Failure and cause

H700 arm04 on frozen f5f815faff stopped at228/244 on2026-10-07 04:41:23UTC. box86 linked successfully, then makeinstall_target tried build.ROCKNIX-H700.arm although config/path correctly creates build.pixelelated-H700.arm. Four exit channels are2, seven input seals match, and the actual owner/container exited. The failure is not disk exhaustion.

DISTRO intentionally remains ROCKNIX for the configuration namespace; DISTRONAME is pixelelated under D-WORKFLOW-144. The same reconstructed-path mismatch exists in box86, lib32, RetroArch's32-bit payload, gpSP, DeSmuME, Daedalus and build_distro cleanup/device-root paths. A previous ROCKNIX build had equal DISTRO/DISTRONAME and would not expose this mismatch; GENERIC_X64 qualification does not exercise the arm-to-aarch64 compatibility handoff.

Can this be done on the VM? Path/hook controls run on the host with isolated fixtures, including old/new identities and negative controls. Actual arm compilation and aarch64 payload inspection are build-host facts. No physical-device operation is required for this repair.

- [x] Preserve failed arm04 logs, stamps and every interrupted package scope before resuming from committed repaired inputs with a new watched owner.

- [ ] Reconcile H700/SM8550 input manifests, live M7 order, work/friction logs and retained evidence. Capacity, device smoke and release publication retain their existing separate gates.

Source repair is within the authorized pixelelated migration/device-build scope; package versions and user data formats stay pinned. Do not reuse or overwrite the failed owner.

## Frozen public issue 510 body

## Settled design and implementation ownership

The owner reaffirmed the post-rclone setup solution under D-CLOUD-179. This issue owns the contract and coordination; #515 now owns concrete repair cases and their qualification, #508 product integration, and #507 the frozen delta audit. An undefined relocation mapping is implementation work, not an unanswered owner design question.

## Ordered implementation path — M7.P5

1. **#510 — settled contract and reference alignment.** Link/retain the remote, then offer category checks, selected folder creation and instructions. Preserve independent paths. D-CLOUD-178/179 settle this; do not ask the owner to choose the overall design again.
2. **#515 — targeted save-folder repair cases and qualification (active, including children #520/#521).** Read public ROCKNIX filters/config and actual emulator writers; distinguish valid layouts from source-proven misplaced saves/states/screenshots. Define exact plans, bounds, collision/source-retention and consent; implement and prove supported actions. Unsupported/ambiguous cases retain instructions. If no safe automatic case exists, retain the case evidence and explicit disposition; never claim an unimplemented repair passed or silently drop a demonstrated requested case.
3. **#508 — coordinated final integration and pins.** Include the qualified foundation and #515's result, remove automatic move/follow and startup/tidy paths, and retain public config/credential preservation. Carry canonical references and proof with the source.
4. **#507 — freeze and independently audit the resulting P5 delta.** Required primary and cross-lab stages; no replay of the accepted candidate16 audit.
5. **#508/#492/#344/#265/#359 — assembled firmware and release gates.** Build the engineering image required for CF10 clean/public ROCKNIX adoption, map final inputs/inclusion, then finish source/licences and named physical/release gates. Source-overlay proof does not establish an installed RC.

**Parallel #511:** setup, ROM and BIOS guides and later verified QR destinations. Local instructions work without the website. The separate Herdr lane still awaits its startup trust answer; it is not a firmware gate.
## Current qualification

The check/create/instructions foundation has completed [source-overlay proof](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/d5e2f78618624cad919afaba6784bef3f7eaf8c7/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-cloud-validator/ui/README.md) at distribution `6f89bc7cecee5972909828103689e2c7c0711c30` and ES `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. Both product branches remain local/unintegrated; the product pin is unchanged. #512/#513/#514 are qualified source fixes and closed; their firmware inclusion belongs to #508.

Evidence: 21 restore controls, 30 validator controls, 1,311 top-level host PASS (zero FAIL/SKIP), ordinary VM WebDAV and SFTP 108 PASS each; 99 UI-index entries comprising 89 reviewed frames, nine rejected frames retained and CF10 assembled firmware/public adoption pending. #512 unit logic passed 183 cases/4,752 assertions; later text-only fixes have separate compile/link/syntax/catalog/vocabulary proof. The prior foundation runtimes are retired and 529 sealed files retained; a new owned #520/#521 source-overlay guest is active for changed proof. Accepted candidate16/device artifacts and the 78-frame firmware baseline are unchanged. No new firmware build or independent #507 audit has started.

## Product contract

The [canonical flow, diagrams and evidence table](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/next/docs/pixelelated/cloud-folder-flow-review.md) define:

- After connection, check selected categories, explicitly create selected folders/notes, change independent paths, or see instructions. Linking alone creates or relocates nothing. Category switches scope checks/creation; automatic sync has separate settings.
- Fresh defaults: `/pixelelated/Saves`, `/pixelelated/Backups`, `/pixelelated/Content`; ROMs under `<content>/ROMs/<system>`, BIOS under `<content>/BIOS`. Preserve existing configured paths until deliberately changed; a general arbitrary-layout browser is outside this first contract.
- Read-only bounded results distinguish present, missing, empty, recognized misplaced and unreadable within selected roots. They do not establish account-wide absence, complete transfer integrity or BIOS compatibility.
- A supported game-save/save-state/screenshot repair requires its own exact plan and confirmation. No blanket tidier, guessed destination or implicit ROM/BIOS/settings archive/game-content/unknown-file relocation.
- ROM/BIOS organization uses a computer/provider interface and useful local expected-path instructions. See instructions gains guide-specific QR only after #511 publishes verified destinations. Normal selective backup/restore and sync retain their separate purposes.
- Adoption starts from public ROCKNIX plus clean installs. The source-cited baseline is release20261001/tag `c445081a59518f37d9776e5412dd7b14910696f7`, with `/GAMES` and nested `/GAMES/backup`. Unpublished fork/PR states are historical, not public compatibility gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The canonical review records the public release/tag and actual config/filter/package references, separated from unpublished experiments; see Who is upgrading in the linked flow review.
- [x] D-CLOUD-178/179 and the implemented diagram define selected-category checks/creation, independent paths and manual content guidance; prospective repairs are separately identified with #515 ownership.
- [x] Required flow/screenshot maintenance is published in both agent entrypoints, the canonical UI rule and evidence-index schema (D-WORKFLOW-155/156; f6037a9133). The final source-overlay CF01–CF15 table links reviewed happy/branch frames and explicitly pending CF10.
- [ ] #515 records source-proven repair cases, exact preview/consent/count/bytes/collision/source-retention/stale-plan/interruption/verification contracts and qualified supported actions, or an evidence-backed unsupported disposition. No unsupported repair is counted as delivered.
- [ ] #508 final integration/adoption criteria are met on coordinated source and then actual assembled firmware; missing/unreadable and unrelated-file preservation remain proved. Foundation proof is complete above, final pin/image proof is not.
- [x] Live M7, #508/#507/#515 and the canonical checkpoint agree on this implementation order and remaining gates; published in next `b115af8d4cebbb8845edf32f519b3d00580c9ff1` with exact GitHub/readback receipts under docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-cloud-plan. Personal review remains separate #516.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: source-derived synthetic fixtures and GENERIC_X64 prove cloud setup, selected roots, applicable repairs, UI and clean/public adoption. No private Dropbox credential or physical-device action is needed. Current work is source-derived #515/#520/#521 qualification; reuse prior proof where inputs are unchanged.

## Latest maintainer requirement — 2026-10-08

> I think we arrived at a good solution for this. I want to make sure everything we had is well documented, put into issues, and that we have a clear implementation path around using our project management methodology.
>
> I feel like we arrived at a good solution that relied on post-rclone remote setup. At the time, verification, directory creation, and user actions could live, so someone could help tidy up certain elements while we provide documentation for how to handle more data-intensive operations.
>
> This would also mean refactoring and redoing what we had done around the initial upgrade path, but I'm fine manually aligning myself with our new framework and directory structure. I can also revert the changes we made in Dropbox and then simply retitle the directory on my end.

## Owner-managed alignment and separate private review

Moving around ROMs, as we found, can be a very data-intensive operation, and so we might want to delineate between organizing or moving ROMs versus all of the other files we deal with. We're not finding ourselves in a situation where we're trying to use a handheld with a limited CPU to move hundreds of GB of files.

For example, we need to think about if a user should be able to have their ROMs in a different directory or not. >
